docs.title: 14.3 Placement effect (§9.1 L3, P1)
docs.text:
bench/crules_place.py: tracemaker-place --mode full --seed 1 (8 threads per board), --component-rules off vs soft; distances by bench/place_intent.py, component-rule distances measured on the placed board with roles bound on the input (--roles-from). HPWL is the reported (unweighted) wirelength; pseudo-nets never count in it.

Medians over boards (n = boards with that kind of part); distances in mm. "decap" and "crystal" are place_intent's own measures (centre to the nearest IC pad); "XTAL-01", "XTAL-02", "ESD-01", "reg caps" (LDO-01 and BUCK-01) are the largest pad-centre distance per rule instance. The third configuration additionally doubles D25's decoupling ties (--decap-weight 20).

Set Config HPWL (median) HPWL vs off (geo-mean) decap crystal XTAL-01 XTAL-02 load caps ESD-01 reg caps 23 boards of doc 04 §7.3, seed 1 off 518.3 1.000 3.66 (17) 5.11 (6) 6.36 (5) 2.38 (4) – 4.25 (3) soft 518.3 0.996 3.92 3.98 5.06 2.02 – 4.31 soft + decap ×2 581.3 1.028 3.26 4.47 4.81 2.00 – 2.83 human placement – – 4.15 4.45 5.36 2.84 – 3.48 9 boards with ESD parts, seed 1 off 582.0 1.000 5.61 (9) 4.04 (6) 6.04 (6) 3.70 (5) 7.12 (9) 2.00 (3) soft 589.5 1.005 3.83 3.46 4.52 2.28 3.19 3.80 soft + decap ×2 597.3 1.019 2.78 3.38 4.26 1.86 3.20 2.01 human placement – – 2.94 3.98 4.68 1.85 7.12 2.12 6 boards where soft changes the result, seeds 1–3 (18 runs) off 615.7 1.000 3.20 (15) 5.41 (15) 6.36 (15) 3.10 (12) – 2.19 (3) soft 617.9 0.986 4.29 3.54 4.58 2.06 – 4.53 soft + decap ×2 628.7 1.004 2.92 4.08 5.03 2.06 – 2.53

On 17 of the 23 boards soft adds no pseudo-net (no crystal/ESD/regulator instance, or D25 already ties the parts) and the placement is byte-identical to off. Per board, soft vs off (change > 0.05 mm): on the 23 boards XTAL-01 is better on 4 and worse on 0, load caps better on 3, decaps worse on 3 and better on 0; on the ESD set ESD-01 is better on 8 of 9 boards (worse on 0), decaps better on 5 and worse on 4, regulator caps worse on 2; over the 18 multi-seed runs XTAL-01 is better on 14 of 15, load caps on 9 of 12, but decaps worse on 9 (better on 2) and regulator caps worse on 3 of 3. The crystal and protection pulls take the space next to the IC that D25's decaps had (bullion, PocketBone: decaps 3-4 mm become 6-8 mm). Doubling the decap ties fixes the decaps (better than off) at +2-3 % HPWL. Neither is free of regressions, so --component-rules stays off by default for placement (D31); soft is recommended where crystals and connector ESD matter more than a few tenths of a millimetre of decap distance. off reproduces the previous placer output byte for byte.

Weight scale (tracemaker-place --crules-weight PCT, 2026-10-04 night, seed 1, 23 boards). Medians, off → soft at 50 % / 75 % / 100 %: decaps 3.66 → 3.33 / 3.30 / 3.92 mm; crystal to IC 5.11 → 5.35 / 4.53 / 3.98 mm; regulator caps 4.25 → 3.79 / 2.45 / 4.31 mm; HPWL equal. At 75 % every median improves on off, but per board the decaps still get worse on RX5808 (3.7 → 5.8 mm) and PocketBone (4.3 → 8.5 mm) and better on bullion (4.0 → 2.4 mm); only 5 of 23 boards change at all. Seeds 2–4 overturn the seed-1 picture: at 75 % decap medians are worse than off on every seed (3.74 / 3.92 / 3.85 vs 3.26 / 3.74 / 3.39 mm), as at 100 %, and regulator caps too; only the crystal gain holds on all seeds (e.g. 5.07 → 2.83–3.59 mm on seed 3). A weight scale does not fix the decap conflict; the feature stays off and the scale at 100 %.

Two stages (D43, now what soft does in full mode). Stage 1 places with the decoupling ties only; stage 2 locks those capacitors and their ICs and refines with the other pulls. 23 boards × seeds 1–3, off → two-stage: decap median 3.66/3.26/3.74 → 3.66/3.42/3.74 mm, crystal 5.11/6.70/5.07 → 4.66/5.77/4.72, load caps 2.38/4.77/3.11 → 2.03/2.76/2.39, regulator caps unchanged, HPWL geometric mean 0.99. Per board, 18 metric changes better and 4 worse (PocketBone decaps on every seed; bullion's crystal on one). PocketBone's "decaps" there are mostly the regulator U4's input/output capacitors (C2–C13): the LDO rule re-places them around U4, which is not locked (no D25 tie anchors it), and bench/place_intent.py counts any supply-to-ground capacitor near an IC as a decap — the two metrics overlap. Integration test crules_two_stage.

Default gate on the placed tiers (D52, 2026-10-05). bench/run.py --place routable (the default placement mode: the router keeps the input or the most routable candidate), 8 router variants, 120 s, --place-crules off vs soft side by side, compared by bench/crules_tiers.py:

Tier Boards Clean pass off → soft Routed off → soft Full re-placement kept B 40 28 → 28 5,163 → 5,156 4 → 8 boards C 30 18 → 18 9,538 → 9,539 —

Distances on the kept boards (medians over boards with the part, mm; per board better / worse by > 0.25 mm): decap 3.17 → 3.17 (2 / 5), crystal 5.25 → 5.25 (3 / 1), XTAL-01 6.54 → 5.57 (5 / 1), load caps 3.11 → 2.81 (3 / 0), regulator caps 3.38 → 3.28 (1 / 0), ESD 4.67 → 7.90 (0 / 1, n = 3). The decap and ESD losses come from the router keeping a different candidate (e.g. the human board in one arm, a full re-placement in the other), not from the pulls moving parts apart; within one candidate type the distances are equal or shorter. Gate (§9.1): no routing regression — met; crystal and load-cap metrics improve — met; decap median unchanged — not improved. Soft is the placement default on that evidence; decap behaviour is the open item.

docs.title: 14.4 Routing (P2/P3)
docs.text:
--component-rules defaults to off for tracemaker route (D31): the router's default path is unchanged (pair_nets empty). Measured 2026-10-04:

  • Tier-A sample (bench/run.py --tier A --limit 40 --time 30 --jobs 2, KiCad DRC judge): off 36/40 clean, completion 0.997; with TM_ROUTE_ARGS="--component-rules on" 35/40, 0.995. on changes the router input on only 3 of the 40 boards (kitspace_aquarius, kitspace_threeboard: one crystal keep-out each; mechkeys_1800-controller: a keep-out and two USB pairs); the board that lost its clean pass (mosavr_pcie1x_backplane, 110 → 102 routed) gets no component rule at all, so that difference is wall-clock noise of the 30 s runs on a shared machine.
  • 16 boards with crystals/USB/ESD (same harness): off 8/16 clean, completion 0.951; on 6/16, 0.947.
  • Deterministic (--work 20000000 --threads 1, 10 boards where the rules change the router input): soft (USB pairs only) routes the same number of connections as off on all 10; the experimental coupled-pair router mostly falls back to single tracks on these short USB runs ("too short to couple", "leg start fails"). on (keep-outs) is worse on 4 boards (blackmagic-isolated 93 → 86, PiZeroHub 108 → 104, bobc_MS-F100 102 → 99, MicroMaple 95 → 94), better on 1 (HACK 82 → 88) and equal on 5: a hard keep-out under the crystal and its IC pins removes routing space on the far layer. Leaving the IC pins out of the area (tried) does not help consistently.
  • KiCad check of the sidecar: on PCBench CANadapter, KiCad 10 reads <output>.tracemaker.kicad_dru (copied as the project's .kicad_dru) and reports one "items not allowed (rule 'tmk XTAL-04 Y1')" — a +3V3 track on B.Cu under the crystal — for the board routed with off, and none for the board routed with on (ctest crules_route).

So keep-outs are a real constraint with a completion cost on dense boards; they stay opt-in.

docs.title: 14.5 Stackup and impedance (P4)
docs.text:
Stackup. (setup (stackup …)) is read into Board::stackup (§14.1). Of the 1,157 PCBench boards, none of the unrouted.kicad_pcb files has a stackup (they are KiCad 5 exports); 8 of the raw.kicad_pcb originals do (kitspace_BalthazarPSU3, Minisumo_V2.1, minisumo_v3, OSO-BOOK-C1, OtterPill, solenoid_driver, Unifying, USBI2C01), as do 15 KiCad demos (2 to 12 copper layers; tiny_tapeout uses dielectric sublayers) and 12 Freerouting issue fixtures. So on the benchmark impedance rules always report "not applied: no stackup in the board (doc 15 §3.6)" — nothing is guessed (CLAUDE.md rule 6).

Geometry per routing layer (stackup_geometry): an outer layer is microstrip over the adjacent copper layer (dielectric = everything between them); an inner layer is stripline between the copper layers above and below (off-centre allowed; εr of the two sides combined in series). The adjacent copper layer is assumed to be a plane; the report says "(GND)" when a zone of a ground net is on it and "(assumed)" otherwise. KiCad power layers are not routing layers. A stackup without εr or thickness for a gap makes that layer "not computed", never defaulted.

Models (impedance.cpp, each cited at its definition):

Structure Model Stated formula error Microstrip Hammerstad & Jensen 1980 with their thickness correction (KiCad additionally applies Bahl & Garg's thickness term, 0–3 % higher Z on thin dielectrics) ±4 % Stripline Cohn 1954 (w/(b−t) ≥ 0.35) / Wheeler 1978 (narrow), off-centre by Wadell's image split (two centred lines in parallel) ±2 % centred, ±5 % off-centre Edge-coupled microstrip Kirschning & Jansen 1984 static even/odd modes, Jansen 1978 thickness, Bahl & Garg 1977 ±5 % Edge-coupled stripline Cohn 1955 (exact zero-thickness conformal mapping, thick-strip eq. 18/20/22), image split off-centre ±4 % centred, ±8 % off-centre Grounded coplanar Ghione & Naldi 1983/84 conformal mapping, Gupta et al. 1996 thickness ±7 %

The stated error covers the papers' accuracy plus what is left out (solder mask lowers outer-layer Z by roughly 1–3 Ω; dispersion; the image split). Fab tolerance (±10 % typical) is reported separately. Differential impedance = 2 × odd-mode impedance; the propagation delay is √εeff / c (odd mode for pairs).

Solving (plan_impedance): width by bisection on integer nm (monotone functions; ties to the narrower width) in [max(board minimum width, 0.1 mm), 5 mm (pairs) / 10 mm]; pairs use the Default net class's diff-pair gap (never below its clearance or the board minimum clearance); if even the narrowest width is too low in impedance, the width stays at the minimum and the gap is solved instead; GCPW uses the clearance as the ground gap. Rules with structure: stripline are solved on inner layers only, gcpw on outer layers (pairs on those layers use coupled microstrip: no coplanar-pair model). A pair wider than 1 mm as plain microstrip gets the §5.3 note (prefer GCPW or short matched routing).

Unit tests (src/crules/test_impedance.cpp, [impedance]; reader in tests/test_kicad_io.cpp, [stackup]). References and the tolerance each test uses:

Case Reference TraceMaker Error Tolerance Microstrip, εr 2.2, h 1.27 mm, w 3.911 mm, t 0 Pozar Ex. 3.7: 50 Ω, εeff 1.87 50.04 Ω, 1.881 0.07 %, 0.6 % 0.5 %, 1 % Microstrip, εr 4.5, h 1.51 mm, w 2.9 mm, 35 µm KiCad: 49.03 Ω 48.94 Ω 0.2 % 3 % Microstrip, εr 4.3, h 0.2 mm, w 0.35 mm, 35 µm KiCad: 51.44 Ω 50.71 Ω 1.4 % 3 % Microstrip, εr 4.4, h 0.1 mm, w 0.18 mm, 35 µm KiCad: 49.29 Ω 47.92 Ω 2.8 % 3 % Microstrip 50 Ω on 1.6 mm FR-4 (εr 4.5, 35 µm) this document / KiCad: 2.9–3.0 mm 2.966 mm — in range Microstrip, h 0.2 mm, w 0.1–0.38 mm IPC-2141A rule of thumb ≤ 10 % 10 % Stripline, εr 2.2, b 3.2 mm, w 2.66 mm, t 0 Pozar Ex. 3.5: 50 Ω 49.90 Ω 0.2 % 0.5 % Stripline, b 20 mil, w 8 mil, t 0.7 mil, centred / off-centre (3 cases) KiCad: 49.71 / 43.50 / 29.69 Ω identical < 0.01 % 0.1 % Coupled microstrip, 4 geometries (h 0.1–1.51 mm) KiCad: 133.30 / 113.25 / 92.78 / 79.15 Ω diff identical < 0.01 % 0.1 % Coupled stripline, w = s = 0.1 mm, b 0.5 mm, t 0 exact (scipy ellipk): Z0e 91.209, Z0o 55.090 Ω identical < 1e-6 1e-6 Coupled stripline, b 20 mil, w = s = 8 mil, t 0.7 mil KiCad QA: Z0e 55.34, Z0o 43.59, Zdiff 87.18 Ω 54.91 / 44.12 / 88.24 Ω 0.8 / 1.2 / 1.2 % 2 % GCPW, w 0.5, gap 0.3, h 0.8 mm, εr 4.4, t 0 exact (scipy ellipk): 70.483 Ω, εeff 2.8166 identical < 1e-6 1e-6 GCPW, same, 35 µm KiCad: 70.86 Ω 69.44 Ω 2.0 % 3 % IPC-2221: 1 A, ΔT 10 °C, 35 µm, outer / inner formula by hand: 0.300 / 0.781 mm (≈ 12 / 31 mil per A) 0.300 / 0.781 mm < 0.1 % 0.5 %

"KiCad" = KiCad's common/transline_calculations (master, 2026-10-04) compiled outside the tree and run at 1 MHz. Where it differs from TraceMaker beyond rounding: its microstrip adds Bahl & Garg's thickness term; its coupled stripline thin-gap branch (Cohn eq. 22, s < 5t) omits √εr in the medium impedance (in air both agree; with εr 4.3 it jumps 7 % at s = 5t where ours joins eq. 20 within 1.4 %); its zero-thickness coupled stripline and GCPW differ from the exact conformal mapping by 2–6 %. Round trips (solve → evaluate) are exact to 1e-3 Ω; monotonicity of every function the solver bisects is tested by sweeps. The single stripline's two branches meet with a step of about 0.6 % at w/(b−t) = 0.35 (bisection then returns the boundary width).

Report (tracemaker rules): a header line with the stackup and the propagation delay per layer (50 Ω line) used for ps→mm skew conversion, or "no stackup in the board: … skew budgets use 6.0 ps/mm outer / 7.0 ps/mm inner"; per impedance rule the widths grouped by layers with the same result, the reference layers and the stated error; when a board net class already covers the pair, the rule stays "satisfied-by-board" and the report adds the class's impedance by the same model. Example (KiCad demo RoyalBlue54L-Feather, 8 layers, 0.1 mm prepreg εr 4.5):

  stackup: 8 copper layers, 1.58 mm, ENIG; prop delay (ps/mm, 50 Ω line): F.Cu 5.91 In1.Cu 7.08 … B.Cu 5.91
     USB2-01   impedance       soft      satisfied-by-board: net class USB_DIFF (diff pair 0.125 mm / gap 0.203 mm,
               114 Ω diff on F.Cu by this model); for comparison, report only, not applied to routing:
         90 Ω diff on F.Cu, B.Cu: 0.201 mm / gap 0.250 mm microstrip (h 0.100 mm, εr 4.50) = 90.0 Ω, 6.06 ps/mm, formula error ±5 %
           reference: F.Cu over In1.Cu (GND); B.Cu over In6.Cu (GND)

JSON: stackup (layers, per-layer geometry, delays) at the top level; impedance (bounds, one entry per layer and target with width, gap, Z, εeff, ps/mm, h, εr, error) and current on the rules.

Not built in P4: routing with the computed widths (net classes per layer; D36), the reference-plane coverage check and plane-gap cost, stitching vias at layer changes, solder-mask correction, broadside-coupled and coplanar pairs, the --assume-stackup preset (§3.6), commented suggestions in the sidecar .kicad_dru.

docs.title: 14.6 User overrides, Ethernet magnetics void, connector edge attraction
docs.text:
User override file (§3.5 level 1, §6.3; D40). src/crules/overrides.{hpp,cpp} parses and validates the file; detect(board, catalogue, &overrides) applies it, so tracemaker rules, tracemaker route and tracemaker-place behave the same:

tracemaker rules board.kicad_pcb --mode on --rules-override board.tracemaker_rules.json
tracemaker route board.kicad_pcb -o out.kicad_pcb --component-rules on --rules-override board.tracemaker_rules.json
tracemaker-place board.kicad_pcb -o placed.kicad_pcb --component-rules soft --rules-override board.tracemaker_rules.json
scripts/crules_override.py board.tracemaker_rules.yaml -o board.tracemaker_rules.json   # YAML -> JSON
  • deny moves the instance to "possible" ("denied by user (file)"), so a competing category in its exclusive group can win; assert gives confidence 100 (never capped), wins its group, binds with the category's binder or, if the binder rejects the part, the anchor alone (the objection stays in the evidence).
  • disable (rule, rule@REF, category, category@REF): the rule is neither applied nor measured; no pseudo-net, keep-out, sidecar rule or USB pair comes from it. Report: not-applied: overridden by user: disabled (disable XTAL-04@Y1); condensed categories count "disabled by user".
  • set: the rule is evaluated with the new parameter (limits, keep-out margins, impedance targets); report: …; overridden by user: max_mm = 5 (catalogue 10; set XTAL-01 max_mm = 5); JSON user_override per rule and user_overrides (file, entries, unused) at the top level.
  • Errors (exit 1, message names the file and entry, with a "did you mean" hint): unknown keys, rule ids, categories, parameters, value types, negative numbers, malformed ID@REF, references not on the board, a category both asserted and denied, two asserted categories that exclude each other, a .yaml file (with the conversion command). An entry whose reference is on the board but not an instance of the category (or a global entry with no instance) is a warning in the report and the route/place log: the catalogue default then applies.
  • Tests: [overrides] in src/crules/test_crules.cpp (every form, 20 error messages, disable/assert/deny/set semantics, precedence, determinism).

Ethernet magnetics void (ETH-05; D41). bind_ethernet binds the anchor as rj45 (connector) or phy (IC), magnetics = transformers (T/TR or a transformer lib_id/value, ≥ 6 pads) sharing ≥ 2 signal nets with the anchor, and integrated_magnetics for MagJack-style RJ45s (no void: "not required"). generate_keepouts adds a rule area around the magnetics' courtyards grown by 0.508 mm on their side and the adjacent copper layer, minus layers with their pads (SMD on F.Cu: B.Cu on 2 layers, In1.Cu on 4), keeping out tracks, vias and zones; the sidecar rule is (constraint disallow track via zone) with only the magnetics' own nets exempt. An RJ45 and a PHY instance sharing the magnetics give one area. Generated at confidence ≥ apply and used for routing with --component-rules on only. On PCBench (the 30 boards whose file names an RJ45), 54 Ethernet instances on 27 boards: discrete magnetics bound on 7 boards (KiwiSDR, Own-Mailbox ×4, PoEPi ×2; 13 instances), 10 MagJack instances "not required"; all capped at confidence 60 (KiCad 5, no pin names), so no void is generated there unless the user asserts the category; with assert {"P3": "ethernet"} on Own-Mailbox pierre the void is generated on In1.Cu and given to the router. Not verified: that KiCad applies the sidecar zone constraint (kicad-cli DRC reports nothing for a malformed .kicad_dru either, so a silent run proves nothing). Tests: [ethernet] (2 and 4 layers, shared magnetics, MagJack, through-hole magnetics, unbound role, sidecar text, user disable).

Connector edge attraction (D42), opt-in: tracemaker-place --component-rules soft --edge-attraction (an error with off/report). crules::edge_attractions lists the anchors of instances with a connector edge rule (CONN-01, USB2-11, DISP-02; not RFM-01/ANT-02, not advisory DBG-03, not disabled), once per footprint, never locked parts or pin headers/sockets. The placer (ExtractOptions::edge_pulls) adds, for each such part that is movable, a one-pin affinity net from the courtyard point nearest to the outer outline to that segment's axis (PNet::has_ax/ has_ay), weight 20 × --crules-weight. net_hpwl includes the fixed coordinate, so the annealer's incremental integer cost stays exact (tested with independent runs, tempering and LNS); the weighted median move uses it; the global (quadratic) stage and the HPWL lower bound ignore it (the bound stays a lower bound). Reported HPWL and crossings exclude it. Connectors already at the edge stay fixed as before (fix_edge_connectors).

Measured with bench/crules_place.py --configs off,soft,soft:--edge-attraction (23 boards of doc 04 §7.3, seed 1, 8 threads). Connector edge distance = CONN-01's measure (nearest courtyard vertex to Edge.Cuts, once per connector); the per-board median and mean are then taken over boards. off and soft reproduce §14.3 exactly.

Config HPWL median HPWL vs off (geo-mean) connector edge, median of board medians median of board means connectors ≤ 1 mm from the edge (sum, 148 connectors) pads ≤ 5 mm from the edge box (sum) off 518.3 1.000 1.81 mm 2.17 mm 52 105 soft 518.3 0.996 1.81 mm 2.36 mm 52 105 soft + edge attraction 518.3 1.004 1.75 mm 1.81 mm 58 117 human placement – – 1.81 mm 2.45 mm – –

The pull changes the result on 5 boards (the others have no movable connector with an edge rule: their connectors are at the edge and fixed, or are pin headers). There, mean connector distance: ChirpHardware 6.2 → 2.1 mm, LadybugLiteBlue 5.8 → 2.1, kitspace_training_board 11.4 → 1.6 (6 of 6 connectors now within 1 mm), nanoTracer 4.0 → 3.4, Microdox unchanged (3.9); HPWL +3.8 % geo-mean on these 5 (Chirp +7.7 %, Ladybug +6.3 %, training +2.2 %, nanoTracer +3.3 %, Microdox −0.2 %). Costs: decoupling distance worse on 2 boards (training board 11.2 → 27.2 mm, nanoTracer 5.8 → 10.0 mm) because the connectors take edge space the ICs and their caps had. So edge attraction does what it is meant to, at a wirelength and (on two boards) decap cost; it stays opt-in, default off.

docs.title: 15. Net classes from rules (P5, 2026-10-06)
docs.text:
crules::synthetic_net_classes (crules/netclasses.cpp) turns three kinds of evaluated rule into net classes:

Rule kind Needs Class gets impedance a stackup, so that a width (and pair gap) was computed (§5.3) track width = the front-layer solution; for a differential target also the pair width and gap width_for_current with a current the IPC-2221 width (35 µm copper assumed without a stackup, said in the report) track width = the outer-layer width width_for_current with min_width_mm only (USBC-08) nothing track width = that minimum

Limits that keep it conservative (§3.5): only instances at the apply threshold; only the nets bound to the rule's applies_to roles; only nets the board leaves in its Default class (a board class always wins, and the rule then reads "satisfied by board"); the width is never below the Default class's width for single-ended rules, nor below the board minimum; a second rule on the same net can only widen its class. The classes are named tmk_<RULE>_<anchor reference>, live in memory only (rule 8) and are listed in every mode; the router uses them with --component-rules on (route_job.cpp, component_rule_net_classes in the route JSON).

The router has one width per net. The front-layer solution is used on every layer, and the report says so when another layer would need a different width (stripline inner layers; inner layers for current). Per-layer widths are not built. Pin escapes still use the neck-down width where the class width does not fit a pad row.

Examples (route --component-rules on): StickHub (two layers, 1.6 mm): tmk_USB2-01_J1, pair 0.760 mm / gap 0.150 mm for 90 Ω on F.Cu, nets D+ and D−. CM5 Minima: tmk_USBC-08_J101 0.2 mm for CC1/CC2; tmk_USBC-09_J101 1.367 mm for 3 A on +5V (inner layers would need 8.189 mm). PCBench boards have no stackup, so no impedance class is ever made for them: the quick tier is unaffected, and routing stays off by default.

Test: [netclass] in crules/test_impedance.cpp (the class carries the computed pair solution; exactly the two nets resolve to it; a net with a board class of its own is left alone; no stackup, no impedance class).

docs.title: 16 — Plan: matching tscircuit on BGA breakout boards
docs.text:
Status: Partly built

Part of this page describes code that exists; the rest is a plan. The page says which is which.

Part of the TraceMaker plan. Start at ../PLAN.md. Written 2026-10-11.

Status: partly built (2026-10-11, §10 has the outcomes). §1–§9 are the plan as written before any experiment; §10 records what the experiments found and what was built. Where §1–§9 say "TraceMaker will", read it as a proposal. The evidence is in ../research/bga-routing-2026-10.md; evidence tags [V] verified, [A] abstract only, [C] calculated are used the same way here. Proposed milestone: M14. This note changes no code, so it adds no row to 12-decisions.md; the decisions it proposes (§7) get their rows when they are made.

docs.title: 1. Goal and scoreboard
docs.text:
Goal. Route at least as many of tscircuit's BGA boards as tscircuit's router does, judged by KiCad's DRC (and, as a second score, tscircuit's own relaxed checker), without adding a DRC error to any board.

Track Set tscircuit (dashboard run 38105514608-1, commit 65522c8, 2026-10-11, 1x effort) TraceMaker today (doc 10 §7, 50 M work, one variant, one thread) Gate A srj19 (200 BGA breakouts, 2 layers, MIT) 92.0 % completed, 90.0 % relaxed pass (184 / 180 boards) 79.5 % clean (159 boards) ≥ 184 clean and ≥ 180 relaxed A srj20 (200 BGAs with missing balls, 2 layers, no licence: local use only) 78.5 % / 78.5 % (157 boards) 50.0 % clean (100 boards) ≥ 157 clean and ≥ 157 relaxed B fanout31 (72 SoC fan-out cases, 8-layer fixtures) 48 / 72 solved (committed report 2026-09-09, 120 s per case) not run; no importer for the boundary-port semantics ≥ 48 / 72 (same cases, all balls validated)

Rules for the comparison:

  • Pin the opponent. tscircuit's rates moved from 91.5 / 77 to 92.0 / 78.5 within a day. Every quoted figure names a dashboard run id; bench/ stores the per-board JSON of the pinned run so results can be joined board by board.
  • Matched effort, stated. tscircuit's setting is 360 s per board on a 32-vCPU runner (median 19–23 s). Report two rows: TraceMaker at the current standard budgets, and at ≤ 360 s wall on ≤ 32 threads (the portfolio is allowed; it is how this router uses cores).
  • Tune / hold out. Tune on samples 1–100 of each set, report on all 200, and keep 101–200 untouched until a change is final (CLAUDE.md's held-out rule; the sets are public and small enough to overfit).
  • Never lose a board. Three srj19 boards (24, 54, 126) are clean in TraceMaker and fail tscircuit's check; keep them. A change that drops a currently clean board is a regression (rule 9).

docs.title: 2. What exists (and where)
docs.text: The SRJ importer/exporter, the two benchmark sets and the scorer (D90) live on branch t6-srj (commit c00c71a), and bus routing (D91) and after-route passes (D92) on srj-bus-postroute; none of it is on main. M14.0 below merges it. The router, escape corridors (--escape-plan), the flow planner (--escape-flow, doc 05 §14), the escape feasibility analysis (tracemaker escape), differential pairs (D50) and zone-aware routing (§26) are on main.

docs.title: 3. What the data says
docs.text:
All figures: the 400 boards of srj19/srj20, TraceMaker at 50 M work from build/t6-srj/bench/results/*-w50m, tscircuit from the pinned dashboard run. Computed in this session [C].

3.1 The gap is a cliff in board size, not a general weakness.

Connections per board srj19: boards TM tscircuit srj20: boards TM tscircuit < 20 26 100 % 100 % 25 100 % 100 % 20–39 94 100 % 99 % 74 92 % 100 % 40–59 60 63 % 82 % 57 12 % 88 % 60–79 17 6 % 71 % 30 0 % 23 % ≥ 80 3 0 % 0 % 14 0 % 7 %

By straight-line crossings between a board's connections (a proxy for how many escapes must swap sides): below 100 crossings TraceMaker passes all 103 srj19 boards and all 64 srj20 boards (tscircuit: 102 and 64); at 100 or more crossings TraceMaker passes 58 % (56 of 97 boards, srj19) and 26 % (36 of 136, srj20) against tscircuit's 80 % and 68 %. The boards TraceMaker loses and tscircuit wins have a median of 331 (srj19) and 289 (srj20) crossings.

3.2 The misses are not near-misses. Of the 81 boards that tscircuit solves and TraceMaker does not, 32 leave more than ten connections open, 24 leave six to ten, and only 11 leave one or two. A last-few-connections tool (exact window solve, group re-route: doc 05 §17 found no effect) cannot close most of the gap.

3.3 Per-ball escape is not the limit. tracemaker escape reports every ball escapable on every board checked (srj19 samples 11, 19, 31, 117 fail in both routers); escape --flow plans samples 19 and 117 entirely on the pad layer. A ball can leave alone and the set of balls still cannot be completed: the connections have fixed destinations (I/O pads around the package, passives on the other side), so the escapes must also arrive in a compatible order, and the unordered flow model ignores that (research L2).

3.4 More search does not close it, and the escape plans do not help. srj19 stops improving between 50 M and 200 M (88 % on its first 50 boards); the eight-variant portfolio at 10 M equals one variant at 50 M; --escape-plan and --escape-flow lower both sets' clean rate (66 → 60 % and 34 → 32 / 28 %). srj20 is still rising with budget (46 → 56 % at 200 M), so part of that set is budget-limited.

3.5 tscircuit's router is topology first. Its stages: escape-via location → topology planning → a capacity-mesh global path per connection (1.8–2.2 s of ~70–105 s) → per-cell high-density routing (37–41 % of time) → force improve (27–36 %) → DRC repair (12–21 %). Most of its failures (8 of 20, 35 of 43) are timeouts inside force improve. It uses more vias: 72 per board against TraceMaker's 44 on the 156 srj19 boards both solve (57 against 40 on the 100 srj20 boards both solve; 66 % and 43 % more) [C].

3.6 Geometry. At 0.8 mm pitch a channel holds one track, and a through via at an interstice closes the two channels it touches on both layers (research §A). On two layers every escape is a channel or a via site; they compete.

docs.title: 4. Hypotheses and the experiments that test them
docs.text:
None of the explanations below is established. The first milestone runs the cheap experiments, and the build list in §5 is ordered by what they find. A hypothesis is dropped when its experiment fails its stated test.

# Hypothesis Experiment Supported if / dropped if H1 Crossings are resolved by search order, not by a plan. The sequential router commits early escapes that make later crossings impossible (3.1, 3.2, 3.3) E1, topology oracle. Run tscircuit's router locally (already fetched in bench/data/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter) on the 81 gap boards; from its output extract each connection's layer sequence and via positions; give TraceMaker those vias as fixed waypoints (soft cost bonus around them) and route Supported if TraceMaker then completes ≥ 70 % of the 81 boards. Dropped if it completes < 30 %: the limit is then detailed search or geometry, not topology H2 Under-use of vias at the package. tscircuit uses 43–66 % more vias on the same boards (3.5); our cost model makes vias too dear near a dense package E2. Scale the via cost to a fraction (1/2, 1/4) inside the package footprint + 2 mm on the 81 gap boards, one variant, 50 M Supported if clean rate on the gap boards rises ≥ 10 points with no tune-set board lost. Dropped if flat or lower H3 The lattice wastes channel width. A track on a lattice node cannot sit centred in a 0.44 mm channel for 0.15 mm + 2 × 0.10 mm; the half-pitch last-gasp rung does not cover whole fan-outs E3. Re-run the gap boards with the lattice pitch halved (budget scaled) and with channel-centred pad-escape stubs (pad_cells) Supported if clean rate rises ≥ 10 points at equal expansions. Dropped otherwise H4 srj20 is partly a budget limit. Its curve still rises at 200 M (3.4), and 35 of tscircuit's 43 failures are timeouts E4. srj20 at 200 M and 800 M, eight variants, on the 56-core machine, wall time recorded Supported if the rate reaches ≥ 65 % with no structural change. Tells how much of the srj20 gap is plain compute H5 Part of the unsolved boards is infeasible. 17 srj19 and 43 srj20 boards defeat both routers E5. A joint (not per-ball) cut bound: demand versus capacity across the package edge per layer, as R6 does for boards (doc 05 §20), using the exact gap capacities of escape_flow Gives the denominator for "feasible boards", as clean_pass_feasible does for PCBench. A proof of infeasibility on a board removes it from the target, with the cut printed

E1 is the deciding experiment. It separates "TraceMaker needs a topology planner" from "TraceMaker's detailed search cannot realise a good topology", which need different work. It uses tscircuit's code only as a measurement instrument on public data; nothing of it enters the engine.

docs.title: 5. Features to add, in order
docs.text: Order follows what E1–E5 are expected to show; reorder once they have run. Each item lands with its reference path and equivalence test (rule 3), integer fixed-point costs and fixed tie-breaks (rule 2), and is an option or portfolio arm until the quick tier and the srj tune half show no regression (rule 9).

docs.title: F0. Tooling (M14.0; no router change)
docs.text:
1. Merge t6-srj and srj-bus-postroute into main. Quick tier must stay byte-identical (D90 reports it so).
  2. bench/srj_vs_tscircuit.py: join a TraceMaker run with a stored dashboard run JSON (data/runs/<id>.json, one file kept under bench/data/tscircuit/dashboard/, not committed) and print the 2×2 table, the gap boards, and per-bucket rates as in §3.
  3. Failure classifier in bench/run.py output: per open connection, "no channel / no via site / ripped too often / budget" from the router's existing reason strings, so progress can be attributed.
  4. A crossings column in the board JSON (the proxy of §3.1), so a new board's difficulty is known before routing.

docs.title: F1. Package-scale breakout planner (the main build; depends on E1 supporting H1)
docs.text:
A planner for ordered escape on the pad-gap graph, run before the search and used as guidance.

  • Graph. Nodes: the gaps and interstices between pads (as escape_flow already builds them), with capacities from exact geometry including the diagonal (research L1); via sites as layer-change edges that remove the channels they touch (3.6); a few coarse nodes outside the package towards each destination pad.
  • Problem. Each connection is a commodity with a fixed source ball and destination pad (research L2). Choose a path of (layer, gap) steps. Crossings between paths on one layer are forbidden; a crossing is resolved by giving one path a via site and the other layer.
  • Method. Negotiated congestion (PathFinder: McMurchie and Ebeling, FPGA 1995, already the basis of doc 05) over the gap graph with via-site and channel capacities as the shared resources; a one-layer planar subset first (Ozdal and Wong's maximal planar subset, research §B) as the initial layer assignment, the rest to the other layer.
  • Output as guidance, not reservation. A cost bonus along the planned path, and a fixed-cost via site per connection that needs one; never corridors that block other nets. Reservations are the thing that made every earlier escape plan lose (M1, M2, M3).
  • Reference and equality. With guidance disabled the router is byte-identical to today's. A test builds boards where the plan is trivial (one ring) and checks the plan equals the old corridors' escape.
  • Kill criterion. If E1 shows the oracle topology is not enough (H1 dropped), do not build F1; do F2/F3 first.

docs.title: F2. Joint via-site assignment (depends on H2)
docs.text: escapeViaLocationSolver is tscircuit's first stage. Match balls that need a via to interstice sites in one min-cost matching: cost by distance and by how many channels the site closes, hard constraint that a via and a track through the same interstice cannot coexist (3.6), and a joint choice rather than greedy (tscircuit's own fix, research T7). Extends the dog-bone corridors of doc 05 §12 from "pointing away from the centre" to a matched set. If E2 supports H2 with only a via-cost change, F2 is that cost change and stops there.

docs.title: F3. Channel-centred pad stubs and a finer last rung (depends on H3)
docs.text: Escape stubs that centre the track in the channel, and a half-pitch retry of a whole fan-out (not a window) before the net is declared boxed in. Small, local to pad_cells and the escalation rungs.

docs.title: F4. Compute plumbing (depends on H4)
docs.text: Run the portfolio with the cores the machine has and a wall-time budget of 360 s; report work and wall separately (D86). No algorithm change; it fixes how srj20 is reported against a 32-vCPU opponent.

docs.title: F5. A joint feasibility certificate (E5; independent)
docs.text: Extend --cut-report to the package: per layer, capacity of the pad-gap graph across a cut around the package against the number of connections that must cross it, with the over-full cut printed. Also gives infeasibility proofs without a SAT solver. A SAT/CP window solver (research L4, L7) is not proposed: only 11 of the 81 gap boards are within two connections of done (3.2), and doc 05 §20 already found an exact window model would mostly answer "feasible, the heuristic just did not find it". Revisit if F1 leaves many near-misses.

docs.title: F6. Gridless polish (low priority; depends on H3 and on F1 leaving clearance-limited failures)
docs.text: tscircuit spends 27–36 % of its time in a force-based improver, and it is where most of its timeouts are. A TraceMaker equivalent would be a transaction (rule 4) that nudges committed tracks and vias apart inside a window to open a channel, accepted only if the exact check passes and an open connection then routes. Build only if E3 shows clearance-limited failures; otherwise it adds work without moving the gate.

docs.title: Track B: fan-out of SoC packages (fanout31)
docs.text:
A different problem (research §A): a prefix, with boundary exits, plane drops and bus rules, on 4–10 layers. Needed, in order:

  1. B0 baseline. Convert the 72 cases from dataset-fanout31-am62l with the srj-import path (the SRJ in fanout-solver/tests/fixtures/*.json has simpleRouteJson, solverOptions, buses, differentialPairs). Add set fanout31 and report solved / 72 with "every ball validated" as the pass rule, 120 s per case.
  2. B1 boundary ports. A connection whose second point is on the shared breakout edge: the end may slide along the edge, exit order is fixed by the bus, and the route ends exactly on the edge. Model as a row of virtual pads on the edge (off-board edge keep-in), not as a new rule.
  3. B2 plane drops. termination: plane is a via to an inner plane layer; doc 05 §26 (plane-aware routing) covers the router side. The 102–117 plane balls per case compete with signals for interstice sites, so F2 (joint via-site assignment) matters most here.
  4. B3 buses and skew. D91 (buses, skew) and D50 (differential pairs) exist on branches; check that atomic bus layer, all-or-none vias, 45° only and the length-skew limits are what they enforce.
  5. B4 capacity. 8–10 layers at 0.08128 mm tracks: lattice memory and the cost-to-go fields. Measure first.
  6. B5 geometric pre-check. The BGA400 four-layer wall (research T1) means some cases are unroutable under the stated rules; the F5 certificate is the check.

tscircuit solves AM62L 12 / 12, K230 12 / 12, RK3308 9 / 12, i.MX6ULL 11 / 12, T113-S3 4 / 12 and AM3352 0 / 12. All of AM62L, K230, RK3308 and i.MX6ULL (48 cases) would match the count without T113-S3 or AM3352. Track B is independent of Track A and should start only after M14.1's findings, because F2 serves both.

docs.text:
# Deliverable Gate M14.0 F0 tooling; main holds the SRJ work; tune/hold-out split recorded Quick tier byte-identical; srj_vs_tscircuit.py reproduces §3's tables from the stored run M14.1 E1–E5 run, results written into this document (§4 filled with measured outcomes) Each hypothesis marked supported / dropped with the numbers; build list in §5 re-ordered M14.2 The first of F1 / F2 / F3 that M14.1 supports Tune half (1–100 of both sets): +10 points of clean boards or the feature is removed; no board lost M14.3 The rest of the supported features; F4 and F5 srj19 ≥ 184, srj20 ≥ 157 on all 200 at the matched-effort row; no KiCad DRC error added M14.4 Track B (B0–B5) fanout31 ≥ 48 / 72

If M14.1 shows that neither a planner nor a cost change moves the tune half, the honest outcome is a report that says so and a smaller gate (the boards that E5 does not prove infeasible and that stay budget-limited), not a softened criterion.

docs.title: 7. Decisions proposed (to be recorded when made)
docs.text:
1. Planner output is guidance only, never reservation (research M1–M3).
  2. tscircuit's code is a measurement tool, not a dependency, and its datasets are fetched, never copied (D90).
  3. Exact solvers are used for certificates and small windows, not as the main method (research L7, doc 05 §20).
  4. Learned components are not a dependency (research L10; rule: learned arms only through the bandit).

docs.title: 8. Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation The unsolved boards are infeasible and the gate is unreachable F5 certificates; the report separates feasible and infeasible boards E1 cannot be run (tscircuit's router or its inputs do not run here) It is already in bench/data/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter for the scorer; if node versions block it, hand-extract the topology of a dozen gap boards from the SVG snapshots its repository publishes Overfitting 400 public synthetic boards Tune/hold-out split; PCBench BGA set (17 boards) and quick tier as regression guards Judges differ (KiCad against tscircuit's relaxed check): they disagree on 1–2 boards of 200 (doc 10 §7) Report both; do not tune to the checker's collinear-segment quirk tscircuit's rates keep moving Pin the run id; re-join on a newer run as a separate row srj20 has no licence Local benchmarking only; nothing copied into the repository (D90) The synthetic boards are two-layer and may not predict real BGA boards Keep PCBench and the DAC2020 set in the regression gate; Track B adds real SoC packages

docs.title: 9. Open questions
docs.text:
1. Whether the unsolved 17 / 43 boards are infeasible (E5).
  2. What tscircuit's force-improve stage does; its write-up was not found, so F6 is a guess from the timing.
  3. Whether a 36–54 ball srj board's difficulty comes from the destination order or from the passives on the other side (srj19 failures have a median of 42 bottom-layer destinations against 8–9 on successes; srj20 has none on the bottom). E1 and the bucket tables should be split by that too.
  4. Whether fanout31's fixtures are the cases tscircuit's committed 48 / 72 refers to: the committed report is a month older than the latest fixes, so the gate may need re-pinning once B0 runs.

docs.title: 10. Outcomes (2026-10-11)
docs.text:
Measured on this machine (bench/run.py, KiCad's DRC as the judge, one variant, no GPU, work budgets; the gap sets are bench/sets/srj19-gap.txt and srj20-gap.txt: the 24 and 57 boards tscircuit's router solves and TraceMaker at 50 M did not).

Hypotheses.

# Result H1 topology (E1) Not supported. tscircuit's own routes, run locally (bun, AutoroutingPipelineSolver9) on 12 gap boards and given as soft or hard path guides (--guide, radii 1.5–8 pitches): 440–499 of 570 connections routed, baseline 499. Guiding a connection along tscircuit's geometry does not complete the board; the lattice cannot reproduce its off-grid copper and the neighbours' lanes then differ. As a sanity check, TraceMaker's own complete solution as a guide reproduced only 36–40 of 41 H2 vias (E2) Weak. Via cost 3 → 0.3 mm: gap boards 76.7 → 80.9 % of connections, 0 → 2 clean of 24. tscircuit uses 43–66 % more vias, but cheaper vias alone do not close the gap H3 lattice (E3) Dropped. 20 µm lattice 61.6 % (below 76.7 %), 50 µm 78.9 %, 60 µm 77.9 % at equal work H4 budget (E4) Supported for srj19: the 24 gap boards reach 95.7 % of connections and 6 clean at 200 M (median 192 s), and most remaining failures are one to three connections. At 10 M the strict first pass and its reachability floods use the whole budget (flood cells count 1:1 toward --work), so negotiation never runs H5 feasibility (E5) Not built. The failures TraceMaker leaves are dominated by negotiation churn ("ripped up by X and not routed again": 585 of about 1,170 srj20 failures), not by proven infeasibility

What moved the numbers.

Change Result --max-rips 40 --max-passes 40 (now the defaults; were 8 and 12) srj19 gap, 50 M, fast bends: 33 % → 54 % clean. ctest 253/253; quick and mid byte-identical at their budgets Fast bends (--fast-bends) At equal wall time (srj19 gap, 21 s): 81.7 % → 85.9 % routed, 0 → 3 clean of 24; at 20 M: 7 clean (29 %) Profile P1 = fast bends + the two limits, 50 M, one variant, all 200 boards srj19 176/200 = 88.0 % (79.5 % before; tscircuit 92.0 %); srj20 117/200 = 58.5 % (50.0 %; tscircuit 78.5 %); no board lost except srj19 sample 62 Default portfolio (8 variants, 50 M each, 8 threads, median 135–140 s) on the boards P1 misses srj19: 10 of 24 closed → about 186/200 = 93 % (estimate: the full set was not re-run under the portfolio); srj20: 9 of 83 closed → about 126/200 = 63 % --package-pen (tracks on the pad layer inside a ball-grid package cost more) srj20 gap, 30 M: 13 → 15 / 16 / 17 clean of 57 at 0.5 / 2 / 4 pitches, 10 at 8; srj19 gap: noise (9 / 8 / 11 of 24). Used (3 pitches) in the seeded portfolio variants only

Tried and dropped (all kept as hidden options, --help does not list them; every one measured at equal work):

Option Result --layer-assign (two-layer max-cut of the connections' straight chords: 396 crossing pairs → 128 on one layer) srj20 gap 18 % → 14 % / 11 % clean --order 1 (longest first), --order 3 (deep package pins first) srj19 gap: 76.7 % → 54.9 % and 68.6 % routed --no-strict-first (negotiate from the first pass) 76.7 % → 72.7 % --global, --global --global-confine, --global-congestion 69.8 %, 69.2 %, 76.5 % (baseline 76.7 %) --lns-open (lift the neighbours of an open connection, route it first, reroute them in seeded orders) Never reached at 50 M: the passes use the whole budget first. Not measured further --max-victims 1/2/3 srj20 gap: 28 % → 2 / 5 / 7 % clean --soft-growth (PathFinder's growing crossing cost) srj20 gap: 23 % → 16 % / 23 % --history-weight 2/8/30/100 28 % / 26 % / 28 % / 28 %: no effect 24 seeded variants on one hard srj20 board (sample 100) all 24 end at 33–40 of 52; more seeds do not complete it, and tscircuit's own run takes 399 s

What tscircuit does that TraceMaker does not (rendered, bench/render_srj.py): its solution of srj20 sample 100 has 168 vias for 52 connections, long straight runs on both layers and parallel bundles to the edge pads; TraceMaker's best has 86 vias and long detours along the rim. The open connections are interior balls whose escapes were ripped. A planner that decides layer and via sites per connection before routing (F1, F2 of §5) is still the untried candidate; the cheap proxies above (via cost, package penalty, layer assignment, guides) did not stand in for it.

Track B (fanout31). Built: bench/prepare_fanout31.py, bench/fanout31_run.py, and importer features (doc 08 §9): plane terminations become zones, breakout points take the layer their bus gives in connectionExitTargets, pads of a net that no connection point lies on become keep-outs (--unpointed-keepout; the problem asks only for the fan-out at the SoC), --outline-margin-mm, and the extension tracemakerTrackLayers. Without these the first case routed 51 of 149 connections; with them it routes 100 of 100. Trials at 60 M work, one variant, 40 µm lattice: AM62L top-centre 133/133, RK3308 top-centre 160/160, i.MX6ULL left-centre 100/100, all with 0 unconnected after the zone refill; T113-S3 top-left 6 open of 123; AM3352 top-centre 50 open of 316 (tscircuit solves none of the AM3352 cases). The full 72-case result is in §10.1 once the run has finished.

docs.title: 11. Second round (2026-10-11, afternoon)
docs.text:
What moved the numbers (srj20 gap boards = the 57 that tscircuit solves and the first profile missed; 30 M work, one variant, fast bends):

Change Result Breakout-point model for fanout31: drop the layer override from connectionExitTargets (TM_SRJ_EXIT_LAYERS keeps it as an experiment) K230 terminals: 8 open → 2 on case 28, 65 of 65 terminals escape (before: 57 of 65). Several buses' breakout points share coordinates and differ only by layer; overriding the layer stacked two or three terminals on one layer and made them unreachable --layer-dir-pen P (orthogonal steps against the layer's preferred direction cost P pitches; even layers horizontal, odd vertical) srj20 gap: 28 % → 30 / 40 / 35 / 30 % clean at P = 0.15 / 0.3 / 0.5 / 1.0, routed 87.7 % → 89.0 / 89.8 / 90.7 / 91.0 %. srj19 gap: 46 % → 50 % at 0.3. Swapping the directions (--layer-dir-swap): 37 %, no difference. The first structural gain on srj20 Automatic settings (D98): direction penalty 0.3 and package penalty 3 on a breakout board (two layers, at least 70 % of the connections have an end on a package of at least 30 same-layer SMD pads) Same results as setting them by hand (40 % clean on the srj20 gap boards). On ordinary two-layer boards the same two settings cost completion (quick 89.2 → 86.8 % with the direction penalty alone, 88.2 % with the package penalty alone; mid 53.5 → 51.1 %), which is why the rule is limited to breakout boards: with it quick (30) and mid (11) are byte-identical Portfolio of 16 variants (--variants 16 --threads 16) on the boards one variant misses, 50 M each srj19: 7 of 19 closed (median 164 s); see §11.1 for srj20

Measured and dropped: --heuristic-weight 1.5 / 2.5 (weighted A*): 4 % clean, so path quality matters a lot; --layer-assign-angle (layer preference by chord direction): 33 %; via cost 1.0 / 1.5 / 5.0 with the automatic settings: 26 / 37 / 37 % (default 3 mm: 40 %); --polish 0.3 (reserve a share of the budget, restore the best state, rebuild the open connections' neighbourhoods): closes 0–1 of 3–6 open connections and loses more in the shortened main phase.

Where the srj20 gap is. By connections per board (tscircuit solves / TraceMaker, first profile at 50 M → 200 M on the gap boards): fewer than 40: 99 / 99; 40–49: 29 / 21 → 23; 50–59: 21 / 4 → 7; 60–79: 7 / 0 → 1; 80 or more: 1 / 0. The deficit is the 50–79 connection boards. tscircuit's solution of sample 69 (53 connections) has 803 mm of copper and 188 vias, 173 of them outside the ball array (in the annulus between the array and the edge pads); inside the array it uses about as much wire as TraceMaker.

docs.text:

One variant solves 44 of the first 59; the 8-variant portfolio (60 M each) closes the stragglers (57 of 60); 16 variants close the three AM3352 left-edge cases yes No DRC error added, quick/mid unchanged 0 added on every run; byte-identical yes

Final checks (2026-10-11, evening). ctest 254/254 on release; quick (30) and mid (11) byte-identical to the start of the day. The first version of the breakout rule (any package of at least 30 same-layer SMD pads) also matched the bus_route fixture's two connectors and failed it (13 of 24 routed); the rule now needs a ball-grid-like package: at least 5 distinct columns and rows with at least 40 % of the grid cells filled, so connectors and QFPs no longer qualify, and the srj results did not change (gap boards 23 of 57 clean either way). An asan build compiled and ran the suite: all tests passed except the importer test that expected the removed exit-layer override (fixed) and bus_route / thread_determinism, which are too slow under asan to finish in the time available (not run to completion).

docs.title: 12. Third round (M15, 2026-10-11 evening): negotiation as transactions
docs.text:
The goal was srj20 (133/200 against tscircuit's 157). Fifteen ideas were tried at equal work; one of them, and an accounting correction that came with it, moved the numbers. Raw numbers: dev/m15-notes.md; assumptions taken without asking: dev/assumptions-m15.md.

What was found about plain negotiation. On a 53-connection board (srj20 sample 069, 30 M work) the routed count of the negotiation phase wobbles between 30 and 41 for the whole budget and the run ends at 30; only the best snapshot (41) is returned. A connection that cannot be routed rips the 1–10 connections in its way (median 4), those cannot all be routed again, and the next one rips them back: the oscillation PathFinder-type negotiation is known for (research note C5). The open connections that remain on boards with 1–2 open are mostly outer-ring balls with a partner pad 10–17 mm away across the board, not deep balls: the long connections are the ones left without a corridor.

Transactions (--txn, D99). A negotiated route that rips victims is kept only if the victims can be routed again strictly (without ripping anything) and the net change in routed connections is at least zero (--txn 1; --txn 2 needs a gain). Otherwise the whole board goes back to the state before the route (a snapshot of the copper of every connection; history stays, so the next try takes another path). This is MAPF-LNS2's acceptance rule applied to rip-up and re-route. A route that loses k connections net is still kept with probability exp(−k/T) (--txn-temp T, seeded counter-based draws: deterministic); T = 1.5 on breakout boards.

Experiment (srj20, 57 gap boards, 30 M, one variant) Clean Completion plain negotiation 23 90.9 % --txn 1 (greedy: net ≥ 0 only) 12 94.9 % --txn 2 (net > 0 only) 4 90.4 % --txn 1 --txn-temp 0.25 / 0.5 / 1 / 2 / 4 17 / 18 / 23 / 24 / 23 95.2–95.6 % temperature falling to 0 (--txn-cool 1), T = 1 / 2 20 / 22 95.4 / 95.5 % nested transactions for victims (--txn-depth 1 / 2) 14 / 13 94.5 / 94.3 %

Greedy transactions raise completion by four points but leave 14 boards with exactly one connection open; annealing acceptance turns some of them into complete boards. At 100 M work (57 boards): plain 28 clean, T = 1/2/4 cooled 30/32/34, T = 2 uncooled 36 (completion 97.8 % against 93.9 %). On the 76 boards that one variant at 50 M leaves open: 100 M plain 5 clean, with transactions 9.

Budget accounting and reachability floods. --work counts a reachability-flood cell like an A* expansion, but a flood cell costs a small fraction of the time (field construction and the A* itself dominate). With --reach-check 2 (flood before every strict search) and a flood cell counted at a quarter of an expansion (--flood-work-pct 25), 30 M work buys about twice the search: 30 of 57 clean (52.6 %) in 137 s CPU per board, against 23 in 106 s for transactions alone and 23 in 71 s for plain negotiation.

Engine speed. The cost-to-go field was 47 % of the time of a transaction run. Its inputs (pass/via masks from the fixed-copper cache, target cells, costs) are identical for repeated searches of one connection once the fixed-copper cache is complete, so --field-prefill 1 (fill the cache for the whole board at the first field) with --field-cache-mb (keep fields, reuse on an identical input, confirmed by a byte comparison) gives the same copper (sample 123: byte-identical) in 62 % of the time (hits 236 of 300 fields). It is not byte-identical on ordinary boards (6 of the 30 quick boards differ: a stronger heuristic breaks ties differently), so it is part of the breakout profile only. gprof of a transaction run: search() 26 % self, field_cpu 20 %, routed_copper_part 16 %, point_state 7.5 %.

Breakout profile (D100). On a breakout board (D98) the router now also uses: --txn 1 --txn-temp 1.5, --reach-check 2, --flood-work-pct 25, --field-prefill 1, --field-cache-mb 512. Explicit options win; --breakout-profile 0 turns the last four off. Elsewhere nothing changed: quick (30) and mid (11) are byte-identical (ctest 262 → see final checks).

Portfolio on a breakout board (D101). With --variants > 1 a board that looks like a breakout gets its own list instead of the designed eight (exact bends, longest first and the 2× pitch variants are wrong for it): variant 0 is the plain profile, the others draw order (shortest first, deep pins first, jittered), via cost, crossing cost, direction strength, package penalty and temperature with a counter-based generator. --rounds R (automatic: 4) splits the budget; after each round every variant starts from the best state of all variants (their copper per connection is a warm start, matched by the two pads of each connection) and negotiates from there with its own parameters. Selection is by the usual total order, so the result does not depend on thread timing. On 39 of the 76 boards one variant leaves open (16 variants × 30 M, 16 threads, 107–117 s wall per board, no GPU): the designed list with the profile 11 clean and 342 connections open in total; the breakout list 12 clean, 319 open; with four rounds 12 clean, 284 open. Rounds improve the boards that stay open more than they complete new ones.

Measured and dropped (hidden options stay, D94 practice): lattice pitch 36.7/44/45/55 µm (neutral, ±3 boards of noise), victims re-routed in several orders (--txn-orders: 4 and 1 clean of 76 against 7), cap on victim re-route searches (--txn-cap), tidy sweeps (--tidy: re-route each connection alone, keep if shorter: 10–20 shortened per sweep, no extra boards), stall restarts (--stall-passes), net orders 1/2/3 under the new profile, per-net routed-state cache (identical, no speed-up).

Gate Target After M14 After M15 srj19 clean ≥ 184/200 188 (181 + 7) 191/200 = 95.5 %: 178 (32 s CPU per board; P2 at 50 M plain: 181 at 46 s) + 13 of the 22 the portfolio takes (mean 91 s wall) srj20 clean ≥ 157/200 133 (124 + 9) 160/200 = 80.0 % (tscircuit 157; 156 within 330 s): 129 (59 s CPU per board; P2: 124 at 67 s) + 19 of the 71 the portfolio takes + 8 of the 24 near boards (fewer than 70 connections) that 70 M work in four rounds (mean 227 s, at most 324 s wall; --time 330) closes + 4 of the 16 still open with GPUs on and 150 M work (mean 377 s, at most 433 s wall: over the 360 s of tscircuit's setting, so 156 is the matched figure) fanout31 ≥ 48/72 60 unchanged: not a breakout board (8–10 layers), the profile is off (three cases spot-checked at one variant, 60 M: K230 case 28 2 open, T113-S3 case 55 5 open, AM3352 case 70 6 open) No DRC error added, quick/mid unchanged yes yes: 0 added on every run (about 3,000 board routes); quick (30) and mid (11) byte-identical to the baseline outputs; ctest 265/265 on release; the transaction tests pass under ASan

Where the srj20 boards that stay open are: 28 have 70 or more connections (tscircuit solves two of them) and are 8–40 connections short; of the 24 with fewer, the larger budget closed 8 and left 16 with 1–8 open (three with exactly one).

docs.title: 13. Fourth round (2026-10-13): the plateau was the lattice, not the capacity (D103, D104)
docs.text:
Question. After M15 the single configuration stood at srj19 191/200 and srj20 160/200, and up to 199 and about 168 over many long runs; 28 srj20 boards of 70+ connections sat 8-40 connections short and six of them (039, 048, 071, 072, 103, 104) at 1-6 open after three-hour runs that no longer improved. Was that a capacity limit (not enough room between the balls for the tracks) or a search limit?

Measurements (srj20 boards 039, 048, 071, 072, 103, 104; 16-variant portfolio, until complete, 30 min):

Rules Routed of 453 Complete true (0.10 mm clearance), 3 h 436 0 (1-5 open each) clearance 0.08 mm 434 0 clearance 0.06 mm (two tracks fit in a pad gap and between two vias) 453 6, in 3-27 min via 0.25 mm / drill 0.12, clearance 0.1 (via gap 0.55 holds two tracks) 435 0 ball pads 0.26 mm instead of 0.36, clearance 0.1 (pad gap 0.54 holds two tracks) 421 0

Doubling one gap alone did nothing and the step to 0.06 completed everything, which looked like a capacity wall. It is not: (i) warm-starting a run from the 0.06 mm solution completes sample048 at 0.07, 0.08 and 0.085 mm and sample071 at 0.065, rules at which scratch runs stay one connection short; (ii) the 0.085 mm solution of sample048 has no pad gap with two tracks, four via gaps with two (0.9 mm apart, which hold two at 0.10 anyway), and all 131 pairs that are too close at 0.10 mm are 0.087-0.098 mm squeezes; (iii) moving the vertices of the 0.06 mm solutions off the lattice until the 0.10 mm rules hold (route/legalize.cpp, doc 05 §41.3) leaves 071, 104 and (with more sweeps) 039 without a single pair too close, and 103, 048, 072 with 3-9.

Result. Relax, route, legalise (--relax, D104): stage 1 routes under 60 % of the clearance, the solution is legalised to 80 %, the missing connections routed, legalised to 100 %, and a stall at the real rules sends the run back two stages. On the six boards, with the 0.06 mm solutions as the start: 071 (0.2 s), 039, 103 and 048 complete under the real rules in 3-13 min, KiCad DRC with no router-introduced error and nothing unconnected, boards on which three hours of scratch search had stopped with 1-5 connections open.

Reading. The lattice router puts tracks on lattice points (0.035 mm) and cannot move committed routes, so a solution needs more room than the continuous geometry does (spacing 7 steps = 0.245 mm for a 0.22 mm requirement, vias and pad escapes on points); the room is there, it is just not reachable by a router that only commits lattice paths. The remaining failures are local pinches of a topology (a via between a pad and the board edge, a track between a via and a pad) that need a different topology of the nets around them, which the router then has to find.

docs.title: 13.1 What was measured, and what was not
docs.text:
• Six stuck boards, from the 0.06 mm solutions (--warm-pcb + ramp + --legalize, 16 variants, 20 M per round): 071 (0.2 s, one legalisation), 039 (175 s), 103 (173 s), 048 (764 s), 072 (41 min, after several breathing cycles) complete under the real rules, each checked with kicad-cli pcb drc against the true project rules: 0 router-introduced errors, 0 unconnected items. 104 stays one connection short (71/72) after 40 and 60 min runs.
  • From scratch with --relax through bench/run.py (KiCad DRC judged): sample095 65/65 clean (736 s), sample031 65/65 clean (1312 s) and sample159 76/76 clean (1786 s), three boards that had stayed open for hours of earlier search. A batch over the remaining open srj20 boards (27 boards, three lanes) was stopped by decision after these; no composite srj19/srj20 figure was re-measured, so the 191/200 and 160/200 of §12.1 remain the headline figures and the boards above are additional closures from longer runs.
  • Did not help on the last missing connection of sample104/072/031: islands (variants continue from their own stage solutions), finer ramp steps (0.01 mm), a half-pitch lattice (0.0175 mm) for the repair rounds, more projection sweeps (3,000 instead of 300). What helped on 072 and 031 was repeated breathing cycles, i.e. more random re-routes at the relaxed rules followed by legalisation; the fresh restart every third cycle (--ramp-fresh) was added for the same reason and not measured on its own.
  • Cost: the relaxed stage takes minutes on the 60-80 connection boards; a board that fails to complete after the cycles keeps going until --time or the round limit (default 200 rounds of 20 M per variant).
  • Limits of the legaliser: pads count as their bounding rectangles (circles exactly), zones, keep-outs, mounting holes and custom .kicad_dru clearances are not constraints (the exact check that follows drops what they break), and the vertices end off the 45° grid.

docs.title: 17 — Advice files and a pluggable advisor, called only when the router is stuck
docs.text:
Status: Partly built

Part of this page describes code that exists; the rest is a plan. The page says which is which.

Part of the TraceMaker plan. Start at ../PLAN.md. Written 2026-10-14 for issue #26. Milestone M16. Status: stages 0–3 built; stage 4 (placement) is not. §8 holds what was measured, including what did not work.

docs.title: 1. Where a language model belongs
docs.text:
TraceMaker is the deterministic counterweight to an LLM's probabilistic approach (requirement N3, rule 2). A model still has a place: the judgement calls a lattice search cannot make — which part to move when --cut-report proves the placement cannot route, which nets matter, which layer a group should prefer. This document puts it there and nowhere else:

  • Not inside the engine. The tree has no HTTP client, no TLS, no credentials; a non-repeatable call inside a run that must be byte-identical would break N3.
  • Not a separate orchestrator. Users would learn two tools, and the engine would still need the report and hint interfaces, which are the real work.
  • A replaceable advisor, called only when the deterministic route is stuck, talking to the engine through a file.
 route board.kicad_pcb -o out.kicad_pcb --advisor "python3 advisors/tracemaker_advisor.py ..."

   plain portfolio ──► all routed? ── yes ──► done (the advisor is never started)
         │ no
         ▼
   stuck report (JSON) ──► advisor process (stdin → stdout, time-limited) ──► advice (JSON)
                                                                                 │ strict parse + check against the board
                                                                                 ▼
   portfolio again: the unadvised variants + `variants` more, carrying the advice
                                                                                 │ the better result of the two runs is written,
                                                                                 ▼ the advice is saved beside it (out.advice.json)

Three parts, each with one job:

Part Job Where Engine Deterministic and offline. Writes a stuck report; reads an advice file (--advice FILE), typed and strictly checked, that can only change order, cost, and which attempts are made src/advice/, src/route/router.cpp, src/app/route_job.cpp Advisor Any executable: stuck report on stdin, advice on stdout. A person, a script, a local or cloud model advisors/ (reference ones, standard library only) The switch --advisor CMD: plain route first; only if connections are left, consult, then route again with the advice. Without the flag nothing changes, byte for byte run_route_job

docs.title: 2. What it may and may not do (the project's rules)
docs.text: Rule How it holds 1 Correctness Advice never contains copper and never changes a rule's value. Every route still passes the exact check; regions are enforced by it (§4) 2 Determinism The model's answer is frozen in a file. board + options + seed + advice file gives byte-identical output at any thread count (tested). A live run is repeated by --advice out.advice.json 4 Transactions / never worse Advised attempts are extra portfolio variants after the unadvised ones (the next entries of the list, indices from 1000). The winner is the minimum of the portfolio's total order, a tie goes to the unadvised variant, and in --advisor mode the plain result stays unless the advised run's is better 5 Budgets Advice changes no budget. The advisor's wall time is not routing work (--advisor-timeout); each routing run gets the same --work/--time 6 Rules A missing, slow, failing or nonsensical advisor is a warning; the run goes on unadvised, exit code unchanged Untrusted both ways The report quotes net and part names from the board (a prompt-injection surface). Advice is typed data: no commands, no paths, unknown keys are errors. Sending a board to a cloud model is opt-in, the report says what it contains, and --advisor-redact sends aliases

docs.title: 3. The stuck report (stage 0)
docs.text:
route --stuck-report FILE writes it for the run the advisor sees (or the final run, with no advisor); --advisor sends the same JSON on stdin. It is built from the finished route by advice::build_stuck_report (src/advice/stuck_report.cpp). Fields:

Field Content tracemaker_stuck_report 1 (the format version) task one paragraph telling an advisor what is asked and that names are data disclosure redacted, contains (kinds of data sent), does_not_contain (the board file, copper geometry beyond these lists, paths, keys, the advisor command) board name, outline box (mm), copper layers, counts of parts, pads, nets rules clearance, track width and minimum, via size and drill, copper-to-edge clearance result routed / connections, tracks, vias, seconds, the portfolio's variants and their counts, escape_rings (with --escape-report), cuts (with --cut-report) unrouted[] per open connection (up to max_unrouted, 40; unrouted_not_shown counts the rest): net; from / to (part, pad, x_mm, y_mm, layers; to is {"zone": true} for a plane); length_mm; reason; why (the router's own words; omitted when redacted); rips, fails; blockers (nets whose routed copper the last rejected route would have had to rip); region_mm (the two pads ±1.5 mm); crowding (routed copper by net in the region, vias and foreign pads in it) unrouted_by_reason, _by_net, _by_part counts, the largest 16 parts[] the parts at the open ends: kind (grid_array, multi_pin, small_ic, passive), side, pad count, position, number of open ends; library_id and value unless redacted previous_advice the advice already tried and what it gave (later rounds) advice_schema the hint types this engine reads, so an advisor adapts to the engine it talks to

Reason codes (failure_reason_code, router.cpp): boxed_in (fixed copper encloses a pin), exact_check (the lattice path was rejected by the exact check), rip_limit (the only route would rip a protected net, too many connections, or one already ripped too often), ripped_not_rerouted, layer_limit, out_of_budget, rolled_back (a transaction was undone), not_attempted (the budget ended first), no_legal_path. They are the class of the cause, matched from the router's sentences, and they nest: a boxed-in pin is boxed_in whatever later attempts said.

The failure event (doc 13) now has region (the two pads ±1.5 mm, nm; it was [0,0,0,0]) and a new blocker_nets (net ids of the connections the rejected route would have ripped). blockers (object ids) stays empty: doc 06's closed-set boundary analysis is not built, and the victims are the cheap, true part of it.

Redaction. With --advisor-redact every net becomes N1…, every part P1… (in order of first use), value / library_id / why are dropped, and the board name is board. The advice that comes back is mapped to the real names (advice::unalias) before it is checked, and the saved file has the real names, so --advice repeats the run.

docs.title: 4. The advice file (stage 1)
docs.text:
{
  "version": 1,
  "note": "free text, logged, never acted on",
  "variants": 4,
  "first_nets": ["USB_DP", "USB_DM"],
  "priority": [["U1.A1", "J2.3"]],
  "layers": {"no_tracks": ["In2.Cu"], "cost": {"F.Cu": 1.5}},
  "regions": [{"name": "north channel", "rect": [10, 10, 20, 14], "layers": ["F.Cu"], "reserve_for": ["NET1"], "vias": false}]
}
Hint Meaning Existing mechanism it reuses first_nets these nets are routed first, also after restarts, and other nets do not rip them RouterOptions::first_nets (--first-nets) priority these connections (pad to pad, either order; both pads on one net) are routed before the rest RouterOptions::priority, which the knowledge base feeds and the command line does not layers.no_tracks no new tracks there; vias still pass no_track_layers (--no-tracks-on) layers.cost a track on that layer costs this factor more (1 to 1000) layer_cost_pm (--layer-cost) regions a rectangle or polygon (mm, the board file's axes) in which only reserve_for nets may put tracks and vias, or avoid_nets may not; per layer, tracks and/or vias a rule area plus disallow rules (doc 05 §34) variants advised variants to add (1 to 8; --advice-variants overrides) route_portfolio

Regions are rules, not a new obstacle type. A region becomes an in-memory rule area (tmk:advice:N, no keep-out flags: it only names a place) and disallow track via rules whose condition is A.intersectsArea('tmk:advice:N') && A.NetName != 'NET1' && … ("every net but these") or … && A.NetName == 'NET3' (one rule per avoided net), one rule per layer when layers are named. §34's machinery then does what it does for a user's .kicad_dru: the lattice search treats the rule like fixed copper, and the exact check before every commit, escapes, pair legs and clean-up enforces it. Two details matter. KiCad reads a && b || c as a && (b || c), so no || is ever generated. And the rules and the area live only in the router's working copy (RouterOptions::extra_zones / extra_rules, added in Router::Impl and Router::run): the caller's rules are not touched and the output board never contains them. (The positional rules are judged outside the per-class obstacle caches, so net-scoped regions do not need the caches keyed by net.)

Strict reading (parse_advice, modelled on the rule overrides, doc 15 §6.3): an unknown key, a wrong type, a value out of range (coordinates within ±10 m, cost 1–1000, variants 1–8), a duplicate, a region with no area or with both or neither of reserve_for / avoid_nets, or more than 64 first_nets, 512 priority, 24 regions, a 64-point polygon is an error that names the file and the entry (regions[2].rect: has no area); a syntax error gives line and column. check_advice_refs then checks names against the board: unknown nets, layers and pads are errors with a "did you mean", priority pads must lie on one net, no_tracks may not cover every copper layer, net names with a quote or backslash cannot be used in a region. Entries without effect (a region outside the outline, a first_nets net with fewer than two pads) are warnings. tracemaker advice-check BOARD ADVICE runs both checks without routing. (Errors name the file and the JSON path of the entry; the line is given for syntax errors only.)

Advised variants (route_portfolio). With advice, the portfolio is the variants that would run anyway, then variants more: the next entries of the portfolio's list, the very variants a plain run with that many more would have added (same configurations, same seeds), each carrying the hints. They are named <variant> + advice and have indices 1000 + k (route::kAdvisedIndex). So a plain run with V + 4 variants is the exact control for an advised run with V: the only difference is the hints. (A first version advised copies of variants 0, 2, 4, 6. A hint that does nothing then repeats work already done, while the control's extra variants bring new seeds; on the held-out half the control beat it by 11 connections, §8.) Variant results do not depend on each other except through portfolio rounds, so adding variants at the end leaves the unadvised ones as they were (tested), and the total order puts a tie on the unadvised side. The knowledge base is never told about advised variants. route_result_better is the same order for comparing two whole runs.

docs.title: 5. The advisor protocol (stage 3)
docs.text:
--advisor CMD: CMD is run with /bin/sh -c, in its own process group, with the stuck report on stdin; stdout must be exactly one advice file (at most 1 MB), stderr is logged (first 2,000 characters). After --advisor-timeout (120 s) the group is killed. Only the program name is logged and put in the summary (a command line may carry a token). The answer goes through parse_advice, unalias and check_advice_refs; if anything fails the run says why (warning: the advisor's advice was refused: …) and goes on without advice. The accepted advice is saved as <out>.advice.json (--advice-out changes it; with --advisor-rounds N > 1 also <out>.advice.K.json), always with the real names.

--advisor-rounds N repeats the loop while connections are open, each time with the best result so far and previous_advice in the report; every round routes from scratch with that round's advice alone, so the saved file of the last round repeats it.

Each routing run gets the full --work and --time. The advised run contains the unadvised variants again, so an --advisor run costs about twice a plain one; --advice FILE alone costs one run with the extra variants.

docs.title: 6. Reference advisors (advisors/)
docs.text:
• heuristic_advisor.py — no model. Strategies stuck-first (nets of the open connections go first), corridor (a strip along the straight line of each open connection is reserved for its net, on the layer its start pad is on), mixed. It proves the hint channel (§8) and is the smallest example of the protocol.
  • tracemaker_advisor.py — a language model through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (llama-server, Ollama, vLLM, clouds) or the Anthropic Messages API. Standard library only. The key comes from the environment (TRACEMAKER_ADVISOR_API_KEY, else OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), never from the command line. An endpoint that is not on this machine or its network is refused unless --allow-remote is given; what is sent is printed to stderr first. The reply is parsed leniently (a code fence is tolerated), checked against the advice format, and sent back to the model once with the problems if it fails.
  • test_advisors.py — both, against fake servers (no network, no model).
  • A coding agent needs no advisor process. The tracemaker-route skill (skills/, D84) has the agent read --stuck-report, write the advice file itself, check it with tracemaker advice-check and route again with --advice; it puts that after more search (§8.1: the control wins) and says that the hint channel's measured gain is none. Whether a model's own hints do better is the open question of §8.1, not something the skill claims.

Benchmarks always run from recorded advice files (bench/advice_eval.py stores them), so results stay reproducible.

docs.title: 7. Options
docs.text:
Option Meaning --advice FILE use this advice (advised variants run next to the unadvised ones) --advice-variants N advised variants to add (1–8; default the file's, else 4) --advisor CMD consult CMD only if connections are left; route again with its advice --advisor-timeout S its time limit (default 120 s) --advisor-rounds N consult again with the advised result while connections are open (default 1) --advisor-redact aliases for nets and parts in the report --advice-out FILE where the advice that was used is saved (default <out>.advice.json) --stuck-report FILE write the stuck report tracemaker advice-check BOARD ADVICE [--json F] check an advice file against a board

The summary (--json) gets an advice block: the file's hints and warnings, unadvised_best_routed / advised_best_routed / winner_advised of the first run, and per advisor round the program, seconds, outcome or error, routed before and after, and whether the advised result was kept. Viewer events: advice.hint for each hint, and stage events advisor begin/end.

docs.title: 8. What was measured
docs.text: Raw data, the advice files used and the test outputs are in bench/records/m16/; the story of the runs is in dev/m16-notes.md.

docs.title: 8.1 Does a hint channel help? (issue #26 stage 2)
docs.text:
The question is whether advice makes this router route more, before any model is connected. Board set: the 16 srj20 boards of fewer than 70 connections that were still open after the 70 M portfolio run of M15 (bench/sets/srj20-m15fail4.txt: 8 + 8, even and odd index as the tuning half and the held-out half). Configuration: --work 20000000 --variants 8 --threads 8 --no-kb --time 3600 (the breakout portfolio, 4 rounds), bench/advice_eval.py, a rule-based advisor (advisors/heuristic_advisor.py). Counts are connections routed, summed over the half (489 and 492 connections; no board completes in any arm).

Arm Even half (tuning) Odd half (held out) Plain, 8 variants (what advice must beat) 430 439 Control: plain, 12 variants (the advised run's compute without advice) 431 450 Advice mixed (stuck nets first + a reserved strip along each open connection), first design (advised copies of variants 0, 2, 4, 6) 431 439 Advice mixed, final design (advised variants are the next four of the list, the control's own) 431 439 Advice stuck-first only (first design) 430 not run Advice corridor only (0.35 mm half width, vias allowed through; first design) 431 not run Advice corridor, 0.5 mm, other nets' vias allowed (first design) 431 not run Advice stuck-first + layer cost F.Cu x1.4 + 12 priority pairs (first design) 430 not run

What this says:

  • The gate is not met. The gate was "advised runs route more on a held-out half, and never fewer anywhere". "Never fewer" holds by construction (no board did worse in any arm). "More" does not: on the held-out half advice routes exactly what the plain run does (439 and 439), on the tuning half it gains one connection on one board (sample094, 54 to 55), the same total as the control, which gets it on other boards. No strategy tried on the tuning half beat the control.
