  • Seeds beat these hints. The control, the same four extra variants without hints, gains 11 connections on the held-out half (sample173 49 to 53, sample136 58 to 61). The same variants with the hints gain nothing: on the held-out half no advised variant routed more than the best unadvised variant of its own run, and on five of the eight boards they routed fewer. The first design hid this, because its advised copies repeated work that was already done and so could not tell "the hints do nothing" from "the hints hurt".
  • Consistent with the repository's earlier evidence. M14 experiment E1 (doc 16): tscircuit's own finished routes as guides did not help either; the literature note puts language-model routing agents far below classical routers.
  • These are the hints a rule can derive from the report (who is open, where, how crowded). A model might write better ones: judgement about which part to move or which nets matter is what the issue expects it to add, and the placement seams (stage 4) are where that would show. This measurement does not say it cannot; it says the channel gives no free gain, and that the stage 3 gate of the issue (proving the channel without a model first) is not met. Stage 3 is built because it was asked for, it is opt-in, and it cannot make a result worse.

An invalid first batch is worth recording because it nearly produced a false result: the driver did not pass --time, the default 120 s wall limit cut variants short on a loaded machine, and the same command gave different plain counts in three experiments (one board: 54, 50, 54). Advice looked like +3 to +11 connections there. advice_eval.py now passes --time 3600, and every table above comes from runs whose plain column agrees across experiments. (Lesson for any work-budget experiment: check that the arms' shared columns match.)

docs.title: 8.2 Checks
docs.text: Check Result Options off: quick / planes (plain and --soft-zones) / mid against origin/main (49fbd3c), CPU-only builds, bench/compare_runs.py --expect-identical byte-identical: quick 30/30, planes 8/8 and 8/8, mid 11/11 (mid prints Gates: FAIL only because PR #28's judge calls three capped KiCad reports "unknown"; the baseline against itself prints the same) Full test suite 291 of 291 pass, release and CPU-only; the new tests and 11 router-heavy existing ones also pass under ASan + UBSan Same advice file at 1, 2 and 4 threads, and twice: identical bytes generated board (CLI test advice_cli, every run); a real srj20 board (sample100, 1, 2, 4 and 4 threads): one sha256 Bad advice (unknown key, name, layer, syntax error, every layer without tracks): refused naming the file unit tests and advice_cli Advisor absent, failing, slow, rubbish, unknown key, unknown net: output board and exit code as without it, the reason in the summary advice_cli (5 failure kinds and a timeout) Advised result never fewer than unadvised by construction; no board worse in the 8 advised experiments (64 board runs) KiCad DRC adds no error on advised boards 0 router-introduced errors on 10 advised boards checked (5 of each design; drc-advised.txt has the final design's) A real model not verified. The reference advisor was tested against fake OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic servers only. One live request to the shared llama-server on this machine ended in HTTP 503 (its engine stopped, exit -6), a second timed out at 150 s; no further attempts were made on a shared service

docs.title: 9. Not built, and limits
docs.text:
• Stage 4 (placement). Advisor-proposed placements as seeds of routability_loop and proposed moves as ECO candidates (src/place/routable.hpp) are not built: they would be kept only if they route more, through seams that exist, and wait for §8's evidence that hints help at all.
  • Per-net layer preference and per-net guide corridors are new router features the issue asked to add only if the simple hints matter; §8.1 says they do not, so they were not added.
  • A hint that picks an attempt ("run the relax-route-legalise profile", doc 05 §41.3) is the hint type the evidence of this repository favours: boards that no ordering or reservation helped (srj20 039, 048, 071, 103) completed with --relax. It is not built: relax drives the whole portfolio (stages, rounds, legalisation) and is not a per-variant tweak, so it needs its own design.
  • A model that answers with many small, plausible hints costs only the advised variants' time; a model that answers with a region that fences a net out of its own pads can make an advised variant route less, which is why advised variants never replace unadvised ones.
  • The report quotes at most 40 open connections; very large boards need --advisor-rounds or a better summariser.

docs.title: 18 — Candidate features for the roadmap (research and plan)
docs.text:
Status: Plan

Nothing on this page is built yet, or it is a proposal.

Part of the TraceMaker plan. Start at ../PLAN.md. Written 2026-10-14 after M16, issues #4–#8 and #24 were closed. Update (2026-10-16): M17 was built and measured (docs/10 §11, D121, D122, bench/records/m17). Two statements below are corrected by it: PCBWorld's "679 real boards" (§2, §3, A1) are derived from PCBench, so A1 is not an independent second corpus; and the paper was read in full (§1). The rest of this note is as written on 2026-10-14. Update (2026-10-24): D3, the run report, was built (§9, D136). Update (2026-10-27): C3, pours and the layer-count advisor, was built (§10, D138). Status (2026-10-15): adopted as the roadmap's M17–M21 on the owner's answers in §7 (decision D118). Nothing here is built. The candidates keep the numbers they have in §4; §5 is the order that the answers gave. This note changes no code. Evidence tags: [R] checked in this repository (file or doc named), [W] from a web source (vendor claims are marked as self-reported), [A] my estimate or assumption.

docs.title: 1. How this was made, and what it cannot tell you
docs.text:
Read: the roadmap, the open ("not built", "still open", "next") passages of docs 04–17, the non-goals of doc 01, the morning reports, the release page, and the current repository for each gap named below. Searched the web (US-only search tool, standard mode) for KiCad 10's release notes, tuning profiles in KiCad's source documentation, the KiCad IPC API, the commercial AI layout tools, pin swapping, and 2026 papers on learned PCB routing.

Limits, so the ranking is read with them in mind:

  • No user research. Nothing here comes from asking people what they need. The ranking follows evidence in the repository and the field, and two guesses about the audience (§7).
  • Vendor material is self-reported. Quilter, DeepPCB and Flux publish comparisons of themselves; I found no independent validation [W] and quote no vendor number.
  • PCBWorld's paper was not read in full when this note was written (only the abstract page); it was read in full on 2026-10-16 for M17, and its D3 set is derived from PCBench (docs/10 §11.1).
  • Nothing was run for this note except reading. No candidate has a measurement of its own gain yet; each carries the experiment that would give one.

docs.title: 2. Where TraceMaker stands (facts to plan from)
docs.text: Fact Source Clean pass (KiCad judge, 8 variants, 120 s) A 100 % (40/40), B 70.0 % (28/40), C 63.3 % (19/30), D 54.5 % (12/22); Freerouting 2.5: 100 / 50 / 46.7 / 36.4 %. No board has an error added by routing [R] dev/morning-report-2026-10-07.md M8 gate (from-scratch clean pass 90 % on held-out set S) is at 85 %; M9 gate (dense-package boards) is at 41 %; M7's SA-PCB comparison was never measured [R] memory note tracemaker-plan, morning report What fails is fan-out at a package; PCBench boards are judged under KiCad's default rules, which their own human layouts mostly fail (6 of 92 pass) [R] doc 05 §16–§20, doc 04 §10 BGA breakout boards: srj19 about 95 %, srj20 78 % (160/200 with up to 433 s) against tscircuit's 92 % / 79 % [R] README, doc 16 §10 PCBench has no stackups, so impedance classes (doc 15 §15) and the plane-split features (doc 05 §42, §44) cannot be measured on the quick tier; the #24 measurement used four plane boards, one seed [R] doc 15, bench/records/issue24/README.md The router has one width per net; per-layer widths are not built [R] doc 15 §15 (line 1642) No pin or gate swapping; non-goal of version 1, "later, opt-in, with back-annotation" [R] doc 01 §4 --relax completes srj20 boards no ordering or reservation helped; I found no measurement of it on PCBench tiers B–D (searched docs 05 and 10) [R] doc 17 §9, doc 05 §41.3 PCBWorld (679 real boards, its published baselines in doc 10 §3) has a fetch script entry but was never fetched or run: bench/data has no pcbworld [R] scripts/fetch_fixtures.sh, ls bench/data, doc 10 Release v0.9.0 has one asset, the promo video. There is no binary and no plugin archive to download; building needs GCC 15 (and CUDA 12.x for the GPU) [R] gh release view v0.9.0 The KiCad plugin was driven in a running KiCad 10.0.6 GUI (Xvfb, one undo step); not checked: that KiCad builds the plugin's virtual environment and shows its button [R] doc 08, morning report 2026-10-07 A long-running tracemakerd is not built; each plugin run starts the engine afresh [R] doc 08 Viewer: control channel (pause, step, seek), minimap, WebGPU backend, TLS not built [R] doc 09 Set-up takes 135 s on LeeChee (obstacle queries); GPU DRC broad-phase and GPU global routing not built, measured not to pay [R] doc 05 §19, D55, D56 #24's three options are off by default; --si-rules is not the best measured combination, and the effect was measured with one seed on four boards, where run-to-run noise is as large as some differences [R] dev/morning-report-2026-10-15.md

docs.title: 3. What the field is doing
docs.text:
• KiCad 10 (released 2026-03-20) [W: kicad.org release post; KiCad source documentation]. Track tuning was rebuilt: time-domain constraints (delay, not only length), tuning profiles with per-layer track width and differential gap, per-layer propagation delay, via delay overrides, a target impedance computed from the stackup, assigned to net classes; a graphical custom-rule editor; PCB design blocks (reusable layout modules); pin and gate swap with forward and back annotation (unconstrained; a constrained system "may come in future versions"); jumpers (same net, no ratsnest); inner-layer footprint graphics and keep-outs; suggested fixes for DRC errors; importers for Allegro and PADS. A .kicad_pro already has a tuning_profiles block (empty in the KiCad demos in bench/data) and the rule severities missing_tuning_profile and tuning_profile_track_geometries [R]; the engine reads neither [R: no match in src/].
  • KiCad IPC API [W]: in KiCad 9 and 10 it talks to a running GUI only; headless use, plotting and export arrive with KiCad 11; KiCad 11 stops bundling Python, so plugins move to their own interpreter. Third-party reports of editing a board through create_items and push_commit match what the plugin does [R].
  • Commercial AI layout [W, self-reported]: Quilter targets complex DDR / PCIe / RF boards and returns several candidate layouts with a scorecard; DeepPCB presents learned global routing; Flux's auto-layout runs after the engineer has routed differential pairs, impedance- controlled lines and high-speed interfaces by hand. Common ground in how they sell: critical interfaces are where trust is lost, and buyers ask whether they can see why the tool did what it did and audit constraints and violations quickly.
  • Research [W: abstract only]: PCBWorld (July 2026; open environment on KiCad, 679 real boards, eight engine-checked metrics) reports that tool-using agents beat grid-action RL and open-loop LLMs, that an RL policy trained on synthetic boards approaches rule-based routers on real ones, and that learning-based methods are not yet competitive with rule-based routers. OmniRouting (August 2026) is a benchmark for LLMs and multimodal models on routing.
  • Pin swapping [W: Altium, Siemens, Cadence material]: described as a way to cut crossovers and layers, needs an up-front definition of which pins may swap, and must be passed back to the schematic. I found no independent measurement of the gain, and one trade article warns that a swap that looks harmless can break FPGA timing.

What this says for TraceMaker: its differentiators (determinism, exact checks, transactions, KiCad as judge, the stuck report, the audit reports) fit "auditable". The field's open ground is high-speed interfaces done with proof; KiCad 10 just made the data for that (per-layer geometry and delay) a native project setting that TraceMaker does not yet read.

docs.title: 4. Candidates
docs.text: Effort: S one session, M two to three, L four or more [A]. Every candidate keeps the project rules (determinism, exact check, a reference path for every accelerated path, off by default until measured, results in bench/records/).

docs.title: Group A — Measure on the field's data, and be installable
docs.text: # Candidate Why (evidence) Effort Gate A1 PCBWorld-Bench run. Fetch the set, route all 679 boards in the standard configuration, classify failures, compare with its published baselines (read the paper first) The newest public benchmark of real KiCad boards; never run [R]; PCBench's weakness (default-rule judge, no stackups) makes a second, independent set worth having S A report with clean pass and completion per board class beside the published baselines, failure classes counted, and the boards TraceMaker loses to a baseline listed. No "better than" claim until the baselines' own settings are matched A2 Prebuilt releases. CI builds a CPU-only Linux x86_64 tarball and the KiCad plugin archive (PCM format) on a tag and attaches both; macOS arm64 if the CI runner allows Release v0.9.0 has no binary [R]; GCC 15 is a high bar for the people the plugin is for S–M On a machine with no compiler: download, install the plugin archive, route plane_smd in under five minutes; a CI job does the same on a clean container A3 A modern-boards set with stackups and real interfaces (USB, DDR, PCIe, RF), 10 to 30 open-hardware boards with licences that allow storing them or a fetch script that pins commits The SI features (D114–D117, impedance classes) are unmeasurable on PCBench [R]; repository boards (StickHub, CM5 Minima, a Jetson carrier) are few M Set committed as a manifest; every SI option run on it with the quick-tier rules (options off byte-identical) A4 Version-drift watch. A scheduled job runs the DRC parity corpus and the round-trip test against the newest kicad/kicad container, and against the KiCad 11 nightly when one exists KiCad changes rule semantics between point releases (D80 followed 10.0.3) and 11 changes the plugin runtime [W] S A failing parity run opens an issue with the first divergent board A5 Settle #24 with data. Five seeds, twelve plane boards; choose the defaults of --si-rules from the result (the best measured combination is not what --si-rules is today) The effect was measured with one seed and noise matches some differences [R] S A table with spread per option; --si-rules equals the combination that wins, or the doc says why not

docs.title: Group B — High-speed done with proof (builds on D114–D117 and KiCad 10)
docs.text: # Candidate Why Effort Gate B1 Read KiCad 10 tuning profiles. Parse tuning_profiles and the net-class assignment; give the router per-layer track width and pair gap (microstrip on the outer layers, stripline inside), use KiCad's via and per-layer delays in the skew and length rules instead of the engine's own table (src/crules/impedance_rules.hpp), and match KiCad's tuning_profile_track_geometries rule in the DRC Closes a gap the docs already name (one width per net) [R] and a KiCad 10 setting the engine ignores [R]. Format must be taken from a populated KiCad 10 project: the demos' list is empty M Boards with profiles route with each layer's profile width; kicad-cli with tuning_profile_track_geometries enabled adds 0 errors; DRC parity corpus extended with profile boards; options off byte-identical B2 Time-domain matching. Length and skew groups in picoseconds with per-layer and via delays (B1's data), meander tuning to a target delay, a check against KiCad's own length / skew rules KiCad 10 headline feature [W]; DDR byte lanes and pairs are where the commercial tools aim [W]; the DRC already reads ps as a unit [R: rule_engine.cpp] M A DDR-style generated fixture and two real boards within tolerance by KiCad's DRC, in delay, not only length B3 Close the audit loop. Run the return-path stitching pass (--stitch-vias return) inside --si-rules, re-audit, and report unstitched layer changes and remaining detours as warnings with the net and the place The audit (§42) and the stitch pass (§39.3) exist but are two commands; the issue's "hooks left" were exactly this [R]. Needs a reference plane net on two layers S–M On the four plane boards (and A3), unstitched layer changes of critical nets fall, 0 added DRC errors, quick/mid/planes unchanged with options off B4 Parallel-run limits (a geometric 3W / parallel-length proxy, report and cost, no simulation) Crosstalk is the next thing after splits and vias on JLCPCB's list in spirit; but no evidence of demand in the repository, and doc 01 excludes simulation M Do not start without A3's boards showing parallel runs that matter. Listed so the question is asked

docs.title: Group C — Routing and placement capability
docs.text: # Candidate Why Effort Gate C1 --relax and --txn on PCBench B–D failures. Run the failing boards of tiers B, C, D with --relax (and transactions), count the boards that complete --relax finished srj20 boards nothing else did; no measurement on the tiers found [R]. The cheapest possible capability gain S Boards gained and boards lost at equal work, clean by KiCad's DRC; if it gains, a portfolio variant, else a recorded negative C2 Pin and gate swap: feasibility experiment first. Fixtures where swaps are legal by construction (identical gates of a multi-unit part, resistor-network pins, a connector-to-MCU bus on interchangeable GPIO) and a "free assignment" oracle: measure routed count, vias and layers with and without the freedom. Build the pass only if the gain is large Vendors claim fewer crossings and layers; no independent number found [W]. KiCad 10 now applies swaps with annotation [W]. Wrong swaps break designs, so the eligibility list must be explicit (a file or the library), never guessed Experiment S, pass L Experiment: a table of routed / vias / layers with and without the oracle on at least ten boards. Build only if a median gain is clear; the pass writes swaps as a proposal file and applies them only when asked C3 Pours and a layer-count advisor. Create a ground (or power) pour on a free inner or back layer when a board has none; try 2, 4 and 6 layers and report the least that completes doc 05 §18 says creating pours is "a possible feature (not built); it would close a few boards, not most" [R]; a layer count is a direct cost M On PCBench boards with no zones, the count completed with a generated pour vs without, DRC clean; the advisor's answer matches a brute-force run C4 Repeated-channel replication. Detect identical sub-circuits (graph isomorphism on the netlist, same footprints), route one, replicate its copper by transform, route the rest Audio mixers, 3-phase drives, LED and ADC channels are common [A]; KiCad's multichannel tools and design blocks do it by hand [W]; multichannel_mixer is a fixture [R] L A research spike first: how many fixture boards contain a repeated block at all. Build only if several do C5 Fan-out at packages (the failure class). After C1, classify the dense-package failures of tiers B–D by cause (pin boxed in, via sites, layer count) and fix the largest class The M9 gate is unmet at 41 %, and doc 05 says what fails is fan-out [R]. Without the classification the fix is a guess Classification S, fix L A table of failures by cause; the fix is chosen from it C6 Pair tuning together (both halves meandering, length-match of a pair to a bus), pairs ending on routed copper doc 05 §15 lists both as not built [R]; the "crossovers for swapped pairs" item of the untracked FEATURES.md is partly done (pair twists, §15) M Pair fixtures: coupled share and skew within the limit with the pair tuned as one C7 Large-board set-up time (135 s on LeeChee): profile the obstacle queries, build the index once Slow set-up is a blocker for the dense 8–12 layer boards N4 names [R] M Same output bytes, set-up time down by a stated factor on the largest five boards

docs.title: Group D — Interaction, agents, explanation
docs.text: # Candidate Why Effort Gate D1 Assistive use inside KiCad. Route the selected nets or the area under a rectangle from the plugin, with a warm engine (tracemakerd) that keeps the board and caches Doc 01 says users finish by hand in pcbnew; the plugin starts the engine afresh each run [R]; KiCad 11's headless IPC [W] would let it run unattended M–L A single-net route from the plugin within a stated latency on multichannel_mixer; still one undo step D2 Engine-grounded agent API (a tool interface, such as an MCP server, over the transactions: route a connection, rip a net, check, score, undo; every commit still passes the exact check) PCBWorld's result is that agents with engine feedback beat open-loop and grid RL [W]; M16 found passive hints gain nothing [R], so the active version is the open question M for the interface, value unknown Stop rule agreed in advance: an agent loop (the rule-based advisor as the baseline agent) must route more than the plain run at the same compute on a held-out half; if not, the interface is kept as a library and nothing more is built D3 A run report for designers. One HTML / markdown file: what was routed, what is open and why (stuck report), which rules were read and which were not, the SI audit, the DRC comparison, the options used and the seed "See why and audit quickly" is how buyers judge these tools [W, self-reported]; the pieces exist as separate outputs [R] S–M A report from route --report FILE for the four plane boards, every number traceable to a JSON field; reviewed by someone who did not write it D4 Viewer control channel: pause, step, seek on a recording, click a net to route it first, minimap Not built [R]; value is explanation and debugging more than routing quality M Seeking in a recording within one second on the largest log D5 Leftovers from #37 / #38: --view-token / --view-insecure in the plugin and Python module, TLS (or a documented tunnel recipe), --si-rules map ignoring the antipads of vias the route adds Named limits in the issue comments [R] S The plugin and module accept the flags; the antipad limit has a test

docs.title: 5. Order (after the answers of §7)
docs.text:
The audience is hobbyists first, with high-speed work limited to the Kookabus boards; KiCad 11 support is wanted; a proposal-only pin swap is acceptable; the agent interface is wanted, with the stop rule of D2. That puts install and measurement first, then the session server that the agent interface and the KiCad assistant share, then KiCad 11 (due about February 2027 [W]), then the hobbyist wins, and the high-speed work last and only as far as the Kookabus boards need it.

Milestone Candidates Why here M17 — Installable and measured A2 prebuilt releases and plugin archive; A1 PCBWorld-Bench run; C1 --relax/--txn on the PCBench B–D failures Hobbyists cannot use what they cannot install; the other two answer, cheaply, how TraceMaker does on boards nobody tuned it on, and whether a known capability is a free gain M18 — Session server and agent interface D2 (the agent API) on top of a long-running board session (tracemakerd, the core of D1) Asked for. One session process serves two users: an agent that routes connection by connection, and the KiCad plugin that routes the selected nets without restarting the engine. The stop rule of D2 decides whether anything beyond the interface is built M19 — KiCad 11 readiness A4 made a milestone: file format, DRC parity and plugin for 11 KiCad 11 is expected about February 2027 [W]: headless IPC (kicad-cli api-server), plotting and export through the API, no bundled Python. No official file-format change list was found [W], so the first task is the watch job, the second is reading a release candidate when one exists M20 — Hobbyist wins C3 pours and a layer-count advisor; D3 run report; C2's experiment and a proposal-only pin swap; C5's classification Two-layer and four-layer boards are the common case; the layer count is a direct cost; a report makes a run auditable M21 — High speed for the Kookabus boards A3 reduced to the Kookabus boards; B1 tuning profiles; B2 time-domain matching; B3 the audit loop; A5 Only as far as those boards need. The files must be found first (§7)

C6, C7, C4 and B4 wait for a board that needs them.

docs.title: 6. Considered and not recommended now
docs.text:
• A learned or RL router. PCBWorld's authors say learning-based methods are not yet competitive with rule-based routers [W], and M12 measured that learned ordering and congestion models would learn little here (doc 05 §25) [R].
  • GPU global routing / GPU DRC broad-phase. Measured to not pay (D55, D56) [R].
  • Signal-integrity simulation. A non-goal (doc 01). The useful, cheaper form is to export what an external field solver needs (stackup, geometry), not to build one.
  • A gridless tile-plane arm. Its measured upper bound is a few connections on the boards tried (doc 05 §25) [R].
  • Rigid-flex. No demand in the repository or the sources read [A].
  • A hosted service. The determinism and "your board never leaves the machine" are strengths; nothing here argues for it [A].

docs.title: 7. Decisions (2026-10-15)
docs.text: Question Answer Effect Who is it for? Hobbyists mostly; some high-speed users, "just the Kookabus boards" Install, assistance and the layer count come before signal integrity; A3 shrinks to the Kookabus boards and B1–B3 are scoped to them Boards you may keep The Kookabus boards Open: I found no Kookabus KiCad files on this machine (~/kookabus-render holds renders and promo tooling, ~/promo_render the promo videos). Where are the .kicad_pcb files, and may they go in the repository (or a fetch script)? KiCad versions Support KiCad 11 M19; the version-drift watch (A4) starts first Pin swap A proposal-only pass is acceptable C2: a proposal file for review; the pass never writes swaps into a board. The feasibility experiment still comes before the pass Agent interface Do it M18 with the stop rule of D2: if an agent loop does not route more than the plain run at the same compute on a held-out half, the interface stays a library and nothing more is built

docs.title: 8. What could make this plan wrong
docs.text:
• B1 leans on KiCad 10 adoption: if the Kookabus boards (and hobbyists) do not define tuning profiles, B1 matters little. A3 will show it, and M21 is last for that reason.
  • PCBWorld's boards may be mostly simple, so A1 could look good and teach little; the failure classification is the useful output, not the percentage.
  • C1 may find nothing: --relax may need the breakout structure to help. A recorded negative still removes a guess.
  • Vendor comparisons are self-reported; the pull toward "AI layout" features may be marketing rather than need.
  • All effort figures are guesses from past sessions.

docs.title: 9. D3 built: the run report (2026-10-24)
docs.text:
route --report FILE writes one HTML (or Markdown) file per run, rendered from the route summary alone, so every number in it is a JSON field (decision D136, how-to Read a run report). It covers the candidate's list: what was routed; what is open and why (the stuck report of doc 17 §3 for the final result, with what each cause means, cut proofs, pins that cannot escape their package, and the items the refilled board leaves unconnected); the rules read and not read; the SI audit (critical nets, pairs, buses, return paths); the DRC of the board before and after (TraceMaker's DRC, zones refilled); the options as given and the seed. tracemaker report renders it again from a saved summary.

Gate, as far as it goes (bench/records/m20-run-report): reports for all eight plane-tier boards, --soft-zones --si-rules, 3 M work. No routing error added on any board; the unconnected count after the refill equals the report's own DRC count on every board. A unit test checks every value of the HTML against its JSON pointer and that the renderer's own words hold no number. The extra work after the route took 0.1 to 2.1 s per board. Options off, the quick tier is byte-identical to main (30/30).

Not met yet: the review by someone who did not write it. interf_u, which on 2026-10-24 spent more than 20 minutes on one core after its portfolio, finished in 128 s on 2026-10-27 after D137's GPU back-off (the stall was the GPU fallback cliff), and RoyalBlue54L-Feather was re-run under --time 3600 (72 s, not time-limited). Found on the way: under load the default 120 s time limit, not the work budget, ended some runs, and their results moved between runs; the summary now says so (time_limited) and the report warns.

docs.title: 10. C3 built: generated pours and the layer-count advisor (2026-10-27)
docs.text:
route --pour auto|NET@LAYER adds a ground (or named) pour to a board without zones and routes with soft zones; route --copper-layers N and tracemaker layers change the copper layer count; route --try-layers 2,4,6 routes each count, fewest first, and writes the first that completes (doc 05 §53, decision D138, records in bench/records/m20-c3).

Gate: the advisor's answer equals a brute-force run (each count converted, routed and judged by KiCad) on 28 of 28 board-and-option pairs (14 two-layer boards, with and without a pour): met. Boards completed with a generated pour against without: 0 against 0 on the 33 non-clean tier B to D boards at their own layer counts (open connections after the refill 1,368 → 1,290), and 1 against 1 at 4 layers, 2 against 1 at 6 on the 14. The candidate's estimate holds: a pour closes few boards. On two layers the plane is cut up by the tracks that share its layer; the pour's thermal spokes, KiCad's default, were starved on 22 boards, so the pour connects pads solid.

docs.title: 11. C2 measured: pin swap is not worth a pass (2026-10-27)
docs.text:
bench/pin_swap.py gave each board an oracle's freedom: connector signal pins and resistor-array resistors taken as swappable by construction, the nets assigned to them by a minimum-cost assignment of pad-to-net distance, the board routed as designed and as swapped at the same work and judged by KiCad (doc 05 §56, decision D141, records in bench/records/m20-c2).

Gate (a table on at least ten boards): 30 boards. On the 20 failing tier B-D boards with a group, open connections 982 → 978 (five boards better, five worse), vias −3 %, length −1 %, none clean either way; on the 10 quick boards with one, 27 → 26 open and 7 → 6 clean. The median gain is zero, so the proposal-only pass is not built and C2 is closed. The oracle is an upper bound: a real design can swap fewer pins.

docs.title: 12. M19 started: the KiCad drift job (2026-10-27)
docs.text: scripts/kicad_drift.py and the weekly workflow kicad-drift.yml (decision D142, records in bench/records/m19-drift): the newest kicad/kicad release, and the newest release candidate when it is newer, upgrades four boards to its own format; this build must re-write them byte for byte, match kicad-cli's DRC counts on the routing-relevant types, and write a routed copy kicad-cli finds no new error type in. 4 of 4 pass on KiCad 10.0.6, 10.0.7 (released 2026-10-18) and the image tagged nightly, which turned out to be a 10.0 release candidate from February, so the job reads the version tags instead of trusting that tag. No KiCad 11 release candidate exists yet; the format, DRC and plugin work of M19 waits for one, and the job will check it the week it appears.

docs.title: 13. C5 classified and fixed: strict searches from the crowded end (2026-10-27)
docs.text:
tracemaker causes routes each open connection of a routed board again alone, with other nets' copper removed near its ends, away from them or everywhere, and names the first change that lets it route (doc 05 §55, decision D143, records in bench/records/m20-c5). On the 33 failing tier B-D boards (1,320 open on the board as it is): other nets' copper passing through a pin's fan-out region 444, the package's own fan-out 335, a channel away from the pins 259, no path even alone 182, both 51, pins that cannot leave their package 49; 684 of them at dense packages. Two more layers close 124.

The largest class is near the pins, and the work profile says why it is not repaired: 17 boards spend their whole budget in failed strict searches that flood their window before finding the target boxed in, and never negotiate. Starting each strict search from the more crowded end proves a boxed-in pin at once. In four of the portfolio's eight variants (all eight lost two clean boards), by default: open connections on the 33 boards 1,383 → 1,220 (KiCad 1,368 → 1,204; 18 boards better, 6 worse; one completes); the other sets in the table of doc 05 §55. Gate (a table of failures by cause; the fix chosen from it): met.

docs.title: 14. B3 built: --si-rules closes the audit loop (2026-10-27)
docs.text:
With --si-rules, the reference-return audit runs on the critical nets after routing; every layer change it finds with the same plane net on both sides and no via of it within 5 mm gets a return-path stitching via (the stitching pass of doc 05 §39.3, as a transaction), the audit runs again, and the report names each unstitched change and each detour over 2 mm with its place (--no-si-stitch turns the stitching off; doc 05 §57, decision D144, records in bench/records/m21-b3).

Gate (doc 18 §4 B3): on the plane boards unstitched layer changes of critical nets fall, 0 added DRC errors, quick/mid/planes unchanged with the options off. Not met on the plane tier, because there is nothing to fix there. Under --si-rules routing, one change stays without a return via in every seed (StickHub, with no plane copper on one side, which a via cannot fix). The other option sets leave 2 to 7, so the --si-rules routing already avoids them (bench/records/m21-a5). The pass is shown working on a constructed board (doc 05 §57), and no KiCad error was added in any run. A3's modern-boards set does not exist yet (the Kookabus files are still missing).

docs.title: 15. B1 built: KiCad 10 tuning profiles (2026-10-28)
docs.text:
The project reader reads KiCad 10's tuning profiles and compiles KiCad's implicit width and pair-gap rules, so the engine's DRC judges profiled tracks as KiCad does. Single-ended profiles are routed at their widest width and narrowed afterwards to each layer's width. Differential profiles keep their pairs on the layers that share one width and gap (doc 05 §58, decision D145, records in bench/records/m21-b1).

KiCad 10.0.6 was measured where its behaviour and its source disagree, and the engine follows the behaviour:

  • an ignored profile rule still decides the width check;
  • hasExactNetclass never matches in a user's rule;
  • the coupled clearance at the profile's gap covers tracks, not pads.

The DRC parity corpus has four new cases, and all 220 match KiCad.

Gate (doc 18 §4 B1):

  • Boards with profiles route with each layer's profile width: met for single-ended profiles, and for pairs on the layers they keep.
  • kicad-cli with tuning_profile_track_geometries enabled adds 0 errors: met on the two boards given profiles. On RoyalBlue, routing with the single-ended profile alone is the same as without one. The pair profile costs 5 of 147 connections.
  • Parity corpus extended: met.
  • Options off byte-identical: the quick tier at the end of the night (morning report).

No real board with profiles exists in the fixtures; the delays are left to B2.

docs.title: 16. A5 settled: --si-rules keeps critical-first (2026-10-28)
docs.text: Five seeds of #24's options on the plane tier (decision D146, records in bench/records/m21-a5). No critical-net measure moves with the seed. --critical-first routes 27 of 28 critical nets against 23 to 25 without it, including RoyalBlue's crystal net and debugger USB pair, at 6 connections of the other nets. The via and split costs alone save a few vias and crossings on common nets, and nothing once critical-first is on. --si-rules keeps all three, and defaults stay off. Gate (settle the defaults on five seeds): met.

docs.title: 17. B2 built: time-domain matching (2026-10-28)
docs.text:
The engine measures a net's length and delay as KiCad 10.0.6 does, quirks included, and checks length and skew rules in ps against the delay. The router tunes nets into ps windows and skew groups, weighting meanders by each layer's delay per mm. The DRC now also has KiCad's diff-pair coupling test, and the router avoids coupling-gap errors (doc 05 §59, decisions D147 and D148, records in bench/records/m21-b2).

Checking B2 against KiCad showed that B1's fixtures were judged by a KiCad that read no profile, because their net settings were at schema 4. Rejudged (doc 05 §58), B1 needed profile inheritance from Default, the pair width from a single-ended profile, and no neck-down on profiled nets. A single-ended profile on Default costs RoyalBlue 23 of 147 connections. The pair profile left 5 coupling-gap errors at its USB-C connector. The router now avoids them (D148) and still routes 104 of 147 connections.

Gate (doc 18 §4 B2):

  • A DDR-style generated fixture within tolerance by KiCad's DRC, in delay: met. ddr8's 20 window and skew errors are now 0, and the delay_tuning test checks this.
  • Two real boards within tolerance in delay: met on interf_u (four memory-data lanes: 7 errors before, 0 after) and RoyalBlue (the debugger USB pair: 1 before, 0 after), both given profiles and rules by make_fixtures.py, at the same routed counts. No fixture board has delay rules of its own.
  • The measurement itself: KiCad's QA board to 0.01 ps; 325 of 329 nets on four demo boards to under 1 µm. Four branched power nets differ, where 10.0.6 depends on pointer order.

docs.title: 19 — A board session and an agent interface (M18)
docs.text:
Status: Partly built

Part of this page describes code that exists; the rest is a plan. The page says which is which.

Part of the TraceMaker plan. Start at ../PLAN.md. Written 2026-10-15. Milestone M18 (11-roadmap.md), candidate D2 of 18-next-features.md. Decision D119. Status: stage A (session, tools, two transports) and stage B (evaluation harness, scripted baseline agent) are what this note specifies; §9 says what is built and what was measured.

docs.title: 1. What it is, and how it differs from the advisor
docs.text:
Doc 17 lets the engine consult an advisor: the plain route runs, a stuck report goes out, an advice file comes back, the route runs again. The agent never sees a board, only a report, and it acts once. Its measured result is that hints derived by a rule gain nothing over the same compute without hints (doc 17 §8.1), and a model's hints have not been measured.

This document is the other direction: a session in which an agent drives the engine. The agent lists the open connections, asks the engine to route some nets with some hints, looks at what happened, rips a net, goes back to an earlier state, tries something else, and saves. The engine stays what it is: every copper item passes the exact check, nothing the agent says contains copper or changes a rule, every call is a transaction that is kept or not, and the whole session replays to the same bytes. PCBWorld (July 2026) reports that agents with engine feedback beat open-loop and grid-action baselines [W, abstract]; whether one can beat TraceMaker's own portfolio at equal compute is the question this milestone answers, with the stop rule of §7.

The same session process is the core of the KiCad assistant (M18's second half, candidate D1): a plugin that routes the selected nets without starting the engine afresh. Only the first half is specified here.

docs.title: 2. The rules, applied
docs.text: Rule How the session keeps it 1 Correctness Copper enters the session only from the router, which checks every segment and via exactly before it commits. check runs the DRC on the session's board; save reports the errors it added 2 Determinism A call's result depends on the board, the session's state, the call's arguments and the seed only. Router work is a count (work), never a wall time. The log of calls replays to the same board bytes (tested) 3 Reference path route over all nets with the defaults equals route --variants V of the command line on the same board and options (tested): the session is a second front door to the same code 4 Transactions A route is kept only if it routes something and, with verify: "refuse" (the default), adds no DRC error relative to the state it starts from; otherwise the state is unchanged and the result says why. report keeps it and names the added errors, off skips the check. undo, restore and history go back to any state 5 Budgets Every route takes a work budget in search steps (expansions plus flood cells). The router's budget stops new searches from starting; the search in progress and the clean-up after the last one finish, so a call can pass it. The session counts what was really spent (work_used) and refuses the next call when --work-limit is spent. The limit is soft, and a call runs with the work it asks for (so a first call is the command line's): an agent that must stay under the limit sizes work from board_info's work_left 6 Locked and unreadable Session copper is locked inside the session: later calls cannot rip it except through rip_net, and rip_net removes session copper only. The board's own tracks and vias are never removed. Rules that could not be read keep the warnings the engine gives 7 Events --view streams the router's events to the viewer, so a person can watch the agent work 8 KiCad files save re-reads the input file and adds the session's copper through the same editor route uses; everything else is byte for byte

docs.title: 3. Safety (the agent is not trusted, and neither is the board)
docs.text:
• Typed arguments. Every tool has a schema; an unknown key, a wrong type or a value out of range is an error naming the tool and the key, as for advice files (doc 17 §4). hints are an advice file, parsed and checked by the same code.
  • No paths from the agent, no commands. save writes to the file named when the session was started (--out) and nowhere else. There is no tool that runs a program or reads a file.
  • Names are data. Net names, references and layer names come from the board and may say anything. They appear only as JSON string values, never in the tool descriptions or in error templates, and the server's instructions tell the agent so (doc 17 §6 wording).
  • Caps. At most 512 open connections listed per call, 64 nets per route, work at most 50 M per call (times up to 8 variants), 256 states kept, a request line of at most 1 MB. Start an unattended agent with --work-limit: without it nothing but the per-call caps bounds what an agent can spend.
  • No redaction in the session. An agent that drives it sees the board's names. Where names must not leave the machine, the advisor protocol's --advisor-redact (doc 17 §3) is the tool; a redacted session would need aliases in every result and is not built.
  • No network. The server speaks over standard input and output only. A model, a key or a network stays in the agent's own process.

docs.title: 4. The tools
docs.text:
Millimetres and the board file's axes; connections are named REF.PIN, as in doc 17 (priority). Every result is a JSON object; an error is {"error": {"code", "message"}} with the code one of bad_argument, unknown_name, limit, not_allowed, failed.

Tool Arguments Result board_info none board name, copper layers, counts (parts, pads, nets, tracks and vias of the board and of the session), open connections, state id, work used and left, rules summary (clearance, track width, via) and the warnings from reading the rules open_connections net (name, optional), limit, soft_zones the connections still open in the current state: net, a, b (REF.PIN, or zone for a plane), length_mm (not for a plane), and, if a route has tried them, reason, why, rips, fails, blockers. soft_zones plans the plane connections too (default: on once a route with soft zones was kept) route nets (names; default: every net with an open connection), work (default 2 M, at most 50 M), variants (1 to 8, default 1), seed, hints (an advice object: first_nets, priority, layers, regions), options (a whitelist of booleans: soft_zones, via_in_pad, diff_pairs, vias_off_pads, escape_plan), verify (refuse by default, report, off), commit (default true) committed, reason (when not), state, connections and routed and open_after (for the nets this call named), open_total (the board's), the new copper per net (tracks, vias, length), added_errors (DRC types, relative to the state the call started from), the connections still open with reason, why, tried (a search ran or the pin was ruled out; false: never attempted), rips, fails, blockers, and work (used, total_used, left). A call can spend more than work (proofs of boxed-in pins and the clean-up count on top; observed up to 1.6 times with one router) rip_net net the session copper of that net removed (a new state); how many tracks and vias; refuses a net with none check full (default true), refill unconnected items and DRC errors by type, the types and counts the session added relative to the input board, and for those up to five examples each (items with positions: which net, where) that the input board does not have. refill judges with the zones refilled, as kicad-cli --refill-zones does (default: on once a route with soft zones was kept; a route with soft zones is verified refilled, because the router counts on the refill) stuck_report redact doc 17's report for the last route (reasons, crowding, parts at the open ends, advice_schema) inspect_pad pad (REF.PIN), radius_mm (0.1 to 10, default 1.5) read-only: the pad (net, position, layers, size, distance to the box of the outline), the open connections that end on it with the last route's reason and blockers, the other pads within the radius (at most 40, nearest first), and the copper within it (the board's and the session's, per net and layer, nearest first, at most 30 rows; within_pad_area marks another net's copper that lies in the pad's own area) inspect_net net read-only: its pads (at most 60), the board's and the session's tracks and vias on it, the session's length per layer, the open connections, the box it spans, and its class width and clearance history none the states: id, the call that made it, routed connections, vias, copper length undo / restore none / state the session goes back one state / to that state (states stay; a new change after a restore starts a new branch) save refill writes the board to --out (the result does not name the path: a replay may write elsewhere); returns counts and the DRC types added

A route with commit: false is a dry run: the result is reported and the state is unchanged.

hints apply to this call's run itself, not to extra portfolio variants: in a session the agent decides, sees the result and can undo, so the "advised copies cannot be worse" guard of doc 17 §4 is not needed; the transaction rule above takes its place.

docs.title: 5. Session state and the log
docs.text:
State = the input board, plus a list of session copper (tracks and vias, in commit order), plus the open-connection reasons of the last route. A state is immutable; each change makes a new one. A router run gets the board with the session copper added and marked locked. The first listing of the open connections of a state costs one router set-up (the planner needs the obstacle model); it is cached per state. A long-running daemon that keeps the set-up between calls is the other half of M18 and is not built.

The log is a JSON-lines file (--log FILE): per call, the tool, the arguments, a digest of the result and the state's digest (FNV-1a 64 of the session copper in canonical order: a digest to compare a session with its replay, not a cryptographic hash). tracemaker session --replay LOG BOARD --out FILE runs the calls again and stops at the first digest that differs. Replay is the determinism test, and it is how a session that went well is reproduced without an agent.

docs.title: 6. Transports
docs.text:
One Session::call(tool, args) serves both, so they cannot differ.

  • MCP over standard input and output (tracemaker session BOARD --out FILE): JSON-RPC 2.0 with initialize, tools/list, tools/call and the notifications/initialized notification, protocol revision 2024-11-05 or the client's, instructions as in §3. Any MCP client can be the agent (a coding agent, an application). To attach it to Claude Code, for example: claude mcp add tracemaker -- /path/to/tracemaker session /path/to/board.kicad_pcb --out /path/to/routed.kicad_pcb (other clients take the same command and arguments in their MCP server configuration). --log FILE records the session for --replay, and --view lets a person watch the agent route in the browser viewer. The server speaks on standard input and output only; the router's own text goes to standard error. An agent that has a shell tool but no MCP client can drive a session with agents/relay.py: start NAME BOARD OUT holds a session under a small daemon, call NAME TOOL '{...}' sends one tool call and prints the answer (result NAME fetches an answer that took longer than --wait), stop NAME ends it. Every request and answer is also appended to the session folder's transcript.jsonl, which bench/agent_score.py reads to score the board the agent saved.
  • JSON lines (--jsonl): one request {"tool", "args"} per line, one response per line. For scripts, tests and the evaluation harness.

docs.title: 7. The evaluation and its stop rule
docs.text:
Question. Does an agent that drives the session route more connections than the same compute spent without an agent?

Compute. Search expansions plus flood cells over all routers of all calls: the summary's work_all_variants.total for a route run, work_used for a session. The agent's own thinking is not routing work and is not counted, as the advisor's wall time is not (doc 17 §4).

Arms (bench/agent_eval.py), each scored the same way: connections routed = unconnected items of the input board minus those of the written board, judged by tracemaker drc beside the input's project files; an arm that adds a DRC error is invalid for that board.

  1. plain: route --work W --variants V (W = 20 M, V = 8: doc 17 §8.1's plain arm).
  2. control: route --work W --variants V+4. More compute with no agent, and the equal-compute reference: its measured work is the agent's --work-limit.
  3. agent: a program that drives tracemaker session with that limit. Its first call is the plain arm (so it cannot do worse than arm 1 by construction); the rest of the compute is the agent's to spend.

Boards. bench/sets/srj20-m15fail4.txt (16 srj20 boards still open after the 70 M run of M15, doc 17 §8.1): an even half to tune an agent on and an odd half held out, looked at once when the agent is final. The same boards and arms as doc 17 §8.1, so the plain and control columns must reproduce its totals (430 and 431 on the even half, 439 and 450 on the odd half); if they do not, the arms were not run the same way and nothing else is read.

Stop rule (decided in advance, D118/D119). The interface is worth building on for agents only if an agent arm routes more connections than the control (arm 2) on the held-out half, summed over the half and not worse on most boards. If neither the scripted agent of stage B nor a model-driven one does, the session stays a library (it is still the core of the KiCad assistant) and nothing more is built for agents. The scripted agent is a baseline, not the test of a model: a negative result for it says that these rules do not beat seeds, not that a model cannot.

docs.title: 8. What is deliberately not here
docs.text:
• No tool that places copper by coordinates. An agent that wants a route in a place says it through hints (a region, a layer cost, an order), and the engine finds the copper. A propose_path tool (a polyline the router takes as a guide, RouterOptions::guides, doc 16 F1) is the next step if §7's result is good, and is not built before.
  • No placement moves (doc 17 §9, stage 4).
  • No critical_first, relax or other portfolio options among the route options: the whitelist is small on purpose, and grows when an agent needs one.
  • No model, key or network in the engine (D109).
  • No multi-board or multi-user server. One session is one board, one agent.

docs.title: 9. Built and measured
docs.text: Records: bench/records/m18/.

docs.title: 9.1 Built
docs.text:
• src/session/ (session.{hpp,cpp}, transport.{hpp,cpp}): the ten tools of §4, the states, the log and its replay, MCP and JSON-lines transports; tracemaker session. One engine change: RouterOptions::plan_only (plan the connections and stop), used to list a state's open connections; off by default.
  • agents/session_client.py (a Python client), agents/repair_agent.py (the scripted baseline, two policies), bench/agent_eval.py (the three arms), bench/sets/srj20-agent-heldout.txt.
  • Tests: tests/test_session.cpp (12 cases, 176 assertions: listing and routing, equality with the plain router, rip/undo/restore, dry runs and refusals, hints, the work limit, save only to --out, replay and a changed log, thread-count independence, every listed tool dispatchable, both transports on bad requests), tests/integration/session_cli.py (the real binary over both transports, a net name that carries an instruction, replay to the same bytes, equality with route --variants 1). ASan + UBSan and TSan clean on the session tests; the CLI test also under ASan + UBSan.

docs.title: 9.2 The first call is the command line's
docs.text: route --work 20000000 --variants 8 --threads 8 and the session's first route with the same arguments on srj20 sample054 give 56 routed, 596 tracks, 154 vias and 69,573,838 work, both. The plain and control columns of the evaluation reproduce doc 17 §8.1's totals exactly (430 / 431 and 439 / 450).

docs.title: 9.3 The stop-rule test with a scripted agent: not met
docs.text:
Sixteen boards (the even and odd halves of srj20-m15fail4), connections routed, summed:

Arm Even half (489 open) Odd half (492 open, held out) plain, 8 variants 430 439 control, 12 variants (the agent's compute) 431 450 agent, policy tabu (each stuck connection once) 430 439 agent, policy persist (retries with other blockers and seeds, plateau moves kept) 430 not run (confirmed on a fresh set, below)

Policy tabu used 77 % of the control's work; none of its 43 repair rounds was kept. Policy persist used 95 % and kept 150 plateau rounds that never reduced the open connections. Neither routed one connection more than the plain run on any of these 16 boards. The control's gain on the odd half (+11) comes from the four extra seeds, which a repair of three stuck connections does not reproduce. Every unrouted connection on these boards is boxed_in (a ball fenced by its neighbours' copper), and the proof of it is the expensive part of a repair call (8.6 M flood cells against 0.85 M expansions in one case).

Because persist was designed after the tabu result on both halves, it was confirmed on 16 boards no agent was developed on (srj20-agent-heldout), run once:

Arm (16 held-out boards, 1,162 open at the start) Routed plain, 8 variants 960 control, 12 variants (the agent's compute) 968 agent, policy persist (95 % of the control's work) 967

Stop rule: not met, by one connection. A model-driven arm (§9.3.1) then tied the control. Exploratory reading by group: on the 8 boards where the plain run leaves only 3 to 6 connections open the agent gains nothing (429, plain 429, control 433); on the 8 where it leaves 22 on average it routes 538 against the control's 535 and the plain run's 531. Eight boards, one run: a lead, not a result. A repair loop earns something where there is something to repair, and the extra seeds of the control earn their gain where little is left. Whether a model does better than this loop is untested.

docs.title: 9.3.1 A model-driven arm
docs.text:
Four model agents (subagents, one brief, four boards each; the first call mandated to be the plain route; scored from the boards they saved, never from their own reports; two sessions replayed from their logs byte for byte) drove the same 16 boards through the tools of §4, inspect_pad and inspect_net included:

Arm (16 held-out boards, 1,162 open at the start) Routed plain, 8 variants 960 control, 12 variants (the agents' compute) 968 scripted agent, policy persist 967 model-driven agents (94 % of the control's work) 968

Stop rule: not met, by a tie (968 against 968). The model never routed less than the plain run, gained +8 over it, used 94 % of the allowance, was better than the control on 5 boards and worse on 6. It gained on boards where the scripted loop did not, and the loop gained where the model did not; one run each. The technique that worked was single-net: look at the stuck ball and its target pad with inspect_pad, remove the nets beside it, route the stuck net alone. The removed nets then mostly failed to return, so a cycle gained 0 or 1 and every board reached a plateau. It cost 615 k tokens for +8 connections; four more seeds give +8 for compute alone. So: with this router and these boards, an agent matches what extra seeds give and does not exceed it, and by D118 nothing more is built for agents until the router can tell an agent more than it does now (below). What the agents asked of the tools, and what was done, is in bench/records/m18/README.md.

docs.title: 9.4 What a session showed that the measurement did not
docs.text:
• The engine's DRC and KiCad disagreed on two boards of this set (sample031, sample191): the engine counted 3 added copper_edge_clearance errors where kicad-cli counted none. The router puts a track with its edge exactly on the centre line of an outline whose stroke is 0.05 mm and whose clearance rule is 0; check_edges (src/drc/drc.cpp) counted touching as a violation at zero clearance, KiCad does not for a straight track. Fixed afterwards (issue #42, D120: the edge threshold depends on the shape, frozen against KiCad in tests/integration/edge_touch); the numbers of this section were measured before the fix. It is why verify has the modes of §4 and why the agent's first call uses report; after it the engine and KiCad agree on copper_edge_clearance for the plain route of sample031, sample007, sample191 and sample039 (65, 72, 69 and 78; bench/records/issue42). The session's refuse mode was not re-run.
  • A model cannot choose blockers blind (this is why inspect_pad and inspect_net exist, §4). A session driven by hand on sample119 (bench/records/m18/README.md) swapped one stuck connection for another and never reduced the open count: the tools name nets and pads, and say nothing of what lies around a pad. And stuck_report after a route restricted to a few nets has no crowding (the other nets are locked copper, not routed copper of that run).
  • Listing the open connections costs a router set-up per state. Fine on these boards; on a large board it is the reason for the daemon.

docs.title: 9.5 Not built, and what follows
docs.text:
• What the agents asked for and the router cannot yet say: which end of a boxed-in connection is fenced and which lanes and via sites are free; a dry run that names the minimal set of nets to remove to free a pin; "stopped at net X" and a reason with blockers for every open connection of a multi-net call. These are router questions (escape analysis per pad, doc 05 §14), not session ones; they are the thing to build if agents are worth another try.
  • The daemon (tracemakerd) and the KiCad assistant that uses it (the other half of M18).
  • Redaction in the session, propose_path, placement moves (§8).

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Get TraceMaker running and route the example board that comes with it, in about five minutes with a download or fifteen with a build. Pick your platform:

Platform How Tested Linux x86_64, glibc 2.38 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04+, Debian 13, current Fedora) download a release yes: CI installs it in a clean container on every release Any Linux with GCC 13 or newer build from source Ubuntu 26.04 (what CI and development use) macOS 15 or 26 on Apple silicon build from source by a contributor (Chris Hemingway, M2, macOS 15): every test passes, results match Linux; not in CI Windows 10 or 11 the Linux download inside WSL2 not yet tried

No GPU, no CUDA and no KiCad are needed for any of them. A CUDA 12.x GPU on Linux makes routing faster and gives the same results (Use the GPUs).

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
Linux: downloadLinux: build from sourcemacOS (Apple silicon)Windows (WSL2)

Check your C library first: ldd --version must say 2.38 or newer (Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 are too old; build from source there).

curl -LO https://github.com/DingoOz/TraceMaker/releases/download/v0.12.1/tracemaker-0.12.1-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
tar xzf tracemaker-0.12.1-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
cd tracemaker-0.12.1-linux-x86_64
export PATH="$PWD/bin:$PATH"
EX=share/tracemaker/examples/plane_smd
tracemaker version

The releases page has newer versions when there are any; the commands are the same with the new number. The archive carries the programs, the live viewer, the example board and the agent skills, and needs nothing else installed.

Install the compiler and libraries. On Ubuntu or Debian:

sudo apt install g++-15 cmake ninja-build git python3 python3-yaml python3-dev \
    libboost-dev libboost-system-dev libeigen3-dev nlohmann-json3-dev libcli11-dev \
    libsqlite3-dev libzstd-dev catch2 pybind11-dev

(g++-13 or g++-14 in place of g++-15 if your release does not have it. Libraries that are missing are fetched and built with the project, which makes the first build slower.) Then:

git clone https://github.com/DingoOz/TraceMaker.git
cd TraceMaker
cmake --preset cpu-only
cmake --build --preset cpu-only
export PATH="$PWD/build/cpu-only/src/app:$PATH"
EX=tests/boards/plane_smd
tracemaker version

With a CUDA 12.x GPU, use the preset release in place of cpu-only (and build/release/... in the path). To use the live viewer, also build its page once: cd viewer && npm install && npm run build && cd .. (needs Node.js). More in Build and test.

Install Apple's Command Line Tools (xcode-select --install) and Homebrew, then:

brew install cmake ninja eigen cli11 nlohmann-json catch2 zstd boost clipper2
git clone https://github.com/DingoOz/TraceMaker.git
cd TraceMaker
cmake --preset macos-metal -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$(brew --prefix)"
cmake --build --preset macos-metal
export PATH="$PWD/build/macos-metal/src/app:$PATH"
EX=tests/boards/plane_smd
tracemaker version

macos-cpu builds without Metal. Metal speeds up only the cost-to-go fields (GPU, §8). For the live viewer, build its page once: cd viewer && npm install && npm run build && cd .. (brew install node).

Tested by a contributor, not in CI

Chris Hemingway built and tested this on an Apple M2 with macOS 15 (GPU, §8.2); CI does not build macOS, so a change can break it unnoticed. If a step fails, please open an issue with the output.

TraceMaker has no native Windows build. It should run in WSL2, the Linux system built into Windows, but this has not been tried yet. Please tell us how it goes.

In PowerShell, as administrator:

wsl --install -d Ubuntu-24.04

Restart if asked, open Ubuntu 24.04 from the Start menu, and follow the Linux: download tab from there. Your Windows drives are under /mnt/c, /mnt/d, …, so a board in your Documents folder is /mnt/c/Users/<you>/Documents/.... The live viewer opens in your Windows browser at the address it prints.

The KiCad plugin in the release is for KiCad on Linux; it cannot be used by KiCad for Windows.

docs.title: 2. Route the example board
docs.text:
The example is a 24 × 14 mm four-layer board with a 0.4 mm-pitch ball array, a QFN microcontroller and two power planes. EX was set in step 1.

mkdir -p out
cp $EX/plane_smd.kicad_pro out/routed.kicad_pro      # the design rules travel with the board
tracemaker route $EX/plane_smd.kicad_pcb -o out/routed.kicad_pcb \
    --soft-zones --via-in-pad --keep-vias-off-pads --first-nets XIN,XOUT \
    --work 3000000 --variants 4 --no-gpu

It takes a few seconds and ends with:

routed 49/49 connections, 108 tracks, 42 vias, ...

The options suit this dense board; a plain tracemaker route board.kicad_pcb -o out.kicad_pcb is where to start on your own boards. Route your first board explains each one.

docs.title: 3. Check it
docs.text:
tracemaker drc --refill-zones out/routed.kicad_pcb

With nothing listed after zones refilled, the board is clean. --refill-zones matters: without it the check uses the zone fill saved in the input file, which predates the new tracks.

KiCad's own check is the final word. With KiCad 10 installed (any platform), open out/routed.kicad_pcb in the PCB editor, or run:

kicad-cli pcb drc --refill-zones out/routed.kicad_pcb

No KiCad? Run kicad-cli from Docker.

docs.title: 4. Watch it route (optional)
docs.text:
tracemaker route $EX/plane_smd.kicad_pcb -o out/routed.kicad_pcb --view --hold \
    --soft-zones --via-in-pad --keep-vias-off-pads --first-nets XIN,XOUT \
    --work 3000000 --variants 4 --no-gpu

Open the address it prints (http://127.0.0.1:8766/) in a browser. --hold keeps the viewer open after routing ends; stop it with Ctrl+C.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Route your first board: the same board, step by step, with what each option does.
  • Route from inside KiCad: the plugin for KiCad 10 on Linux.
  • Command line: every option.

docs.title: D1 — Engine in C++20 and CUDA, viewer in TypeScript
Decision
docs.text: Engine in C++20 + CUDA; viewer in TypeScript + WebGL2/WebGPU; harness and plugin in Python

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Rust core (as KiCadRoutingTools); all-Python

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: CUDA ecosystem, existing C++ design, GCC 15 + nvcc available; Python is what kicad-cli/IPC tooling uses

docs.title: D2 — Placement in scope with four optimality levels
Decision
docs.text: Placement is in scope, with four explicit optimality levels

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Report-only placement (clean-sheet doc)

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: User requirement; honest claims instead of "optimal" in name only

docs.title: D3 — Analytic placement, then annealing, then exact windows
Decision
docs.text: Analytic global placement, then SA/LNS, then CP-SAT windows

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: SA only (SA-PCB); GA only (Allegro X AI); RL (RL_PCB)

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Analytic gives a provable relaxed optimum and a strong start; SA handles discrete PCB moves; CP-SAT gives exact local optima

docs.title: D4 — Octilinear lattice routing first, gridless later
Decision
docs.text: Detailed routing first on a fine octilinear lattice with exact validation; gridless tile plane later

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Gridless first (clean-sheet doc); Manhattan lattice (OrthoRoute)

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Faster to make correct, GPU-friendly; Manhattan-only routing scores poorly on mixed boards

docs.title: D5 — GPU never makes the final legality decision
Decision
docs.text: GPU accelerates fields, batches, broad-phases and placement — never the final legality decision

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: GPU end-to-end router

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Quality and determinism; CPU reference for every kernel

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Failure memory with four tiers (search, run, strategy, persistent)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: History cost only

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: User requirement; each tier has published precedent

docs.title: D7 — Native .kicad_pcb I/O, DSN for benchmarks only
Decision
docs.text: KiCad .kicad_pcb native I/O; DSN only for benchmarks/legacy

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: DSN/SES as main path

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: DSN loses rules (Freerouting evidence: 33/99 clean pass)

docs.title: D8 — KiCad DRC is the benchmark judge
Decision
docs.text: KiCad DRC (kicad-cli) is the benchmark judge

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Own DRC only

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Own DRC can be wrong in ways that hide errors

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Integer fixed-point costs everywhere decisions are made

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Floating point

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Bit-identical CPU/GPU, deterministic atomics

docs.title: D10 — Browser viewer served by the engine
Decision
docs.text: Viewer in the browser, served by the engine; WebGL2 baseline, WebGPU when available

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Native ImGui/Qt; WebGPU-only

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Remote use from any machine, GPU rendering, no install; WebGPU is not yet default on Linux Firefox

docs.title: D11 — Own CUDA kernels, no PyTorch or DREAMPlace runtime
Decision
docs.text: Own CUDA kernels for placement and routing; no PyTorch/DREAMPlace runtime dependency

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Embed DREAMPlace/Xplace

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: PyTorch wheels dropped Volta; CCCL 3/cuCollections partly untested on Pascal; BSD-3 code is ported, not linked

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: FLUTE (BSD-3, from OpenROAD stt) for Steiner trees

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: GeoSteiner

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: GeoSteiner is CC BY-NC (non-commercial)

docs.title: D13 — Courtyard gap fallbacks in full placement
Decision
docs.text: Full placement aims for a 0.25 mm courtyard gap (board rule if present), falling back to KiCad's default of 0, then to keeping unplaceable parts at their input positions, then to the refine result

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Always 0; always 0.25 mm

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Most human boards are packed below 0.25 mm; the fallbacks keep full mode usable on dense boards

docs.title: D14 — SimPL spreading instead of electrostatic density
Decision
docs.text: Global spreading uses SimPL rather than the electrostatic method

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: ePlace/DREAMPlace-style density

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Simpler on CPU and adequate for PCB part counts (doc 04 §7)

docs.title: D15 — New placement kept only if it routes as well
Decision
docs.text: Placement keeps a new placement only if it routes at least as well as the input under the same router budget (--route-check, --mode auto)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Trust HPWL

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Lower HPWL from denser packing routed worse on PCBench (13 vs 15 fully routed boards)

docs.title: D16 — Double-pitch portfolio variants on large boards
Decision
docs.text: Large boards (≥ 3M lattice points per layer) get two portfolio variants at double pitch

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: One pitch for all variants

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Fine-pitch lattices are time-limited on large boards (P8000: 325 → 334 of 361 in 120 s)

docs.title: D17 — CLI, Python module and plugin share one route function
Decision
docs.text: The CLI's route and the Python module's route() call one function (tmk::app::run_route_job); the KiCad plugin uses the module in-process when importable, else the binary

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Bindings that drive Router directly; plugin with the binary only

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Identical results by construction (tested byte for byte); no subprocess when the module fits KiCad's Python, and the binary still works when it does not

docs.title: D18 — Position-independent build when bindings are on
Decision
docs.text: With bindings on, the whole build is position independent (-fPIC -fno-semantic-interposition); bindings are off in sanitizer builds

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: A second PIC copy of the engine libraries; shared engine library

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: One set of objects; routing output and speed unchanged (C-BISCUIT: same board, 5.29 s vs 5.30 s); an instrumented extension cannot load into a plain interpreter

docs.title: D19 — PCM package without a bundled engine by default
docs.text: Superseded by D121

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: PCM package uses metadata schema v2 with runtime: ipc, does not bundle the engine by default (env TRACEMAKER / TRACEMAKER_PYTHONPATH), optional Linux bundling; licence field defaults to GPL-3.0-or-later until the project licence is chosen (requirement N8)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Always bundle binaries

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Native builds depend on the system's CUDA runtime, SQLite and libstdc++ and the module on the Python version; KiCad 10 ships PCM schema v2 and kicad-python 0.8 validates against it

docs.title: D20 — Annealed replica exchange for parallel tempering
Decision
docs.text: Parallel tempering is annealed replica exchange: the ladder (refine: 16× → 1× the annealing temperature; full: √8× → 1/√8×) follows the annealing schedule, exchanges decided at a barrier from a dedicated stream

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Fixed ladder T0 … 1e-4·T0 (textbook PT); independent runs only

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The fixed ladder accepted ~3 % of exchanges and cost +5 % vs independent runs; the annealed ladder is −4 % (refine, 23 boards) at the same move budget and identical for any thread count (doc 04 §8)

docs.title: D21 — RUDY overflow and pin density as routability term
Decision
docs.text: Routability term is RUDY overflow + pin density on a ≤ 32×32 grid, integer nm, power nets excluded; the router loop shrinks bin capacity around failed connections

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Electrostatic R(x) in global placement; airwire-crossing density only

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Cheap to keep incremental and exact in the annealer (reference = from-scratch recompute); capacity shrinking is the PCB analogue of RePlAce cell inflation

docs.title: D22 — Router as a callback in router-in-the-loop placement
Decision
docs.text: Router-in-the-loop and ECO take the router as a callback (RouteFn) and accept a placement only if it leaves fewer connections unrouted (ties: shorter HPWL for seeds only)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Link tm::route into tm::place; accept on estimated overflow

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Keeps tm::place independent of the router and testable with a synthetic router; the router's verdict, not an estimate, decides (rule 4)

docs.title: D23 — Exact windows by own branch and bound, not CP-SAT
Decision
docs.text: Exact windows (doc 04 §3 F) by own branch and bound over candidate slots (own spot, other window parts' spots, HPWL-median spot; 4 rotations), not CP-SAT

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: OR-Tools CP-SAT

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: OR-Tools is not installed; B&B is exact over its candidate set, has a full-enumeration reference path, and is small enough to run inside annealing

docs.title: D24 — --route-check restores a rejected placement by copying the input
Decision
docs.text: --route-check restores a rejected placement by copying the input file

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Re-saving the edited document

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The editor edits the document in place, so re-saving wrote the new placement while reporting "kept input" (M7 bug, fixed 2026-10-03)

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Decoupling capacitors are tied to the nearest IC supply pin (in the input placement) by a two-pin pseudo-net at signal weight (PNet::affinity), counted in the objective only; on by default, --no-decap-affinity turns it off

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Hungarian assignment + distance constraint (doc 04 §2)

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Power nets carry weight 1, so full placement moved decaps 4 → 16–19 mm from their ICs (place_intent.py). The pseudo-net keeps every placer stage (B2B, annealer, LNS, bound) exact and unchanged and brings decaps to 1.8–3 mm (closer than the human layouts) for 1–9 % more HPWL. Assignment by optimisation is still open.

docs.title: D26 — Component-rule catalogue in YAML, embedded as generated JSON
Decision
docs.text: The component-rule catalogue stays docs/component_rules.yaml; scripts/crules_catalogue.py writes src/crules/catalogue.json, which the build embeds; a ctest fails if the JSON, the YAML and the rule ids in doc 15 drift

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: A YAML parser in the engine; JSON as the edited source

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: One small generated file instead of a new dependency; the YAML keeps comments and stays readable for people editing rules

docs.title: D27 — lib_id detectors match the footprint name only
Decision
docs.text: lib_id detectors match the footprint name only, unless the pattern names a library (connector_usb:, rf_module:)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Match the whole library:footprint string

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Library nicknames are free text: on PCBench UCCBPCB the nickname usb_ccb_custom: made an MCU, a jumper and headers "USB connectors" (precision first, doc 15 §9.1)

docs.title: D28 — Component proximity rules reuse affinity pseudo-nets
Decision
docs.text: Component proximity rules reuse D25's objective-only two-pin pseudo-nets (ExtractOptions::affinities): weight 10, ×2 for a protection part to its connector; each part is pulled by one rule (crystal > oscillator > ESD > regulator > decoupling), D25's own ties are kept unchanged and win

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Hard distance constraints in the legaliser; a separate cost term

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Same exact incremental cost in every placer stage; reported HPWL/crossings/congestion unchanged; no conflicting pulls on one part; off reproduces the previous placer byte for byte

docs.title: D29 — Generated keep-outs for crystals and switching inductors
Decision
docs.text: Generated keep-outs (crystal + load caps XTAL-04, switching inductor BUCK-06/BOOST-04) are rule areas on the copper layers where none of the parts has a pad and no other part has a pad inside, tracks only, used by the router only with --component-rules on and never written to the output; the full net-exempt rule (all layers, tracks and vias) goes to the sidecar <output>.tracemaker.kicad_dru as intersectsCourtyard rules

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Keep-outs on every layer; editing the user's .kicad_dru

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: KiCad rule areas cannot exempt nets, so a keep-out on a part's own pad layer would cut its pads off; soft adds no hard constraints (doc 15 §3.5); rule 8 forbids touching the user's files. KiCad's DRC reads the sidecar (checked on PCBench CANadapter)

docs.title: D30 — Per-net coupled routing for detected USB pairs
Decision
docs.text: Per-net coupled routing through RouterOptions::pair_nets (pairs routed coupled first when diff_pairs is off), filled from detected USB 2.0 D+/D- pairs with --component-rules soft or on

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Name-based P/N detection only (--diff-pairs, all or nothing)

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: USB nets are often named DP/DM (not P/N or +/-); a three-line hook (pair_wanted) keeps the router change minimal while the router is being changed elsewhere

docs.title: D31 — --component-rules off by default for placement and routing
docs.text: Superseded by D52

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: --component-rules defaults to off for both tracemaker-place and tracemaker route; soft is opt-in

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Default soft (doc 15 §3.5 planned it once the §9 gates pass)
