docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Measured on the 23-board placement set, 9 ESD boards and 6 boards × 3 seeds (doc 15 §14.3): soft brings crystals 6.4 → 5.1 mm, ESD parts 7.1 → 3.2 mm and load caps closer at equal HPWL, but decoupling and regulator caps move away on some boards (decaps worse on 9 of 18 runs); doubling the decap ties fixes that for +2–3 % HPWL. Held-out detection recall for USB connectors, connectors and mounting holes is below the 0.8 gate. off reproduces the previous output byte for byte

docs.title: D32 — Escape planning v1 as reserved corridors
Decision
docs.text: Escape planning v1 is reserved corridors (perimeter out, dog-bone for inner SMD balls) checked by the normal router, not a min-cost-flow pre-route

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Min-cost-flow escape routing first (doc 05 §3)

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The BGA failures were mostly infeasible under the fixture rules or time-starved strict passes; corridors fix the "channel taken first" case cheaply (logicbone +26, decelerator +33 at a fixed budget) and cannot create violations. MCF stays open for deep arrays

docs.title: D33 — Escape planning in two of eight portfolio variants
Decision
docs.text: Escape planning runs in two of the eight portfolio variants (not all)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: All variants; opt-in only

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: All variants: tier B +8 connections, tier C −7, BGA set +31, tier A equal: neutral on average, so it is an arm the portfolio can pick where it helps

docs.title: D34 — Escalation rung necks vias down to board minimum
Decision
docs.text: The escalation rung necks vias down to the smallest via the board minimums allow (drill ≥ 0.2 mm)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Net-class via only

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: KiCad checks vias against the board minimums; d20_tri +24, OtterCast +17 with 0 added KiCad errors

docs.title: D35 — Escape feasibility reported beside the clean pass
Decision
docs.text: Escape feasibility (tracemaker escape) is reported beside the clean pass (dead_pins, clean_pass_feasible), never instead of it

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Drop infeasible boards from the benchmark

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: PCBench ships no .kicad_pro; some boards cannot be routed clean by any router under the rules they are judged by (designers' own boards fail them). Hiding them would flatter both tools

docs.title: D36 — Impedance rules computed and reported only
docs.text: Superseded by D58

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Impedance rules (P4) are computed and reported only: width/gap per routing layer from the board stackup in tracemaker rules; routing widths and net classes are unchanged and --component-rules stays off by default

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Synthesise per-layer net classes and route with them

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The benchmark has no stackups (0 of 1,157 PCBench unrouted files), the formulas carry ±2–8 % model error plus ±10 % fab tolerance, and the reference-plane assumption is not yet checked by plane coverage; a report lets a designer confirm before anything is enforced (doc 15 §14.5)

docs.title: D37 — Closed-form impedance models from the papers
Decision
docs.text: Closed-form models: Hammerstad & Jensen microstrip, Cohn/Wheeler stripline, Kirschning & Jansen coupled microstrip, Cohn coupled stripline, Ghione & Naldi GCPW; off-centre striplines by Wadell's image split; quasi-static, solder mask ignored; width/gap by integer-nm bisection

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: A 2-D field solver; KiCad's calculator code (GPL, and its coupled-stripline thin-gap branch drops √εr)

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Same physics as KiCad's PCB calculator so users can cross-check; independent implementation from the papers; deterministic; agreement with KiCad 0–3 % and with exact conformal results to 1e-6 (doc 15 §14.5)

docs.title: D38 — Adjacent copper layer as the assumed reference plane
Decision
docs.text: The copper layer adjacent to a routing layer is taken as its reference plane (microstrip outside, stripline between the neighbours inside); a ground zone on it is reported as confirmation, otherwise "(assumed)"

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Require a zone; search for the nearest plane-typed layer

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: KiCad boards rarely type planes as power; 2-layer boards pour GND on the far side; the report keeps the assumption visible per layer

docs.title: D39 — Differential pairs solved for width at the class gap
Decision
docs.text: Pairs are solved at the Default net class's diff-pair gap (≥ its clearance and the board minimum); the width is solved, and only if the width would fall below the board minimum (≥ 0.1 mm) is the gap solved instead

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Solve width and gap jointly for Zdiff and a common-mode target; fixed S = W

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: One free variable keeps the result unique and deterministic; the gap the board already uses is the one the router will keep

docs.title: D40 — User rule override file in strictly checked JSON
Decision
docs.text: The user override file (doc 15 §6.3) is JSON read by the engine (--rules-override on rules, route, tracemaker-place); YAML is converted by scripts/crules_override.py. Unknown keys, rule ids, categories, parameters, value types and board references are errors; an entry that names a part not detected as its category is a reported warning

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: A YAML parser in C++; silently ignoring entries that do not apply

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Same approach as the catalogue (D26: no YAML library for one file); a typo must never drop an override, but a board edit must not stop routing when the catalogue default (the conservative side) still applies

docs.title: D41 — ETH-05 magnetics keep-out like XTAL-04
Decision
docs.text: ETH-05 (no copper under discrete Ethernet magnetics) becomes a generated keep-out like XTAL-04: tracks, vias and zones on the magnetics' side and the adjacent copper layer where the magnetics have no pads, at confidence ≥ apply, used by the router only with --component-rules on; RJ45 jacks with integrated magnetics get none

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: A void on every layer; a void under MagJacks too

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The catalogue says "same, adjacent" and "not required under integrated-magnetics RJ45" (TI SNLA387); keeping the area off the pads' layer keeps the transformer's own pins routable

docs.title: D42 — Opt-in connector edge attraction by axis anchor
Decision
docs.text: Connector edge attraction is an opt-in placement objective (--edge-attraction): a one-pin pseudo-net from the connector body point nearest to the outline to the nearest outline segment's axis (x for a vertical segment, y for a horizontal one), weight 2 × signal; pin headers and sockets are not pulled

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: A virtual fixed part at the nearest outline point; a separate distance-to-polygon term in the cost

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: An axis anchor is exact in the integer HPWL the annealer already maintains incrementally (no new cost term to keep in sync), does not pin the connector to one point along the edge, and penalises rotating the mating side inwards; headers are mostly board-to-board or jumpers (CONN-01 note)

docs.title: D43 — Two-stage component-rule pulls in full placement
Decision
docs.text: --component-rules soft in full placement runs in two stages: decoupling ties only (D25 and DEC-*), then those capacitors and their ICs are locked and the other component-rule pulls (crystal, load caps, ESD, regulator caps) refine from there (--no-crules-two-stage reverts)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: One stage with all pulls (the first version); scaling the weights

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: One stage: decaps worse on 9 of 18 multi-seed runs. Weights (50/75 %) did not fix it on seeds 2–4. Two stages, 23 boards × 3 seeds vs off: decap median equal (3.66/3.42/3.74 vs 3.66/3.26/3.74 mm), crystal 5.11/6.70/5.07 → 4.66/5.77/4.72, load caps 2.38/4.77/3.11 → 2.03/2.76/2.39, HPWL geometric mean −1 %; 18 per-board metrics better, 4 worse (PocketBone decaps on all seeds). Component rules stay off by default

docs.title: D44 — Flood-fill reachability pre-check before strict searches
Decision
docs.text: A flood-fill reachability pre-check runs before strict searches that are likely to fail (a retry with a larger window, or a connection that failed before); "no path" skips the A* and its cost-to-go field (--reach-check 1, default; 0 off, 2 every strict search; --reach-verify re-checks with the full A*)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Reusing the failed search's explored region on window growth; a coarse-grid check; checking every strict search

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The flood uses the same legality tests with no bend states or costs, so it admits every A* path and its verdict is exact (0 mismatches under --reach-verify). 10 hard boards, one variant, 100 M: 8,285 → 8,332 routed, no board worse; every-search mode 8,336 but swings ±45 per board. Tiers A–D neutral (2,637 / 5,165 / 9,523 / 16,628 routed, clean pass unchanged). Region reuse would not keep the A* optimal in the larger window; a coarse grid would not be exact

docs.title: D45 — Replay logs as zstd-compressed JSON lines
Decision
docs.text: Replay logs stay JSON lines (the live protocol, doc 13), zstd-compressed as independent frames when the file ends in .zst (snapshot in its own frame, frames closed every 1 MiB, checksums); plain .jsonl stays the default. Heatmaps are coarse grids (≤ 128 cells a side) of A* expansions and PathFinder history, sent by work done (every max(200k, budget / 40) expansions)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: FlatBuffers for the protocol and the log now (doc 09 §2, §6); a custom binary record format; gzip

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: FlatBuffers is installed (flatc 23.5) but the message set is still changing (escape plan, component rules added in M9/M13), every message would need a schema in C++ and TypeScript plus a viewer decoder, and the gain is decode speed the viewer does not need yet. zstd on the JSON gives the compactness (12–13× on C-BISCUIT and CANadapter, 260 kB → 20 kB) with one small dependency, stays readable with zstd -dc, and keeps the Python tools (report/render_events.py, the record/replay test) working on the same text. Independent frames bound the loss when a run is killed and leave room for a seek index. FlatBuffers stays an open M3 task for when the message set is stable

docs.title: D46 — Evidence code D for rules with TraceMaker default values
Decision
docs.text: Catalogue evidence gains a fourth code, D: the cited source was read and supports the rule, but gives no number, so the value is a TraceMaker default. D rules are demoted from hard to soft at run time like R rules; each verified rule carries a checked field (date, status, document, section/page). The 41 R rules were checked against their sources (doc 15 §8.10): 9 confirmed, 9 corrected, 11 left as defaults (D), 12 not verifiable (stay R)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Keep R for every rule with a TraceMaker default; mark the rules V once the qualitative statement is read

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: R meant "not re-read", which is no longer true for 29 rules; V would claim the numbers come from the source when they do not. D keeps both facts visible and keeps those rules from becoming hard by accident. No current D rule is hard and no engine-read parameter changed (RF-03, SHLD-01 and BUCK-07 values changed; their kinds are not enforced yet), so placement and routing are unchanged

docs.title: D47 — Portfolio variant set independent of thread count
Decision
docs.text: The router portfolio's variant set is a setting (--variants), not the thread count: with --work it defaults to all eight variants for any --threads; the variants run on a pool of --threads workers in index order and the winner is the minimum of a total order (routed desc, vias, copper length, variant index). Without --work the default stays one variant per thread

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Variants = threads (as before: --threads 1 --work ran variant 0 only, so the output changed with the thread count); successive halving first

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Requirement N3: route --work N --seed S is byte-identical at 1, 2, 4, 8 threads (test thread_determinism); wall-clock mode is not deterministic anyway, so it keeps one variant per thread and its speed. Fewer threads than variants costs wall time, not quality; --variants 1 reproduces the old single-router run byte for byte. --time is a safety stop per variant, counted from that variant's start

docs.title: D48 — Opt-in side assignment by annealer flip moves
Decision
docs.text: Side assignment (doc 04 §3 C/E, §9) is opt-in (--flip) and done by the annealer: a flip move (KiCad top/bottom mirror plus any turn, at the body centre or the nets' weighted median) for movable surface-mount parts on 2+ copper-layer boards whose footprint the writer can mirror exactly, plus a via-estimate cost (per net min(front, back) surface-mount pins × weight × --flip-via-mm 2). No FM/CP-SAT partition in stage (C), no side capacity in (B), no flips in ECO or exact windows. Orientation states become 0–7 (bit 2 = other side). The writer reproduces KiCad's FOOTPRINT::Flip, so a flip rewrites the footprint's child coordinates and layers (doc 04 §5 said only at, layer and pad layers change)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: FM min-cut partition with area capacity per side, CP-SAT for ≤ 40 parts (doc 04 §3 C); flipping on by default

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The annealer already holds the exact legality and incremental cost, so a flip move gets side assignment that respects courtyards on both sides, through-holes and copper for free; a partition before legalisation knows none of that. Off by default because double-sided assembly is a design decision and the via cost is real (23 boards: HPWL −7.9 % full / −7.6 % refine, crossings −31 %, but the via estimate rises 85 → ~480, routability unmeasured). Mirroring geometry by KiCad's own rules was verified against pcbnew on 2,529 footprints with 0 differences

docs.title: D49 — Opt-in min-cost-flow escape planning v2
Decision
docs.text: Escape planning version 2 (min-cost-flow channel assignment on the pad layer, dog-bone sites by a second flow, then the same flow per further layer with the vias as obstacles; doc 05 §14) is opt-in (--escape-flow) and in no portfolio variant; one planning rule set per array (the most common class width/clearance/via), gap capacity from the narrower diagonal for all tracks

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Replace version 1 in the two escape-plan variants; exact per-net capacities; Yan & Wong's separate per-diagonal accounting

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: One variant at fixed budgets on the 7 BGA-set boards with deep arrays: off 2,687, version 1 2,736, version 2 2,703 routed (better only on DoroidOscillo, +6 over version 1); narrower bands did not change that. A shared rule set keeps one power net from closing every channel; the narrower diagonal is conservative, so planned escapes always fit; the plan only reserves, so it cannot create violations (0 added KiCad errors on 3 outputs)

docs.title: D50 — Differential pairs searched as one object
Decision
docs.text: Differential pairs (doc 05 §15) are searched as one object: A* over (layer, lattice point, direction, side) with straight steps, 45° turns followed by a miter-safe straight run, and coupled via pairs, every move checked exactly on both tracks; breakout/fan-in legs validated lazily when a start or goal is popped; gap from the custom diff_pair_gap rule, else the net class's diff-pair gap, else the clearance between the halves. A ripped half takes its partner and the pair is re-tried coupled; the clean-up re-couples split pairs with exact restore; a pair that boxes in a pin between its pins is taken back. Off by default (--diff-pairs, pair_nets)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: v1's centreline with an envelope disk and legs checked afterwards; routing the halves separately with a coupling cost; coupled copper dearer to cross in negotiation; budget held back for re-coupling; refusing pairs that straddle a pin

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: v1 coupled none of the USB hub's 5 pairs; v2 couples them at 84–94 % with 0 KiCad errors. On 18 boards (59 pairs) 35 pairs are ≥ 50 % coupled at the rule gap, completion 2,201 → 2,210, two boards −1 within fixed-budget noise. Separate routing cannot guarantee the gap; the dearer crossing cost PmodHDMIIn two connections; refusing straddling pairs lost edid-injector's 88 % coupling for nothing. Off by default because coupling costs space on dense boards and the pair detection is by name only

docs.title: D51 — DRC follows KiCad 10 connectivity on broken boards
Decision
docs.text: The DRC follows KiCad 10's connectivity on broken boards: net propagation before the checks (pads' net to the tracks/vias/board graphics of single-net clusters; zone-only vias take a zone's net), dangling tracks/vias judged on the any-net item graph, same-net items joined by copper overlap, KiCad's short/clearance split (zone overlaps are clearance; track/via overlaps short even net-less; pads short only with two nets), per-layer via reports, zero-clearance track/via-to-hole and edge tests, via/pad holes against fills, free vias, net-tie exclusions, KiCad's circle-in-rectangle gap (a via inside another net's rectangular pad is clearance), net-class drills for vias written without one, slots left out of hole-to-hole, and a zone's own clearance as a local clearance on its fill. The board reader no longer treats KiCad 9+ user layers typed signal (odd ordinals) as copper (multichannel_mixer-unrouted had 11 phantom copper layers; this also changes routing on such boards). Measured with scripts/drc_broken_parity.py (defects injected deterministically by tracemaker selftest-defects). The router keeps end-point connectivity and net-class clearance to fills for now

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Keep file nets and anchor connectivity (TraceMaker's own, stricter notion of a short); emulate only the counts

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: KiCad's DRC is the judge and reads the board after propagation (verified in its 10.0.6 sources and on injected defects: a stray via on another net's track is no short there). The router changes (zone clearance, overlap links) alter routing and need a quick-tier run, so they are left for a follow-up

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: tracemaker-place defaults to --component-rules soft (proximity pseudo-nets for crystals, load caps, ESD parts, regulator caps and generalised decoupling; objective-only, two-stage in full mode per D43); routing's default stays off

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Keep off (or report) until decap distances also improve

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Placed tiers B and C (70 boards, rules off vs soft side by side): clean pass 28 → 28 and 18 → 18, routed 5,163 → 5,156 and 9,538 → 9,539; XTAL-01 median 6.54 → 5.57 mm, load caps 3.11 → 2.81 mm, decaps 3.17 → 3.17 mm (losses traced to the router keeping a different candidate). Full mode, 23 boards × 3 seeds (D43): crystal and load caps better, decaps equal. No routing cost, a measured gain for crystals; doc 15 §14.3

docs.title: D53 — Global congestion map off, global router v2 deferred
docs.text: Superseded by D56

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: The global congestion map (--global-congestion, doc 05 §16) stays off, and the rest of global router v2 (Steiner topology, via capacity, GPU pattern/maze port) is deferred

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Turn the map on; continue with v2

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: 18 hard boards at a fixed budget: 13,285 routed without, 13,289–13,294 with (noise); corridors 12,933. With cut-based capacities under 5 % of tiles reach 6/8 utilisation; about two thirds of unrouted connections on tiers B–D are boxed-in pins, which tiles cannot see

docs.title: D54 — Connection planning by copper gap, group re-route removed
Decision
docs.text: Connection planning weighs pad pairs by the gap between their copper, not by centre distance (--plan-gap, default on; doc 05 §17). The group re-route (R4 trial) is removed

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Keep centre distance; keep the group re-route as an option

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Fixed budget, one variant, 24 boards: 11,905 → 11,986 routed. KiCad-judged tiers A–D neutral (tier D side by side 16,618 → 16,622, clean pass equal), no added errors. The group re-route changed no board's result

docs.title: D55 — DRC zone-fill edge index instead of GPU broad-phase
Decision
docs.text: The DRC tests items against zone fills through an edge index and caches area-rule results per fill; no GPU broad-phase is built

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: LBVH broad-phase on the GPU (doc 07)

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Profile of vme-wren: broad-phase 14 ms, exact tests against fills 650 of 730 s. With the index 7 s, reports byte-identical to the linear reference path (doc 05 §19)

docs.title: D56 — Global router v2 kept off and M6 closed
Decision
docs.text: Global router v2 (net-shared edges, via capacity, layer-true corridors, integer costs) is kept off, and the GPU pattern/maze port is not built; M6 is closed

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Turn corridors or the map on; port GAMER/GGR kernels

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: 18 hard boards at a fixed budget: 13,305 routed without, 12,967 with corridors, 13,324 with the map (noise). Tile-graph routing takes 0.02–0.5 s per board (doc 05 §19)

docs.title: D57 — M8 closed with its gate not met
Decision
docs.text: M8 is closed with its gate measured and not met: from-scratch clean pass 85 % on the held-out set S (gate 90 %). R6 cut proofs are built (--cut-report); R4, R5, GPU tempering and CP-SAT windows are not

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Keep M8 open until 90 %; build the remaining rungs

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Four of the six failing boards cannot be made clean by any placement under the rules the judge applies (three have a part that fits nowhere legally, one is not routable clean in its human placement); cut lines are at most 40 % full and the group re-route changed no board (doc 04 §10, doc 05 §20)

docs.title: D58 — Impedance and width rules as synthetic net classes
Decision
docs.text: Impedance and width rules become synthetic net classes (tmk_<RULE>_<ref>) for Default-class nets of instances at the apply threshold; used by the router only with --component-rules on; one width per net (the front-layer solution)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Per-layer widths; writing the classes into the project file

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The router has one width per net, and the user's files are never written (rule 8). Board classes win; a class is never narrower than the board allows (doc 15 §15)

docs.title: D59 — Restart-based successive halving stays off
Decision
docs.text: Successive halving for the portfolio (--halving) is restart-based and stays off

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Resumable router runs; halving on by default with fewer threads than variants

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: 24 boards: 12,385 / 12,451 routed at 2 / 4 threads against 12,402 / 12,508 for the first variants on the whole budget (doc 05 §22)

docs.title: D60 — Plugin refills zones only on request or after moves
Decision
docs.text: The plugin refills zones only on request or after it moved footprints

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Always refill

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: KiCad records the refill as its own undo step; the plugin's promise is one undo for a routing run (doc 08 §8)

docs.title: D61 — JSON protocol kept, FlatBuffers dropped
Decision
docs.text: The viewer protocol and replay log stay JSON; the FlatBuffers schema is dropped from the roadmap

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: A .fbs schema with C++ and JavaScript codecs

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: D45's reasons held: zstd JSON logs are 12–13× smaller than plain, recording does not change routing, the browser parses JSON natively. No measurement shows the protocol as a bottleneck

docs.title: D62 — M9 closed with two items unbuilt
Decision
docs.text: M9 is closed with two items unbuilt (negotiated fallback for escapes, escape templates) and its gate not met

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Build both

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The flow planner the fallback belongs to measured below the simple corridors and is off; planning takes 0.1–2 s, so a template cache saves nothing (doc 05 §23)

docs.title: D63 — Half-pitch variant for small boards, no gridless arm
Decision
docs.text: One portfolio variant (cheap vias) routes small boards at half the lattice pitch; no gridless arm is built

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: A gridless tile-plane router as a portfolio arm

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Half pitch at four times the work: 4,140 → 4,153 routed on 12 nearly clean boards, one more complete. As a variant: tier B 27 → 28 clean, tier C equal, routed +7 and +8, no added errors (doc 05 §25)

docs.title: D64 — Coupled pairs may twist at layer changes
Decision
docs.text: Coupled pairs may twist at a layer change (on with pair routing); learned ordering and congestion models are not built

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Twists off; a learned net-ordering model

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Twists: 59 pairs, one gains coupling (0 → 86 %), none loses, median share 57 → 63 %. Ordering changes measured no effect on completion and tile congestion is absent (doc 05 §24, §25)

docs.title: D65 — Rule areas block tracks and vias by own flags
Decision
docs.text: A rule area blocks tracks when it forbids tracks and vias when it forbids vias (the obstacle model read only areas forbidding tracks, and they blocked vias too)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Keep the old reading

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: KiCad's meaning; a full-board "no tracks" area on a plane layer is the usual way to keep a plane whole, and it made every via through that layer illegal. A "no vias" area blocked nothing before

docs.title: D66 — Opt-in soft zone fills as via targets
Decision
docs.text: Soft zone fills and untouched planes as via targets are opt-in (--soft-zones); zone-only clusters count only for nets with pads and fills of at least 1 mm²

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Make them the default; switch them on when a board has inner planes and only SMD pads

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The output keeps stale fills that the user must refill, and the benchmark boards are judged as written. Padless zone-only clusters planned an empty connection (review of PR 1); slivers of a stale fill would become mandatory targets

docs.title: D67 — Vias kept off SMD pads narrower than 2 mm
Decision
docs.text: Vias stay off SMD pads narrower than 2 mm (--keep-vias-off-pads, any net, net-class clearance), exposed pads excepted

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Allow same-net vias in pads (the default); a separate via-in-pad cost

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Plane targets made in-pad vias the cheapest plane connection (about 100 on one board, 0.5 mm vias in 0.25 mm pins), which needs filled and capped vias and spoils fine-pitch lands. 2 mm keeps 0402/0603, QFN pins, crystals and test pads clear and lets exposed pads take thermal vias

docs.title: D68 — Via in pad at the board minimum via, opt-in
Decision
docs.text: A via in pad (--via-in-pad) is the board's minimum via, only for inner balls or enclosed pads, at four vias at the current via price on either end, one per pad; none when the minimum via could not be read

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: A fixed price; a fallback size

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Rule 6. The fixed price was undercut when the clean-up raises the via price, and the penalty was charged at the source only: on inpad_cost both balls took a via in pad instead of two ordinary vias (review of PR 1)

docs.title: D69 — --first-nets routes named nets first and protects them
Decision
docs.text: --first-nets routes the named nets first, again after every restart, and neither negotiation nor the via clean-up rips them for other nets

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Length limits per net; a crystal corridor from the component rules

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The simplest control that fixed the case (crystal 25.7 → 4.3 / 5.1 mm); the catalogue (doc 15) detects crystals and could fill the list

docs.title: D70 — Native macOS with an optional Metal backend
Decision
docs.text: Native macOS uses Apple Clang and an optional Metal cost-to-go backend; field_gpu, compiled_backend, and backend-neutral device indices replace CUDA-specific routing APIs. CUDA remains the Linux backend and CPU references remain universal. Metal kernels are embedded, compiled once per device, and use reusable per-thread shared buffers, ordered dispatches, and an atomic convergence flag.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: CPU-only Mac support; CUDA translation layer; a full GPU router or GPU placer

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Direct Metal supports Apple silicon without changing routing decisions. Integer CPU equality and real-board byte equality gate the port. GPU availability is not a speed guarantee; Metal reports working-set headroom rather than claiming free VRAM.

docs.title: D71 — Metal cost-to-go field by segmented prefix-min scan
Decision
docs.text: The Metal cost-to-go field solves each line as a segmented prefix-min scan of 64-bit keys d[j] − c·j on one 32-lane SIMD-group, sweeps each direction pair (forward, backward) and all layers in one dispatch, batches 16 then 8 rounds per command buffer with early-exit dispatches after convergence, and gives every calling thread its own command queue. Every round ends in the CPU reference's state, so fields and round counts are bit-identical.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Keep one thread per line (first kernel); threadgroup-wide Hillis-Steele scans with staged lines (tried: 3.2× single-caller, still slower than the CPU under 8 callers); a GPU-resident A*

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Fields were 50 % of the router's CPU time on a private 4-layer board and the first kernel was slower than the CPU under portfolio load. The scan kernel: 4.6× one caller and 3× the CPU with 8 concurrent callers on 2,311 captured fields (0 mismatches), route 16.2 → 9.2 s and --mode routable 336 → 228 s with byte-identical outputs on default rules (0.075 mm lattice); on the project's rules (0.050 mm) the A* loop dominates and fields are ~1–5 % of a 121 s route (doc 07 §8.1). A* stays on the CPU (D5).

docs.title: D72 — Router enforces net- and layer-only custom disallow rules
Decision
docs.text: The router enforces custom disallow track/via rules whose conditions depend only on net, net class, type and layer, as a per-net layer mask and a per-net via switch, and physical_hole_clearance between holes and any other item's copper (new tracks and vias against existing holes, new via holes against fixed and routed copper, any net; a net gets no vias when the rule holds between its vias and its own tracks); keepout areas block tracks and vias by their own flags (D65). The DRC reports disallow as items_not_allowed and physical_hole_clearance as hole_clearance, as KiCad does. Disallow rules and net-independent physical_hole_clearance rules keep the per-class obstacle cache.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Leave these rules to KiCad's DRC after routing; evaluate every rule per probe on the exact path (any custom rule disabled the cache and cost-to-go fields); block nets on layers by rule areas

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Users write these rules to shape the layout (inner layers for planes, no via in pad); a router that ignores them produces boards KiCad rejects (a private 4-layer board: 119 inner tracks, 64 vias in pads, a via in a footprint keepout). Pre-evaluated masks cost nothing in the search; keeping the cache avoids a several-fold slowdown. Position-dependent disallow conditions are warned, not guessed (CLAUDE.md rule 6). Doc 05 §27.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Router hot paths (doc 05 §28): the net class of every net is resolved once when the router is built (no name matching per lattice point); rule-lookup probe items come from a per-thread pool; a cell's via check is skipped when no other layer could improve at the bare via cost; a new via's routed-copper check tests layer-independent parts once; PathFinder history is read once per cell per search; second round: one-pass fixed via codes (fixed_via_code_reference kept and tested), no shape allocation in hot checks, degenerate-segment fast path in seg_seg_closer (tested exact). The skipped via checks cannot improve any state, but they leave fewer via codes cached, so the cost-to-go field sees fewer known via-blocked cells and expansion counts change slightly; since --work counts expansions, identical output is empirical (48 of 48 boards at the merge, doc 05 §28), not guaranteed. Only fixed_via_code and seg_seg_closer have reference tests; the other equivalences were checked by reading.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Fewer route-check variants or a smaller work budget in the placement loop (changes results); a mutable class cache inside DesignRules (shared across threads); small-buffer shapes to remove the remaining point allocations (wide refactor)

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The 20M-work route check on a 0.05 mm lattice went from ~140 s to ~10 s, which makes routability-driven placement with project rules practical; the second round removes a further ~20% of CPU time (measured by instructions retired, since timings are noisy on a shared machine)

docs.title: D74 — Footprints clear of the outline are unplaced parts
Decision
docs.text: Footprints entirely clear of the board outline's bounding box are unplaced parts, not intentional overhangs: they stay movable, and their pads are left out of the test that accepts the largest Edge.Cuts loop as the outline (≥ 80 % of pads inside). Parts that touch or straddle the outline keep the overhang rule.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Treat every part outside the outline as an intentional overhang (old behaviour: a board straight from Update PCB from Schematic could not be placed, and with most pads outside the outline was rejected for its bounding box); a flag to mark parts unplaced

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: From-scratch placement of a fresh netlist import must work without the user first dragging parts onto the board; an off-board footprint with pads is never a finished layout. Test: [place] "parts dropped beside the board are placed".

docs.title: D75 — Opt-in minimal repair of illegal input placements
Decision
docs.text: With --repair-input (off by default), placement legality for choosing a result is absolute: an input with an overlap or outline violation involving a movable part (board courtyard rule, else 0) is replaced, as the comparison baseline and fallback, by its minimal repair (place::repaired: only the conflicting movable parts re-placed at the nearest legal spot). routable seeds with the repair and verifies against it; other illegal seeds are routed for reference only and never become the incumbent. --route-check writes the repair when the new placement routes worse; eco starts from it. An input with no repair is compared as it is (old behaviour), and the report names the conflicts left.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Strict: never keep an illegal input, the best legal candidate wins even if it routes worse (14 of 30 PCBench tier-A hand placements have model conflicts, some clean in KiCad; tried: auto on LogicBoxen went 0 → 8 unrouted); keep the old rule and only report the conflicts (the private board would still output shorts); judge only conflicts involving moved parts (the old rule: a routable run kept an overlapping input plus one ECO move and called it "legal")

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: A result with overlapping parts is not a placement, whatever its route count, and the hand layout should stay as close as the conflicts allow. The model is conservative, so an unrepairable input is not presumed wrong. Chosen by the contributor's user over the strict and report-only variants. Made opt-in when merged (2026-10-07): by default the input is compared and kept as it is, as before, because the repair is never compared with the original (rule 4) and the conservative model moved a part of a placement KiCad calls clean (kitspace_threeboard: U1 by 0.25 mm in x and y). --scratch is unaffected. Tests: [m8] "with absolute seed legality illegal seeds are reference only unless the input is accepted as it is", "minimal repair: only parts in a conflict move".

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Layer limits are two opt-in router options for all nets: --no-tracks-on (no new tracks; vias and plane connections stay) and --layer-cost (integer per-mille factor on track length, never below 1)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Read the limit from KiCad's layer type (power); allow factors below 1 to prefer a layer; per-net limits on the command line

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Issue #6. Layer types are often left at signal or set to power on layers that do carry signals, so the type would change results on boards whose owners asked for nothing. Below 1 the search heuristics stop being lower bounds. Per-net limits are KiCad custom rules. Six 4-layer boards: inner-layer track 34 % → 0 % (1,058 → 1,038 routed) or → 6 % at factor 4 (1,054 routed), no added errors (doc 05 §29)

docs.title: D77 — Coupled-pair work counts every leg check
Decision
docs.text: A coupled-pair attempt's work is its closed states plus every exact leg check of a start or goal candidate, legal or not; it is added to the router's total every 64 steps, when the work budget and time limit are checked, and leg checks have no per-attempt cap

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Count only closed states (old); cap leg checks at the state budget; charge per candidate instead of per check; poll only the time limit

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Rejected candidates were free, so an attempt with every leg blocked by fill polygons ran 635 s at --work 20000 and overran --time 900 by 148 s. Per check follows the cost (0–72 checks per candidate). The cap lost coupling on three of 18 boards at 30 M. Polling the budget keeps budgeted runs deterministic (same output at 1 and 2 threads); the time limit stays a safety stop. Pairs off: byte-identical (quick tier); 17 of 18 pair boards byte-identical at 30 M, the 18th identical once the budget includes its 958,420 leg checks (doc 05 §30)

docs.title: D78 — Router zone-fill probes through the DRC edge index
Decision
docs.text: The router's obstacle tests answer probes against zone fills from the DRC's edge index (geom::PolygonIndex via drc::ZoneFills); the per-edge loop stays as the reference path

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Keep the linear loop; index only the coupled-pair leg checks; cache fixed codes harder

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The answers are equal by construction and by test, so it is a pure speed change: six KiCad demos at 10 M 515 → 119 s, CM5 with fills 21 → 1.6 s, every output byte-identical. Indexing one caller would leave the lattice codes and exact checks slow; caching does not help exact checks at new positions (doc 05 §31)

docs.title: D79 — Plane targets exclude teardrops and unreachable fills
Decision
docs.text: Plane targets: a teardrop zone ((attr (teardrop ...))) is never a target; a fill is a target for a pad only if the pad can reach it (a via type the net may place, or a shared layer the net may use for tracks); with --soft-zones a routed item's contacts with same-net plane fills count in joined

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Leave teardrops to the 1 mm² rule; keep teardrops hard under soft zones; check reachability only for zone-only clusters; credit contacts in default mode too

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Orphaned teardrops are ≥ 1 mm² and became targets on signal nets; teardrops attached to pads were targets in every mode (complex_hierarchy defaults 77 → 84/84, 21 → 3 unconnected after refill). Unreachable planes replaced pad-to-pad connections with failed ones. Hard teardrops had no consistent effect. Default-mode credit would change outputs that are not broken; soft-zone output changes only where planes are. Quick tier byte-identical (doc 05 §32)

docs.title: D80 — Custom-rule conditions follow observed KiCad item sets
Decision
docs.text: Custom-rule conditions follow the observed KiCad 10.0.3 item sets: numeric comparisons in internal units without literal rounding, whole-rule dropping for unknown symbols and a lone unitless numeric literal, typed disallow priority including ignore, own item layers, absolute pad/via positions, exact rounded-core area enclosure and prepared courtyard polygons on the footprint's own front and back sides, with KiCad's reference or library-id footprint selectors. New item-dependent predicates stay DRC-only, with the existing router warning. Rules that use one of the 17 KiCad functions TraceMaker does not evaluate are kept and warned about, the call taken as false as before; \|\| binds tighter than &&; Width exists on tracks only; numeric equality is exact (review with KiCad 10.0.6).

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Port the fork's conservative match on unknown conditions; compare bounding-box corners; substitute the DRC iteration layer; add Clipper2

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The original 61-case corpus had 26 item-set mismatches. Invalid conditions must really be dropped, and geometric equality of counts can hide different items. Existing integer geometry handles concavity, holes and full copper containment without a dependency. Frozen KiCad item/pair multisets live in tests/integration/rule_parity/, exercised by the KiCad-independent rule_parity ctest; deciding cases and regression results are in doc 05 §33.

docs.title: D81 — Named regression board sets with work budgets
Decision
docs.text: Regression runs use named board sets in bench/sets/ (quick, mid, planes) with deterministic work budgets (run.py --work, no knowledge base); plane boards are judged after a KiCad refill (--refill) with the board's project and rules beside the output; bench/compare_runs.py checks the gates of doc 10 §5

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Manifest files and a report generator as first planned; keep sampling by --limit with work budgets passed through TM_ROUTE_ARGS; judge planes on stale fills

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Board lists are the smallest thing that names a tier and survives sampling changes. Work budgets make two runs of one binary byte-identical, so "unchanged" can be checked, not estimated. Stale fills and default rules gave false results on the plane set (hundreds of false errors without the project files). The planned statistics and dashboard are not needed for paired regression checks (doc 10 §4)

docs.title: D82 — Router applies positional disallow rules
Decision
docs.text: The router applies position-, size- and footprint-dependent disallow track/via rules to every new track and via as the DRC judges board items (all rules in order on the actual copper, a via's span telling blind from buried). The exact checks block such copper. The lattice search treats the rules like fixed copper (blocked on the track's copper, "tight" within the margin), outside the per-class caches. Per-net masks stay for position-independent rules.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Keep them DRC-only with a warning (D80); rasterise each rule into per-net lattice masks; fold the verdict into the per-class obstacle codes; a three-valued static evaluation so that positional ignore rules also widen the per-net masks

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Rule 6: the board owner's rules are not to be routed through. Judging the same copper with the same evaluator keeps router and DRC in agreement. Rules may name nets inside one class, so the class codes cannot hold them, and masks per net would multiply the lattice memory. Boards without such rules route byte-identically (quick, mid and planes tiers). Eight PCBench boards with "no vias under ICs" and "bottom clear under front ICs": KiCad items_not_allowed 476 → 0, at the price of completion where the rules close a pin's only exits: mean 97.6 % → 88.8 % at 3M work (doc 05 §34)

docs.title: D83 — tracemaker escape analyses outstanding pins under router rules
Decision
docs.text: tracemaker escape analyses outstanding pins only (nets the existing copper does not complete; complete ones are satisfied), under the router's custom-rule limits (per-net layers and vias, positional disallow rules) and its zone and via options (--soft-zones, --keep-vias-off-pads). Dead pins that escape without the rules are named as walled in by them

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Port the fork's shared off-lattice access graph with witness/exhausted/unknown verdicts (D66 there); keep analysing every pin against hard fills

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The analysis feeds preflight and dead_pins: it must ask the router's question. Retained fills made 18 CM5 pins look dead that soft-zone routing connects. The access graph was dropped with its router half; the lattice search is complete over its domain, so dead keeps its meaning, qualified by the reported lattice (doc 05 §35)

docs.title: D84 — Board-prep and route guidance as agent skills
Decision
docs.text: Board preparation and routing guidance ship as two agent skills in skills/ (tracemaker-board-prep with a stdlib preflight.py, tracemaker-route with a stdlib signoff.py), installable with npx skills add. Rule findings come from tracemaker drc's diagnostics, the preflight's own vocabulary only when the binary is absent; the escape check uses the suggested route's zone and via options; sign-off judges both boards beside the input's project files. For connections the route leaves open the route skill goes through more search first, then the stuck report, and only then an advice file that the agent writes itself (D109's channel with the agent as the advisor), and says that the measured gain of hints is none (doc 17 §8); a test checks that every option the skills name exists in the engine's commands

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Document the advice only in docs/; reimplement the rule engine's vocabulary in the preflight; judge the routed file where it lies

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Speed and legality depend on project settings users do not see (an unused fine class, a cache-disabling rule, stale fills after deleting routing). The engine is the authority on which rules it applies. KiCad finds a board's project by file name: judged where it lies, a routed StickHub showed 449 false added errors (track_width, clearance, edge) against 1 with its project

docs.title: D85 — In-engine exact zone refill for judging
Decision
docs.text: Zones are refilled in the engine for judging (drc --refill-zones, routing with --soft-zones): exact polygons with Clipper2 following KiCad 10's fillCopperZone, connectivity judged on them by the existing code; teardrop zones dropped as kicad-cli's forced teardrop update does; with --soft-zones the route job refills, counts and routes the remaining connections once more with the refilled fills fixed (same budget as the first pass, --no-refill-repair to only count). The fills are not written

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: A raster fill (no dependency, approximate at thin necks, never writable); keep calling kicad-cli; split the soft-zone budget between the passes

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The engine's connectivity already matched KiCad's on 16 of 16 routed plane boards; only the fills were missing. Exact fills reach the same unconnected items per net as kicad-cli on all 16 and on 191 of 200 PCBench boards (the rest are KiCad 5 files with duplicate zone ids and one target item). The repair took the plane set from 119 to 95 unconnected at 3 M + 3 M work units, against 103 for 6 M without it. Clipper2 was already the planned polygon library (doc 02)

docs.title: D86 — Reported route time covers the whole job
Decision
docs.text: A route job's reported seconds covers the whole job, every portfolio variant included (variant_seconds and variants keep the per-variant times); bench/run.py with --work gives each board the cores per job (at most 8) as router threads

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Keep reporting the winner's time; fewer variants or successive halving to cut the time

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: With --work all eight variants run whatever the thread count, and one thread ran them in series: the reported time was 1/5 to 1/8 of the process (doc 10 §6). More threads leave the output byte-identical (D47) and cut a board's wall time by 66–74 % at four threads; fewer variants change results

docs.title: D88 — Per-phase work counters and route CPU time
Decision
docs.text: The router counts its work per phase (expansions, flood cells, searches, cell and fixed-copper checks, cost-field cells, commits, rips) and reports it in the route JSON; bench/run.py records each route's CPU time, and compare_runs.py reports CPU changes at equal work beyond the noise band of the byte-identical boards. The --work budget is unchanged. Quality is judged at equal work, speed at equal wall time (doc 10 §5, gate 5)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: A work budget weighted by calibrated per-operation costs; weights fitted at build time; CPU time as a gate

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Counting is deterministic and explains where a budget went. Weighted work narrows the gap between work and time but cannot close it: the cost field took 3 s on Metal and 13 s on the CPU for the same board, so no single set of weights is time-faithful on every platform, and each re-fit shifts every stored result. Weights fitted per build would make output depend on the machine. CPU time is too noisy for a gate: byte-identical boards moved +9 % to +14 % between two runs (doc 10 §6)

docs.title: D89 — Terminal options screen and options file
Decision
docs.text: Route options can be chosen on a terminal screen (tracemaker tui) and kept in an options file (route --config FILE, name = value lines; the command line wins). The screen lists the options from the command-line definitions themselves; its choices and a file's lines are turned into arguments and parsed again like typed ones. Plain termios and ANSI sequences, no new dependency (issue #18)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: A hand-written list of options for the screen; ncurses or FTXUI; CLI11's own config-file support; applying a file's values directly to the option variables

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: A second list would fall behind the sixty-odd options; reading the definitions cannot. One screen of rows, a filter and a prompt does not need a UI library, and a dependency would have to exist in CI and on macOS. CLI11 (2.5) did not read a config file given to a subcommand: the file was ignored without a message. Re-parsing gives a file's values the same checks and conversions as typed ones and makes "the command line wins" a matter of leaving out what was typed (doc 02 §2.1)

docs.title: D90 — Simple Route JSON supported at the edge only
Decision
docs.text: Simple Route JSON (tscircuit's routing-problem format) is supported at the edge only: srj-import writes a problem as a self-contained KiCad board with its project and rules, the unchanged pipeline routes and judges it, and srj-export writes the routed copper back as SRJ traces. Nets follow tscircuit's own connectivity grouping; rules the problem does not state are absent, not KiCad's defaults. The BGA breakout sets srj19 and srj20 run in bench/run.py with KiCad's DRC as the judge at the distances of tscircuit's published pass criterion (0.1 mm copper, 0.1 mm via hole to via hole), and bench/srj_score.py adds tscircuit's own checker on the exported solution as a second score (doc 08 §9, doc 10 §7)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: An SRJ model inside the engine; routing SRJ rectangles directly; tscircuit's checker as the only judge; a re-implementation of its checker

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: One board model and one exact check stay the source of truth, and KiCad remains the judge every other number in the project uses, so the SRJ figures are comparable with them. A converter is small and testable by counting (problem connections = KiCad ratsnest = router connections on all 400 problems). Running tscircuit's checker itself, pinned, avoids arguing about an imitation; it is a second score because it has no say on what KiCad checks and reports some collinear tracks of different nets as touching when they are not

docs.title: D91 — Bus routing inside the existing search
Decision
docs.text: Buses are routed inside the existing search, not by a second router (doc 05 §38, opt-in: --bus NAME=PATTERN, --buses, --bus-skew-mm, --bus-first). A group's connections between two components are routed one after the other in pin order; each is searched inside a guide around the neighbour lane routed before it (same layers along its tracks, any layer at its vias) and kept only with the neighbour's layers, as many vias and a bounded detour; otherwise it is routed freely and reported as having left the bus. Nets outside the groups do not rip a group (as --first-nets). A bundle stays where the router's order put its first connection. Skew matching uses the length-tuning meanders, with a limit only from a custom skew rule or the option; tracemaker buses measures any routed board

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: A coupled multi-track search like the pair router's (state space grows with the lane count; pins are not at lane pitch); the global router's corridors or the per-net layer masks as the carrier (corridors are per tile of eight pitches and belong to the global plan; a mask holds for the whole net, not per stretch: the guide is the corridor test on lattice cells); buses first by default (four dense mid boards routed 11 / 1009, 40 / 1616, 11 / 634, 1 / 410 at 20 M work: kept as --bus-first); ripping a group as a whole, or no protection (936 and 947 against 952 connections on six boards at 100 M); a default skew limit

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Seven generated boards at 20 M work: every group within its limit (0.16–0.35 mm against 0.25–2 mm; 0.56–9.3 mm without), completion equal, no KiCad error added, equal vias per member wherever no member left. Six real boards: 957 → 952 connections at 100 M, 89 → 99 bus nets on their group's vias and layers; 886 → 853 at 20 M. quick byte-identical with the options off

docs.title: D92 — After-route passes: widen power, stitch vias, style metric
Decision
docs.text: Three after-route passes in their own module (src/passes/), off by default: --widen-power widens new tracks towards a stated width only (net class width for neck-downs, --widen-net, a width_for_current rule's width), per track through the router's segment_state, capped at the via or pad a track ends on; --stitch-vias places free through vias of a plane's net against the in-engine refill, on a grid where its fills overlap on two layers and beside the vias of signals that need a reference plane, allowed through the middle of another net's plane but never near its edge, and verified by a second refill; a style metric (bends, acute angles, stair-steps, short and off-angle segments, detour ratio) is measured on every route result and by tracemaker style, informational in the benchmark. Each copper-changing pass is a transaction judged by unconnected items per net (doc 05 §39)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Widening inside the router's clean-up (grows router.cpp, and the clean-up has no notion of targets); widening by moving neighbours (shove) or splitting tracks at tight spots (later, with a benchmark); inventing widths from net names (never: only stated targets); stitching against the stored fills (stale after routing) or with fills as plain obstacles (no via could pass a power plane on a multilayer board); thermal or teardrop handling for vias (KiCad joins vias solidly); making the style metric a clean-up objective now (first measure, then decide)

docs.title: D93 — Options screen with global, project and file scopes
Decision
docs.text: The options screen is a coloured frame with a help panel, and options have scopes: global ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tracemaker/route.conf), project (tracemaker.conf in the board's folder) and the --config file, the higher over the lower. The scope bar shows where edits go (Tab moves it); each value shows its scope; a file holds only its own scope's values. route still reads a file only when --config names it

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Letting route load the global and project files itself; one merged file; a prompt for the path on every save

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: A run that silently depends on a file in the user's home directory is not reproducible from its command line (rule 2), and a second route that finds a tracemaker.conf next to a board would route differently from the same command elsewhere. The screen reads the files to show and edit them and prints the explicit command. Per-scope layers make "reset" and "which file does this value come from" well defined, and saving one scope cannot copy another's values into it (doc 02 §2.1)

docs.title: D94 — Higher rip and pass limits, extra seeded variants
Decision
docs.text: The router's rip limit per connection is 40 and its pass limit 40 (were 8 and 12), and a portfolio may have more than eight variants: --variants N beyond the designed eight adds seeded diversifications (fast bends, jittered order, via and crossing cost cycling, escape plan on every other one, --package-pen 3 on the others)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Keep the old limits; or make the extras the default portfolio (not measured on the whole sets)

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: At 50 M work on the 24 srj19 boards one variant misses, 33 % → 54 % clean; srj19 88.0 % (was 79.5 %) with one variant; quick and mid are byte-identical because their budgets end before the old limits, ctest 253/253. Extra variants gave nothing on one hard srj20 board (24 seeds all 33–40 of 52) but cost nothing when not asked for (doc 16 §10; doc 05 §40)

docs.title: D95 — Unhelpful options kept as hidden flags
Decision
docs.text: Options that were measured and did not help are kept as hidden flags with their results recorded, not deleted: --guide, --layer-assign, --order 3, --lns-open, --no-strict-first, --max-victims, --soft-growth, --history-weight; --package-pen helps a little and is used only in portfolio extras

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Delete them (smaller surface)

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: A flag costs a line in main.cpp and lets the next session repeat or extend the measurement; the results table in doc 16 §10 says what each did, so it is not re-tried blind (doc 16 §10)

docs.title: D96 — SRJ fan-out import options for fanout31
Decision
docs.text: Simple Route JSON fan-out problems (tscircuit's fanout31) are imported with: plane terminations (buses[].termination) as zones, breakout points on the layer connectionExitTargets names, --unpointed-keepout (pads of a net that no connection point lies on are keep-outs), --outline-margin-mm, and the extension field tracemakerTrackLayers (layers outside it get a rule area that forbids tracks and lets vias through). Clearance is the stated track width, 0.08128 mm

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Model the far chip's pads as part of the problem (rejected: it asks for 149 connections the benchmark does not score)

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The problem asks for the fan-out at the SoC only and its nets name the far chip's pads; without these the first case routed 51 of 149 connections, with them 100 of 100. The clearance sits between the stated trace-to-pad 0.05 mm and pad-to-pad 0.1 mm (doc 08 §9; doc 16 §10)

docs.title: D97 — M14 plan as measured outcomes, not a build order
Decision
docs.text: The M14 plan (doc 16) is a plan with measured outcomes, not a design to build in order: hypotheses H1–H5 were tested first, and the build list is what survived. The deciding experiment (E1, tscircuit's own routes as guides) used its router as a measuring instrument only (bun, installed in the scratch area, no tscircuit code enters the engine)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Build the planner first (as the plan listed)

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The experiments showed the topology planner (F1) is not justified by topology alone, and that search effort and negotiation limits were the cheap lever (doc 16 §4, §10)

docs.title: D98 — Automatic preferred directions on breakout boards
Decision
docs.text: On a breakout board (two copper layers, at least 70 % of the connections have an end on a ball-grid-like package: at least 30 same-layer SMD pads on at least 5 × 5 distinct positions, at least 40 % of the grid filled) the router sets --layer-dir-pen 0.3 (even layers prefer horizontal, odd vertical) and --package-pen 3 automatically; either can be set (or 0) explicitly. fanout31 breakout points keep the layer and position written in their connection (no override from connectionExitTargets)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Always on for two-layer boards with a package (rejected: quick 89.2 → 87.7 %, mid 53.5 → 51.1 %)

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Preferred directions: srj20 gap boards 28 → 40 % clean, srj19 gap 46 → 50 %; quick and mid byte-identical with the 70 % rule. The override stacked terminals of different buses on one layer (K230 0/12 → 12/12 without it) (doc 16 §11)

docs.title: D99 — Negotiation as transactions with annealing acceptance
Decision
docs.text: Negotiation runs as transactions (--txn, automatic on breakout boards): a negotiated route that rips victims is kept only if the victims can be re-routed strictly and the net change in routed connections is at least zero; otherwise a snapshot of every connection's copper is restored (history stays). A loss of k connections is kept with probability exp(−k/T), T = 1.5 (--txn-temp), drawn from a seeded counter-based stream. Nested transactions, several victim orders, victim re-route caps, a cooling schedule, tidy sweeps and stall restarts were measured and are not used (hidden options)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Plain rip-up and re-route (before); greedy acceptance only; nested ejection chains; depth-limited victim counts

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Plain negotiation oscillates (the routed count wobbles ±5 for the whole budget); greedy transactions climb but stop one connection short on 14 of 57 boards; annealing acceptance finishes some of them. 57 srj20 gap boards at 30 M: completion 90.9 → 95.5 %, clean 23 → 23–24 (T 1–2); at 100 M clean 28 → 36. No DRC error added on any run; rollback is exact (tests/test_txn.cpp)

docs.title: D100 — Breakout profile reach-check and field caching
Decision
docs.text: The breakout profile (D98's trigger) also sets --reach-check 2, --flood-work-pct 25 (a flood cell counts a quarter of an expansion against --work), --field-prefill 1 and --field-cache-mb 512; --breakout-profile 0 turns the last four off. The fixed-copper cache is filled for the whole board at the first field, so a cost-to-go field is a function of its connection and window only and is kept; reuse is checked by a byte comparison of the inputs

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Flood cells at 1:1 (as before); lazy cache; a field per search

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: A flood cell costs far less time than an expansion (transactions + reach-check 2: 30 of 57 clean at 30 M against 23, at 137 s against 106 s CPU per board); the field was 47 % of the time of a transaction run and its inputs repeat (62 % of the wall time on sample 123, same copper). Not byte-identical on ordinary boards (6 of 30 quick boards differ), hence breakout boards only

docs.title: D101 — Breakout portfolio with warm-started rounds
Decision
docs.text: Portfolio on a breakout board (--variants > 1): variant 0 is the plain breakout profile, the others draw order, via cost, crossing cost, direction strength, package penalty and temperature from fixed sets with a counter-based generator (--breakout-portfolio 0 restores the designed eight); --rounds R splits the budget into R rounds, and after each every variant continues from the best result so far (warm start by connection)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: The designed eight (exact bends, longest first, 2× pitch variants); independent variants only

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Variants of the designed list are wrong for breakouts (fast bends and shortest first win; longest first routes 5 against 7 of 76); rounds point all search at the best state. See doc 16 §12 for the measurements

docs.title: D102 — Portfolio search state saved and resumable
Decision
docs.text: Portfolio runs save their search state: --state-out F writes the best routes (per connection, keyed by pad pair) after every round, atomically; --state-in F starts from them (warm start, seeds continue the sequence); bench/run.py always passes --state-out <board>.state and --resume-run NAME resumes from an earlier run

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Keep only the final KiCad output (not resumable: connections cannot be recovered from copper)

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Runs of 3 h per board that end open should be continuable later; a crash or kill loses at most one round. Test: saved state in tests/test_txn.cpp

docs.title: D103 — Clearance continuation ramp with warm starts
Decision
docs.text: Clearance continuation: --ramp-from C0 --ramp-step S --ramp-rounds N [--ramp-cycle K --ramp-stall M] runs the portfolio rounds under clearances lowered by (board - c) for c = C0, C0+S, … below the board's, each stage warm-started from the previous routes that are legal under its rules (--state-recheck: legal against fixed copper, then greedy vertex cover of the conflict graph, then the strict exact check); the last stage and the returned result are always under the board's rules, and with --ramp-cycle the last stage can go back K stages when it stalls ("breathing")

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Route straight at the board's rules (plateau at 1–6 open on six srj20 boards after hours); tighten the rules in the router itself without staged warm starts

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: At the board's rules the search from scratch stalls although solutions exist (sample048 completes at 0.085 mm when warm-started from the 0.06/0.07 solutions, 30 min from scratch at 0.08 leave one open); the solution at 0.085 uses only 4 double-used via gaps and 43 % of the top pad gaps, so the plateau is search, not capacity. Test: clearance ramp (two cases) in tests/test_txn.cpp

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Relax, route, legalise: route/legalize.{hpp,cpp} moves the vertices of routed tracks and vias (topology fixed) until the clearances of the board's rules hold, by Gauss-Seidel projection over the pairs that are too close; --legalize applies it to every warm start (--warm-pcb, --state-in, ramp stages), --relax = ramp at 60 % and 80 % of the clearance with legalisation and breathing between the stages, until complete

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Route at the board's rules on the lattice only; a sequential-LP compaction (HiGHS) in the engine

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: At 0.06 mm all six stuck srj20 boards complete in minutes, and their solutions can be made legal at 0.10 mm by moving vertices (071, 039, 103, 048 complete at the true rules, KiCad DRC clean, after hours of scratch search at 72-76 of 74-78); the lattice wastes room it cannot use. Projection needs no LP solver and gave about the same as the LP prototype. Only routes that pass the exact check are kept, so legality does not depend on the heuristic. Tests: legalisation and clearance ramp cases in tests/test_txn.cpp

docs.title: D105 — Layerless legacy fills inherit the zone's sole layer
Decision
docs.text: A legacy filled_polygon without a layer inherits the zone's sole copper-mask bit; explicit fill layers always win and zero or multiple copper bits leave the fill layer unknown. The lossless document is not changed.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Drop every layerless fill; choose the first zone layer

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: KiCad 5 omits fill-layer tokens for single-layer zones. Dropping them hides real plane copper from obstacle and connectivity checks; guessing on ambiguous zones invents copper.

docs.title: D106 — Benchmark gates compare violation multisets
Decision
docs.text: Native benchmark gates compare physical violation multisets; routing also evaluates error-severity starved_thermal and isolated_copper without requiring a reported track. Placement retains its rigid-single-footprint exclusion, except zone-dependent thermal/island findings. KiCad 10.0.x evaluated error caps are unknown, never clean or a passing comparison; warning-only caps remain diagnostic. Existing completion remains the capped DRC-list ratio, with saturation disclosed separately (doc 10 §4)

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Count deltas by type; ignore all pad/zone-only findings; import an uncapped connectivity worker and change completion here

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: A removed clearance elsewhere cannot excuse a new one; refills can reveal copper damage while naming only pads or zones. Saturated lists cannot prove a zero delta. This isolates error-gate correctness from connectivity metric changes and preserves CLI/report compatibility

docs.title: D107 — Fixture preparation by native conversion and ID repair
Decision
docs.text: Fixture preparation privately converts with version-matched native LoadBoard/SaveBoard before repairing generated/zero/duplicate/missing identities and UUID-dependent item order, then refills and publishes the unrouted board last; source/human boards and rule bytes stay untouched

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Repair IDs after the first refill; strip-only preparation; transplant PCBench quality/thermal-retention machinery

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Native conversion can generate random item IDs or leave legacy zones sharing zero IDs; identity-dependent load order must be stable before native geometry/DRC. Failed preparation removes only its generated runnable artifacts because existing consumers do not read validity manifests. Repeated board/rule bytes, not native report hashes, are the reproducibility contract; fresh paired baselines are required for the changed prepared input (doc 10 §1)

docs.title: D108 — KiCad 10 defaults and legacy migration precedence for rules
Decision
docs.text: Seed supported KiCad 10 defaults, retain missing project keys and explicit zeros, and follow native legacy migration precedence: exact legacy setup triggers suppress project board settings, while legacy net classes independently replace project classes/assignments

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Zero minimums for partial projects; unconditional project-over-legacy overlays; suppression whenever any setup exists

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: KiCad's constructor sets track/via minimums to 0.2/0.5 mm. BOARD::SetProject skips project board-settings loading only after parser-marked legacy design settings and independently migrates root net classes. Native controls and consumer-visible unit tests distinguish rule triggers from local mask fields and verify legal written widths (doc 08 §3.1)

docs.title: D109 — Engine never talks to a model; advice files
Decision
docs.text: The engine never talks to a model. A language model is one possible writer of an advice file (--advice FILE: typed hints, strictly checked, that change only the order of connections, the cost of a layer and where some nets may not go), run by an out-of-process advisor (--advisor CMD: stuck report on stdin, advice on stdout) that is consulted only when the plain route leaves connections open. Advice never contains copper or rule values; unknown keys, wrong types and unknown names are errors

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: An HTTP/TLS client and API keys inside the C++ engine; a separate orchestrator program; letting a model place copper

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The tree has no HTTP client, and a non-repeatable call inside a run that must be byte-identical breaks N3 and rule 2. The model's answer is frozen in a file, so board + options + seed + advice is repeatable. Two tools for one job would leave the report and hint interface, the real work, in the engine anyway (doc 17 §1–§2)

docs.title: D110 — Advised attempts as extra portfolio variants
Decision
docs.text: Advised attempts are extra portfolio variants: the next variants (default 4) entries of the portfolio's list, the ones a plain run with that many more variants would add, carrying the hints and appended after the variants that run anyway with indices 1000 and up (a first version advised copies of variants 0, 2, 4, 6: with a hint that does nothing they repeat work already done, and a plain run with four more variants beat them by 11 connections on the held-out half, doc 17 §8). The winner is the portfolio's total order, so a tie goes to the unadvised variant; in --advisor mode the plain result is kept unless the advised run is strictly better (route_result_better). Each routing run gets the full --work / --time; the advisor's wall time is not routing work

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Applying the advice to every variant; replacing the plain run by the advised one; counting the advisor's time against the budget

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Advice can then only win by routing more (rule 4), and the unadvised variants are untouched (tested), so adding advice cannot cost connections. Against a plain run with the same number of variants the only difference is the hints, which is the comparison that matters. The price is about twice the work in --advisor mode (doc 17 §4, §5)

docs.title: D111 — Advice regions as in-memory rule areas and rules
Decision
docs.text: Advice regions are an in-memory rule area plus disallow track/via rules (doc 05 §34) whose conditions use only && (A.intersectsArea('tmk:advice:N') && A.NetName != 'NET1', or == 'NET3'): "reserve for" or "keep out", per layer, tracks and/or vias. They live in the router's working copy (RouterOptions::extra_zones / extra_rules) and never in the output board or the caller's rules

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: A new obstacle type with a per-net scope in the obstacle caches; keep-out zones (they block every net, so the named ones cannot be exempt)

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: §34 already applies position-dependent rules in the lattice search and in every exact check, outside the per-class caches, and handles nets. KiCad's grammar reads a && b \|\| c as a && (b \|\| c), so no \|\| is generated and "every net but these" is a conjunction of inequalities (doc 17 §4)

docs.title: D112 — Stuck report as part of the route
Decision
docs.text: The stuck report is part of the route: structured RouteResult::Unrouted (reason code, the router's words, rips, fails, pad positions, blocker nets) and a JSON report with the open connections, the crowding of their regions, the parts at their ends, the portfolio's variants, cuts and escape_rings. It carries a disclosure block, is size-limited (40 open connections), and --advisor-redact replaces net and part names by aliases (N1, P3) that are mapped back before the advice is checked. The failure event gets region and blocker_nets

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Sending the board file; sending names unconditionally; waiting for doc 06's closed-set boundary analysis before reporting blockers

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Names from a board are a prompt-injection surface and, sent to a cloud model, a disclosure; the report must say what it holds. The victims of the rejected route are the cheap and true part of "blockers" (doc 17 §3)

docs.title: D113 — failure event explains what rejected the path
Decision
docs.text: A failure event says what rejected the path (issue #8): the attempt's track width, clearance and the narrowest legal width, the bottleneck of the best way from the closest approach (gap_nm with routed copper counted, gap_fixed_nm with only fixed copper), the path that was tried, and a verdict: contested (fixed copper leaves room, routed copper closes the way), rule (a narrower legal track or the board minimum clearance passes), placement (nothing legal passes), unknown when the evidence is incomplete. The gap is a widest-path search over the router's own obstacle tests (doc 13, "The failure verdict"), measured at a connection's 1st, 2nd, 4th, 8th ... failure, with a deterministic budget, and it counts no work

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Measuring the free distance at the blocked lattice neighbour of the closest approach (it measures the approach to a wall, not the gap in it: a 0.3 mm gap with 0.2 mm clearance read 0.14 mm free); re-running the router's own search at other widths (it counts expansions against the work budget and would make a viewer change the run)

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The label has to be a number the lattice would agree with, and a viewer must not change what is routed. The unknown verdict keeps a failed search alone from sending someone to a footprint move or a clearance change (the comment on the issue)

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: The reference-return audit (issue #7) is a read-only geometric pass: copper under each selected trace on its reference layer, and where there is none the return is the shortest path on the remaining reference copper (A* over the visibility graph of the region's vertices), reported as a detour and a separation; a layer change closes through the nearest stitching via of the reference net or the nearest capacitor between the two reference nets, within a radius; a pad's return pad is the nearest pad of the reference net. Selected by net name, class or pair, off by default; thresholds are warnings; after a route the zones are refilled for the new copper

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: A field solver; one assumed ground ball per pin; judging the fills stored in the file after routing (they have no antipads for the new vias); adding the audit to the DRC errors (KiCad has no such rule, and a geometric estimate is not a violation)

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: The issue asks per net for continuous copper and the detour, not for a current-density map. The nearest-pad return and the nearest stitch or capacitor follow the comment on the issue. A geometric estimate with stated limits is useful and honest; presenting it as a violation would not be (doc 05 §42)

docs.title: D115 — Footprint check against trusted datasheet references
Decision
docs.text: The footprint check (issue #5) compares a board's footprints with references: records made from a datasheet (JSON, or the manufacturer's .kicad_mod, with document, revision and page), used only when the reference's brand is on an explicit trusted list. The pattern is aligned by translation and quarter-turn rotation, mirrored only as the footprint's side requires, then pad numbers, positions, sizes, drills and types are compared; every difference is an error. route --footprint-refs runs it before routing and stops on an error unless --footprint-warn-only. Read-only

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Reading datasheet PDFs (a drawing is not data, and an extracted number would itself need checking); fetching land patterns from the network or from a vendor API (an unpinned, unvouched source); a built-in list of trusted brands applied silently (whose datasheets to believe is the user's call; a starting list is shipped to copy); comparing courtyard, silkscreen, paste or mask; treating an untrusted reference as a verdict

docs.title: Reason
