  • Let the router flash layers it reaches, as KiCad would. Correct, but the commit check would need to rebuild a via's shape as tracks arrive; four fixture boards use the option and none is in a bench tier.
  • Leave the tuning-pattern and parallel quirks out. Each changes vme-wren's verdicts, and both are small.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• vme-wren: 425 clearance and 20 shorting reports left (other causes, listed in the records), and all 28 gap and 6 uncoupled-length errors are KiCad's. jetson still matches. The eight B1/B2 pair-rule boards route byte for byte as before.
  • Rule parity: 234 cases, three new (via_unused_layers, diff_pair_tuning_pattern, diff_pair_near_parallel), all matching KiCad. The D149 build fails the three.
  • Assumption A92 records the router's stricter rule.
  • Still open on vme-wren: fromTo() (34 length errors), the pad-to-track rule resolution, copper-graphic shorts, and a 10-minute DRC.

docs.title: D151 — Clearances resolved in KiCad's order; copper graphics compared as KiCad compares their nets
Context
docs.text:
After D150, vme-wren still had 425 clearance and 20 shorting reports from the engine's DRC that KiCad 10.0.6 does not make:

  • Clearance. The engine floored every clearance at the board minimum (0.125 mm), but the board's custom rule allows 0.1 mm under the FPGA and the DDR. KiCad's DRC_ENGINE::EvalRules returns a matching custom rule's value before the board-minimum floor, and checks a pad's local override before any custom rule.
  • Shorting. These were between shapes of one footprint: copper lines that meet in the outline of each U.FL connector. In KiCad a footprint's copper shape has no net at all (PCB_SHAPE::IsConnected) and nets are compared by pointer, so two footprint shapes are never tested against each other, and neither are two board-level items without a net.

Doc 08 §3.2, records in bench/records/d151-clearance.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• RuleEngine::clearance in KiCad's order:
  • a local override (pad, then footprint), floored at the board minimum;
  • else the last matching custom rule, final with no floor;
  • else the net class, with the coupled-pair relaxation and a zone's own clearance, floored at the board minimum.
  • hole_clearance and hole_to_hole: a matching custom rule replaces the board minimum instead of being raised to it.
  • Copper graphics:
  • two footprint graphics (of one footprint or of two) are not checked against each other;
  • a board graphic is not checked against another board item without a net (graphic, pad, track or via).
  • Hole names: a hole without copper is named "NPTH pad of " in reports, as KiCad names it, and is listed in its hole_clearance reports.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
• Keep the floor as a safety margin. The router would keep 0.125 mm where the designer allowed 0.1 mm under a BGA. Fan-outs there need the rule, and the DRC would keep reporting errors that KiCad does not.
  • Port KiCad's pointer and UUID-order logic for graphics in full. Whether an overlap is a short or a clearance error depends on which of the two items has the larger UUID, and the engine keeps no UUIDs. The two rules above are the ones the fixtures need.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• vme-wren matches KiCad on every routing-relevant type, and jetson still does. Of the other 15 demo boards 12 match as before; microwave's shorts go from 10 to 8 (KiCad 6), One-Air-Max and RoyalBlue differ as before.
  • Rule parity: 239 cases, five new, all matching KiCad. The D149 build fails all five.
  • Among the fixtures only vme-wren has a rule below its board minimum, and no board with custom clearance rules has local overrides, so no bench board routes differently.
  • On merge with D139 (branch cache-safe-custom-rules), its check that the per-class cache judges custom rules as the exact check does must use this order.

docs.title: D152 — Delay tuning rips the routed connections a meander needs and routes them again
Context
docs.text:
With D139 (custom rules keep the per-class cache), RoyalBlue54L-Feather-delay routes 125 of 147 connections instead of 119, but KiCad reports one more error: skew_out_of_range on the USB pair /Debugger/D+ and D-, 2.69 ps against the 0.5 ps rule usb_pair_skew (within_diff_pairs). D+ leaves the connector about 8.6 ps short of D-. The tuner (doc 05 §59) adds meanders only where nothing else is: here its 1.5 to 0.4 mm meanders were blocked by the extra routed connections. The free room took only 0.25 mm meanders, and D+ stopped at 76.8 of 79.5 ps. One of the router's eight variants tuned the pair, but it was not the best one.

Doc 05 §61, records in bench/records/d152-room.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Router::tune_with_room, used by tune_delays for each net with a ps length window and for each net brought to its group's or pair's delay:

  1. The plain tuner runs first. If the net is in range, nothing else happens.
  2. Otherwise the board goes back to the untuned net and the tuner runs again. At each meander height, after both free sides, it tries each side that only routed copper of other nets blocks (Obstacles::segment_state, rippable owners). It rips those connections and places the meander. A connection may be ripped only if it is routed, not implicit, not coupled, not a bus or bundle lane, of another net and not the pair partner, and its net has no length, ps or mm skew rule. At most 16 connections are ripped.
  3. The ripped connections, and any connections of their nets that lose their implicit route, are routed again strictly, in connection order, each with the transaction cap (txn_cap, else 200,000 expansions). This happens after the search budget is spent, so they get 400,000 work units of their own (with --time, 2 % of the time limit).
  4. The result is kept only if the net is in range and every one of them routes again. Otherwise the board goes back to the plain attempt's result, as before.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
• Rip by proximity. Rip every connection within a meander's height of the net's tracks, then tune. Tried first. It never helped on RoyalBlue: the plain tuner had already filled the free room with small meanders. In the room it left, fixed copper blocked the last 0.22 mm one.
  • Tune before the late routes go in. Tuning runs once, on the best state at the end. Tuning each variant at its own end, or before clean-up, would change every board with a length rule. It would also not stop later routes from taking the room.
  • Keep D139 without the fix. One KiCad error more on a board with a 0.5 ps rule.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• RoyalBlue54L-Feather-delay: 125/147, no added KiCad errors (main: 119/147, none). One connection is ripped and routed again; D+ is tuned to 79.43 ps against D-'s 79.49 ps. The other three B2 boards never reach the room step. New test delay_room: it skips without the prepared demos.
  • The tuner can now change routed connections of other nets. Each change is an ordinary strict route, checked exactly, and kept only if all of them route again.
  • Only delay tuning makes room. tune_lengths (mm windows), tune_skew (mm pair skew) and the bus tuner do not (open).

docs.title: D154 — Late reachability proof on long strict searches, and speed-ups that keep the output
Context
docs.text: A speed review (doc 05 §62, records in bench/records/d154-speed) profiled five hard PCBench boards with gprof, one variant at 20 M work. The A* loop took 27–57 % of CPU, CPU cost-to-go fields 14–33 %. Every board spent its whole budget in the strict first pass, and most of it went to a few failed searches: 77 % of logicbone's budget (15 searches), 84 % of sbc's (108), 91 % of kitspace_d20's (60). Most of those failures exhaust a region from which no path exists. The pre-check of doc 05 §13 proves that cheaply, but run before every strict search (--reach-check 2) it also floods every search that would succeed in a few hundred expansions. On LeeChee_1800, 28 % of the run was the exact inside-board test against a 572-edge outline. The per-class obstacle caches held a full board lattice per class: 1.6 GB per router on Teensy_test_layout.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Late reachability proof, on by default: RouterOptions::reach_after = 100,000 and reach_after_cap = 10,000 (--reach-after, --reach-after-cap; 0 turns it off or removes the cap). A strict search to a pad that has expanded reach_after states, and had no pre-check, floods forward from its sources and backward from its targets, a cell in turn, over the pre-check's moves. The backward flood follows the reverse of each forward move. When one flood runs out before they meet, there is no path: the search stops as an enclosure ("boxed in", or "boxed in (target)" for the target end) or as a window miss when that region touched the window edge. When they meet, or the floods have visited reach_after_cap cells, the A* continues unchanged. Flood cells are charged at flood_work_pct. --reach-verify covers the proof too.
  2. Same output, less time or memory:
  3. The CPU field sweeps a row at a time and is vectorised (field_cpu; the old sweeps are field_cpu_reference, compared in a test).
  4. The inside-board test reads only the edges of the point's raster row (Obstacles::inside_exact, reference inside_exact_linear, compared in a test).
  5. The per-class caches are LazyCodes, allocated in 4,096-code chunks on first write.
  6. A search's target marks live in a reused buffer.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
• --reach-check 2 everywhere. Doc 05 §13 already measured it: swings both ways, because successful searches pay for the flood. The late proof leaves searches that end within 100,000 expansions alone.
  • No flood cap. It loses on Teensy (1,090 → 1,080 at 20 M) and LeeChee (1,010 → 991). On those boards long searches do succeed, and their floods met only after ~70,000 cells.
  • Earlier trigger (30,000 or 50,000). Without the cap, 30,000 lost 115 connections on LeeChee. With the cap, 50,000 matched 100,000 except on sbc (345 against 341) and cost more CPU on LeeChee.
  • Field only for long searches (--field-after), off. Field time fell, but total CPU rose (LeeChee 18.3 → 25.6 s), because the octile phase spreads over more cells and their legality checks.
  • Ties to the deeper state (--tie-deep), off. Mixed: sbc 341 → 333, Teensy 1,093 → 1,095.
  • -O3 with LTO. About 1 %.
  • A vector heap of structs for the open list. 4–8 % slower than std::priority_queue of pairs, so the queue stays and its container is used for the re-key.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Measured (doc 05 §62):

  • Quick tier (1 M work): byte-identical on 30/30 boards, with 22 % less route CPU.
  • Mid tier (20 M work, 8 variants): 7/11 boards byte-identical, and the other four route as many or more (EEZ +21, decelerator +10, LimeSDR +3, logicbone equal). Route CPU falls 29 %.
  • One variant: the old router needs 1.4× (logicbone) to 2.6× (kitspace_d20) the CPU time to reach the same routed count.
  • Wall clock: at 60 s with 8 variants, the mid tier routes 9,349 → 9,401. At 120 s, tier B is clean 29 → 29 and routes 5,197 → 5,198; tier C is clean 16 → 17 and routes 9,529 → 9,537. Route CPU is 4–5 % lower: the boards that finish early mostly finish sooner.
  • Memory: per router, 1.6 → 0.56 GB on Teensy and 1.65 → 0.44 GB on logicbone.
  • Global router: a LeeChee --global run went from 158 s to 7.5 s, which explains doc 05 §19's set-up wart.

The proof covers strict searches only; negotiated (soft) searches and breakout boards (pre-check on every strict search) do not use it. Docs changed: 05 (§19, §62), 07 (§5 field row).

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text:
The design documents: what TraceMaker is meant to do, how it does it, and why, with the papers each algorithm comes from cited where it is defined. They are the source of truth for the design: when the code has to differ, the document changes in the same pull request, with a decision record.

Read them in this order the first time:

Document What it explains Requirements What the product must do, its scope, success criteria and glossary Architecture Processes, the pipeline, threading, determinism, the repository layout Data structures and DRC Geometry, spatial indices, search structures, the exact design-rule check Placement Optimality levels; analytic placement, legalisation, annealing, exact windows, ECO moves Routing The routing stages, the escalation ladder, the cost model, and every routing feature since Failure memory Learning from failed attempts: records, nogoods, history, bandits, the knowledge base GPU acceleration What runs on the GPU, the kernels, and how CPU and GPU give identical results KiCad integration File I/O, kicad-cli, the plugin, the DRC judge Live viewer Streaming, replay and the visual design of the browser viewer Benchmarking Datasets, metrics, baselines, the harness and the gates

Studies and features with a document of their own:

Document Status Placement test plan How placement is tested: levels, datasets, metrics, gates Component-aware rules Partly built (M13 P0–P3): detect parts such as USB, crystals and regulators, and apply their layout rules BGA breakout Partly built (M14, M15): matching tscircuit on its BGA breakout sets, with measured outcomes Advice files and advisors Partly built (M16, stages 0–3): hints for the router when it is stuck; the engine never talks to a model Agent interface Partly built (M18, stages A–B): a board session an agent drives over MCP or JSON lines

Background, outside this site: the routing-stage design and the Freerouting evidence it rests on (cpp_autorouter_clean_sheet.md), a survey of placement and routing approaches (pcb-routing-optimization.md), and verified facts on KiCad, its APIs, benchmark sets and GPU techniques (research/).

docs.title: How-to guides
docs.text:
Recipes for one job each, for people who already know what they want to do.

  • Build and test: presets, compilers, sanitizers, which tests skip and why.
  • Run kicad-cli from Docker: KiCad's DRC without installing KiCad.
  • Use the GPUs: check, choose and share devices; build for CUDA 12.
  • Read a run report: what a route did, what is open and why, and where each number comes from.
  • Fetch boards and run benchmarks: fixture sets, the quick tier, tiers A–D, keeping records.
  • Make a release: measure, bump, tag, publish.
  • Write and publish the docs: this site, decision records, generated pages, the C++ API.

docs.title: Fetch boards and run benchmarks
docs.text: The method, the sets and the gates are explained in Benchmarking; the results kept so far are in Benchmark results. This page is the recipe.

docs.title: Fetch the boards
docs.text:
scripts/fetch_fixtures.sh                 # freerouting, dac2020, kicad-demos, derived (about 2.4 GB), once
scripts/fetch_fixtures.sh tscircuit       # tscircuit's BGA breakout problems (srj19, srj20)
scripts/fetch_fixtures.sh pcbworld        # PCBWorld-Bench
python3 bench/check_env.py                # what is there and what is missing

The boards go to bench/data/, which git ignores. They are never committed: about half of them state no licence. The default sets are pinned to the commits the published results were measured on; TM_FIXTURES=latest takes upstream's current state instead. PCBench (1,158 boards, each with .kicad_pcb and .dsn) ends up in bench/data/freerouting/scripts/benchmark/fixtures/PCBench.

docs.title: The quick tier
docs.text:
Run it before finishing any change to routing or placement:

python3 bench/run.py --set quick --work 1000000 --route-args "--variants 1" --jobs 4 --name my-change-quick

Thirty PCBench tier-A boards with a deterministic work budget, about 30 s. Compare with a run of the unchanged program on the same machine; no board may get worse in clean pass or completion (doc 10 §5). For changes to search, plans or rip-up also run --set mid --work 20000000.

docs.title: Tiers A–D (release numbers)
docs.text:
python3 bench/run.py --tier B --limit 40 --time 120 --threads 8 --jobs 2 --name my-run-tierB

--limit 40 for A and B, 30 for C and 40 for D (the whole tier, 22 boards), with the default seed 1, give the same boards as the release records. Without --limit the default of 50 picks a different set.

Timed runs depend on machine load. A loaded machine can halve the search steps in 120 s. To tell a regression from load, run the previous release's binary beside the new one at the same time (the release 0.10.0 record shows how).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Each run writes bench/results/<run>/ (git-ignored): the routed boards, boards.jsonl with one result per board, report.md and summary.json with set, boards, clean_pass, completion and seconds, which the progress dashboard shows. python3 bench/compare_runs.py <run> <run> compares two runs board by board.

The judge is kicad-cli 10.0.6: a board is clean when every connection is made and no physical violation was added against the input board (D106). A board is unknown, never clean, when an error type is at KiCad's report cap before or after.

docs.title: Keep the results
docs.text:
bench/results/ is not in the repository. Before a milestone or a change is called done, copy what it rests on into bench/records/<name>/: the run folders' summary.json, boards.jsonl and report.md, the option or advice files used, test output, and a README.md with the tables and what they mean. Then regenerate the results page:

python3 scripts/gen_reference.py bench

Report losses as plainly as gains, and say what was not measured.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
cmake --preset release && cmake --build --preset release      # with CUDA 12.x
cmake --preset cpu-only && cmake --build --preset cpu-only    # without CUDA

The programs land in build/<preset>/src/app/tracemaker, build/<preset>/src/place/tracemaker-place and build/<preset>/src/server/tracemaker-view.

Preset What it is release Optimised, CUDA kernels for sm_60 and sm_70 cpu-only Optimised, no CUDA. Results are identical to release debug No optimisation, CUDA asan, tsan AddressSanitizer + UBSan, ThreadSanitizer. Python bindings are off in these (D18) dist The release binaries: no CUDA, static libstdc++, SQLite and zstd, no tests (scripts/make_release.py) macos-metal, macos-cpu Apple silicon, with or without the Metal backend (contributed, not run by the project)

scripts/bootstrap.sh configures, builds and tests release, cpu-only and asan in one go.

docs.title: Compilers
docs.text:
The presets do not fix the compilers. CMakeLists.txt takes the newest of /usr/bin/g++-15, -14, -13 for C++ and /usr/bin/g++-13 or -12 for CUDA host code (nvcc 12.4 rejects GCC 14 and newer). To choose your own:

CXX=/path/to/g++ cmake --preset release                        # or -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=...
TM_CUDA_HOST_CXX=/path/to/g++-13 cmake --preset release        # or -DCMAKE_CUDA_HOST_COMPILER=...

On the development machine

g++ on the user's PATH is a Nix toolchain whose linker cannot see the system CUDA libraries. Do not export CXX to it; the presets put /usr/bin first on PATH for this reason.

Stay on CUDA 12.x: CUDA 13 cannot compile for the Pascal (P100) and Volta (V100) GPUs.

Warnings are errors (-Wall -Wextra -Werror), and the sanitizer presets must stay green.

docs.title: Test
docs.text:
ctest --preset release                 # 391 tests, about 20 minutes
ctest --preset release -R route        # only tests whose name matches
ctest --preset asan                    # memory errors; its integration tests are slow
  • Tests that need a benchmark board, kicad-cli or a GPU skip (exit code 77) when it is missing; they never fail for that reason. Get the boards with scripts/fetch_fixtures.sh (benchmarks) and kicad-cli from Docker (kicad-cli from Docker).
  • After the first build, run scripts/fetch_fixtures.sh derived once more to build the placement test set.
  • Unit tests use Catch2 and live next to the code (src/<module>/test_*.cpp) or in tests/. Integration tests are scripts in tests/integration/, registered in tests/CMakeLists.txt.
  • A test with a work budget must not depend on wall-clock time: pass --time 3600 with --work, or a slow build stops early and fails for the wrong reason.
  • Every accelerated path (GPU, spatial index) has a test that compares it with its reference path.

docs.title: Before you finish a change
docs.text:
• ctest --preset release passes.
  • A change to routing or placement runs the quick benchmark tier and reports the result, good or bad (benchmarks).
  • A change to the design updates its doc and adds a decision record in the same change.

docs.title: Write and publish the docs
docs.text: This site is built with MkDocs and the Material theme from the Markdown in docs/, and published to GitHub Pages by CI (D134). Every page also reads correctly on GitHub.

docs.title: Preview locally
docs.text:
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
.venv/bin/mkdocs serve                      # http://127.0.0.1:8000, reloads on save
.venv/bin/mkdocs build --strict             # what CI runs: any broken link or missing page fails

docs.title: Where a page goes
docs.text:
The site follows Diátaxis: decide what the reader is doing, and the place follows.

The reader wants to… Kind Folder learn by doing, step by step tutorial docs/tutorials/ get one job done how-to guide docs/how-to/ look up a fact reference docs/reference/ (generate it from the code where possible) understand how and why explanation the numbered design docs, docs/NN-name.md

The numbered design docs keep their names and stay in docs/, because code, commits and issues cite them as "doc 05 §34" and docs/05-routing.md. A new design doc takes the next number. Add every new page to nav in mkdocs.yml and to the index page of its section.

docs.title: The page header
docs.text:
Every page except the decision records and the generated pages starts with:

---
status: current          # current | partly-built | plan | historical
code: [src/route, src/passes]   # the code the page describes; [] for none
reviewed: 2026-10-21     # optional: when someone last checked the page against the code
---

The site shows a banner on pages that are not current. scripts/docs_check.py (run by CI) fails on a missing or wrong header and warns when a page's code has had more than 25 commits since the page last changed or was reviewed. When it warns, read the page against the code, fix what is wrong, and set reviewed to today's date.

docs.title: Links
docs.text: Link to other pages with relative paths to the .md file ([routing](https://github.com/DingoOz/TraceMaker/blob/main/docs/how-to/05-routing.md#5-cost-model)), as GitHub does. Links to files outside docs/ (../src/route/router.cpp, ../PLAN.md) are fine: on the site they are pointed at the file on GitHub by scripts/mkdocs_hooks.py.

docs.title: Record a decision
docs.text:
A design decision is a record in docs/decisions/, one file each:

scripts/decisions.py new "Short title in plain words" --docs 05,10

It takes the next free number, fills in the template (Context, Decision, Alternatives, Consequences) and updates the index in docs/12-decisions.md. Edit the file it prints. When a later decision replaces an earlier one, set the earlier record's status: superseded and superseded_by: DNNN, then run scripts/decisions.py index. scripts/decisions.py check (CI) verifies the records and that the index is up to date.

A branch started before the records existed may still append a row to the old table in docs/12-decisions.md. scripts/decisions.py import --title D132="Short title" turns such rows into records.

docs.title: Generated pages
docs.text:
Page Made by When to run it Command line scripts/gen_reference.py cli --build build/release after changing an option or its help text Benchmark results scripts/gen_reference.py bench after adding a record to bench/records/ Decision index scripts/decisions.py index new does it; after editing a record's title or status C++ API mkdir -p build/api && doxygen docs/api/Doxyfile not committed; CI builds it

CI fails when a committed generated page differs from what the script makes now.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text:
.github/workflows/docs.yml builds the site on every pull request that touches the docs (strict, plus the checks above) and publishes with mike to the gh-pages branch:

  • a push to main publishes version dev;
  • a tag vX.Y.Z publishes version X.Y and points latest (the default) at it.

The Doxygen reference is built in the same job and published under api/ of each version. GitHub Pages must be set to deploy from the gh-pages branch (repository Settings > Pages), once.

docs.title: Use the GPUs
docs.text: TraceMaker runs without a GPU and gives the same results with one: the GPU computes cost-to-go fields (and, in the placer, the density and annealing work) faster, but never decides what is legal (decision D5). Every kernel has a CPU reference and a test that both agree bit for bit (GPU acceleration).

docs.title: Check what it sees
docs.text:
build/release/src/app/tracemaker gpu-info

It lists each device with its name, UUID and the memory it may use. A cpu-only build prints This build has no GPU support (cpu-only). CPU reference paths are used.

docs.title: Choose devices
docs.text:
The router uses the GPU when the build has CUDA and a device has memory free. --no-gpu computes everything on the CPU. The placer is the other way round: its --gpu option turns the GPU on.

Choose devices by UUID, never by index: CUDA orders the fastest device first (the V100 is device 0 on the development machine), while nvidia-smi lists the P100 first.

nvidia-smi -L                                         # names and UUIDs
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=GPU-xxxxxxxx-... build/release/src/app/tracemaker route board.kicad_pcb -o out.kicad_pcb

docs.title: Shared GPUs
docs.text: The development machine's GPUs are shared with other jobs (a llama-server has held nearly all their memory). TraceMaker treats GPU memory as scarce: a failed allocation or kernel falls back to the CPU with the same result, and the route summary counts the fallbacks (fields 0 GPU + 34 CPU ... 0 GPU fallbacks). Tests must pass with no GPU available; do not stop other people's jobs to free memory.

docs.title: Building for CUDA
docs.text: CUDA 12.x only (CUDA 13 dropped Pascal and Volta). nvcc 12.4 rejects GCC 14 and 15 as host compiler, so CUDA host code is built with g++-13 or g++-12 while the rest uses GCC 15 (Build and test).

docs.title: Run kicad-cli from Docker
docs.text:
KiCad's design-rule check is the judge of every benchmark (decision D8). When KiCad is not installed, scripts/kicad-cli runs kicad-cli from the kicad/kicad:10.0.6 Docker image instead.

docker pull kicad/kicad:10.0.6
scripts/kicad-cli version
scripts/kicad-cli pcb drc --format json -o drc.json board.kicad_pcb

To call it as plain kicad-cli, which the tests and bench/run.py look for, put scripts/ on your PATH or link the script into a folder that is:

ln -s "$PWD/scripts/kicad-cli" ~/.local/bin/kicad-cli
python3 bench/check_env.py      # finds kicad-cli, the engine binary, Freerouting and the fixtures

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The script mounts your home directory, and the current directory when it is outside your home, at the same paths in the container, so file arguments work unchanged. It runs as your user, so the files it writes are yours.

  • Files must be under your home or the current directory. A board in /tmp that is neither is invisible to the container, and kicad-cli reports that it cannot open it.
  • A different KiCad version: TRACEMAKER_KICAD_IMAGE=kicad/kicad:9.0.6 scripts/kicad-cli .... Benchmark results are only comparable with the same version; the records say which one they used.
  • "permission denied" on the Docker socket: you were added to the docker group after this shell started. The script then retries through sg docker; a new login fixes it for good.

scripts/kicad-python does the same for KiCad's Python (pcbnew), which the board generators such as scripts/make_plane_smd_board.py need.

docs.title: Make a release
docs.text: A release is a version tag, two files built by CI (D121), release notes and a versioned copy of this documentation. The owner pushes the tag and publishes the release.

docs.title: 1. Measure
docs.text:
On the release branch:

  1. ctest --preset release: every test passes (skips are listed in the record).
  2. Tiers A–D at 120 s (benchmarks), ideally on an idle machine. Run the previous release's binary beside it if the machine is shared.
  3. Copy the runs, the test log and a README with the tables into bench/records/release-X.Y.Z/, then python3 scripts/gen_reference.py bench.

docs.title: 2. Update the version and the words
docs.text:
• The version in CMakeLists.txt (project(... VERSION X.Y.Z)), which tracemaker version prints.
  • README: How good is it?, the test count, Known limits. State both readings when the judge changed between releases.
  • docs/11-roadmap.md and dev/progress.json for the milestones the release closes.
  • python3 scripts/gen_reference.py cli --build build/release if options changed (CI checks it).

docs.title: 3. Build the files
docs.text:
CI does this on every tag; to try it first:

python3 scripts/make_release.py --build-viewer     # tarball and PCM zip in build/release-files/
python3 scripts/test_release_install.py build/release-files/tracemaker-*-linux-x86_64.tar.gz \
    build/release-files/tracemaker-*-pcm-linux-x86_64.zip   # clean container, no compiler: routes the example board

The Release files workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml) can also be run by hand (Actions > Release files > Run workflow); it keeps the files as workflow artifacts and publishes nothing.

docs.title: 4. Tag and publish
docs.text:
git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "TraceMaker X.Y.Z"
git push origin vX.Y.Z
  • Release files builds the tarball and the PCM zip again, tests them, and attaches them with SHA256SUMS to a draft release for the tag.
  • Docs publishes this site as version X.Y and moves the latest alias to it (Write and publish the docs).

Put the release notes on the draft, read them, and publish it.

docs.title: Read a run report
docs.text: A run report is one file that tells you what a route run did: what it routed, what is still open and why, which rules it read and which it could not, the signal-integrity audit, the DRC of the board before and after, and the options and seed that repeat the run (doc 18 D3, decision D136).

docs.title: Make one
docs.text:
tracemaker route board.kicad_pcb -o routed.kicad_pcb --report report.html
  • --report FILE writes HTML, or Markdown when FILE ends in .md.
  • The report is rendered from the run's JSON summary and nothing else. With --json SUMMARY the summary goes there; without it, it is written beside the report as FILE.json. Keep the two together: the report's numbers are fields of that file.
  • tracemaker report SUMMARY.json -o FILE renders the report again from a saved summary. A summary written without --report has no rules, stuck report or DRC sections, and the report says so.
  • --report adds work after the route: a DRC of the board before and after (zones refilled when the board has copper zones) and, when connections are open, the escape analysis of the stuck report. On the plane-tier boards this took 0.1 to 2.1 s (doc 18 §9).

docs.title: What each section says
docs.text: Section What it shows Where it comes from Top Routed of all connections, items left unconnected after the zones are refilled (with --soft-zones), routing DRC errors added, whether the time limit rather than the work budget ended the search (the result then depends on machine speed), rules that could not be read /routed, /connections, /open, /completion_pct, /unconnected_after_refill, /drc/added_routing_errors, /time_limited, /rules/not_read_count Result Tracks and vias added, the winning variant, the lattice pitch, the work done, the wall time top-level fields of the summary What is open and why Open connections by cause, with what each cause means; cut proofs (lines more nets must cross than tracks fit through); pins that cannot leave their package; the parts with most open ends; each open connection with the router's last explanation and the nets in the way; what the board as written leaves unconnected once the zones are refilled /stuck: the stuck report of doc 17 §3 for the final result, without its advisor parts; /drc/after/unconnected_items Rules Whether the project and custom-rule files were found, what could not be read (the route may break those, rule 6), board minimums, net classes with their net counts, custom rules, net classes from the component rules /rules, /component_rule_net_classes Signal-integrity audit Critical nets, differential pairs, buses and return paths, when the options that turn them on were given /critical_nets, /pairs, /buses, /return_paths DRC before and after Errors, warnings and unconnected items of the board the router started from and of the board it wrote; per violation type, how many the route added /drc Options and seed Seed, work budget, time limit, variants, threads; every option as given on the command line or in --config; the portfolio's variants; advisor rounds /run, /variants, /advice

docs.title: Trace a number
docs.text:
In the HTML, every value is underlined with dots: hover over it to see its JSON pointer, or tick Show the JSON field of every value to show all of them, and the source of each table's rows below it. In the Markdown, each value in the text has a footnote with its pointer, key/value tables have a column of pointers, and other tables name the array their rows come from (Rows: /stuck/unrouted/<row>).

jq reads a pointer as a path: /stuck/unrouted/3/why is jq '.stuck.unrouted[3].why' summary.json.

docs.title: What the report does not claim
docs.text:
• The DRC is TraceMaker's own (KiCad's violation names and, for routing rules, KiCad's results, doc 03 §6). It counts violations by type, so a type whose count did not grow may still hold a new violation that replaced an old one. Sign off with kicad-cli pcb drc (Run kicad-cli from Docker).
  • "No legal path" means the search found none, not that none exists. Only a cut proof or a pin that cannot escape its package is a proof.
  • The explanations are the router's own words, written while it worked; they name the last thing that failed, not every thing.

docs.title: Project
docs.text:
Where the project is going and how it got here.

  • Roadmap: the milestones M0–M21, each with a gate that must pass before the next starts, and where each one stands.
  • Candidate features: the researched features adopted as M17–M21 (decision D118), with the evidence for each and the ideas that were rejected.
  • Decisions and risks: every design decision as its own record (what was decided, the alternatives, the reason, and what replaced it), and the risk register.
  • Benchmark results: the measured runs kept in bench/records/, each record with a README that says what was measured and what it means.

Outside this site:

  • dev/assumptions.md: choices made without asking the owner, to be confirmed.
  • report/: the design and results report and the roadmap and test report (PDF, release 0.8.0).
  • reports/realworld/: eight real-world boards routed under their own rules.
  • CONTRIBUTING.md: how to report a bug or send a change.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Facts to look up. The pages marked generated are made from the code or the records by a script, and CI fails when they no longer match, so they cannot drift.

  • Command line (generated from --help): every option of tracemaker, its subcommands, tracemaker-place and tracemaker-view.
  • Viewer protocol: the JSON messages between the engine and the live viewer.
  • Benchmark results (generated from bench/records/): every recorded run.
  • C++ API (generated by Doxygen from the headers): classes and functions of the engine.
  • Component rules catalogue: the detected part categories and their rules (component_rules.yaml).
  • kicad_plugin/README.md: the plugin's environment variables and Python module.

docs.title: C++ API
docs.text:
The engine's classes and functions, generated by Doxygen from the headers in src/:

Open the C++ API reference

The link works on the published site. Locally, build it with mkdir -p build/api && doxygen docs/api/Doxyfile from the repository root and open build/api/html/index.html.

docs.title: How it is made
docs.text:
The headers document their declarations with ordinary // comments above them, as the code style asks. scripts/doxygen_filter.py turns those comments into Doxygen documentation when Doxygen reads a header, so the code keeps one comment style and needs no /// or @param markup:

In the header Doxygen reads it as the comment block right after #pragma once the file's description a // block directly above a declaration that declaration's documentation a // block followed by a blank line a plain comment (a section heading in the file) int x; // text the member's documentation

docs.title: Undocumented declarations
docs.text:
scripts/check_api_docs.py counts the public declarations that have no comment, per header, and CI warns when a header has more than its count in docs/api/undocumented-baseline.txt. Old code does not have to catch up, but a new declaration should come with a comment that says what it is for. When a change documents old declarations, scripts/check_api_docs.py --update lowers the baseline.

Modules, one namespace each under tmk:

Namespace Folder What it is tmk src/core units (tmk::Coord, integer nanometres), events, the seeded RNG, version tmk::sexpr src/sexpr the S-expression reader and writer behind byte-for-byte round trips tmk::model src/model the board: nets, footprints, pads, tracks, vias, zones, rules tmk::geom src/geom points, shapes, exact predicates, polygon booleans tmk::index src/index spatial indices, each with a linear-scan reference tmk::io src/io KiCad and Simple Route JSON reading and writing tmk::drc src/drc the design-rule check and its rule engine tmk::route src/route the router tmk::passes src/passes after-route passes: widening, stitching, style tmk::place src/place the placer tmk::learn src/learn failure memory and the knowledge base tmk::gpu src/gpu CUDA and Metal kernels and their CPU twins tmk::crules src/crules component-aware layout rules tmk::analysis src/analysis read-only audits: return paths, footprint checks tmk::advice src/advice advice files, the stuck report, advisors tmk::session src/session the board session for agents tmk::server src/server the live viewer's server tmk::app src/app the command line, the route job, the TUI

docs.title: Benchmark results
docs.text: Every benchmark run whose summary.json is kept in bench/records/, grouped by record. Clean is the share of boards with every connection made and no error added in KiCad's DRC (the judge of D8 and, since 2026-10-14, D106); FR 2.5 is Freerouting 2.5.0-RC12's published result on the same boards. Each record's README says what the runs were for and how to read them; numbers from different records are not always comparable (judge version, time limit, machine load).

docs.text: Every option of every program, as its own --help prints it. This page is generated from the build, so it is what the code accepts; the README's Common tasks table says which options to reach for first.

docs.title: tracemaker
docs.text:
TraceMaker: placement-aware PCB autorouter for KiCad


tracemaker [OPTIONS] SUBCOMMAND


OPTIONS:
  -h,     --help              Print this help message and exit

SUBCOMMANDS:
  version                     Print the version
  gpu-info                    List GPU devices and their available memory budget
  inspect                     Read a .kicad_pcb and print a summary
  rules                       Detect component categories and report the component-aware layout
                              rules (doc 15)
  drc                         Check a board against its KiCad design rules
  route                       Route all unrouted connections of a board
  report                      Render the run report from a route summary (route --json, with
                              the sections route --report adds)
  escape                      Escape feasibility of dense packages: pins that cannot leave
                              their package under the board's rules
  pairs                       Differential pairs of a routed board: coupled share, gap,
                              intra-pair skew
  buses                       Buses of a routed board: members routed, vias and layers per
                              member, lengths and skew (exit 4 when a limit is missed)
  return-paths                Reference-return audit of high-speed nets: copper under each
                              trace on its reference layer, the detour round voids, layer
                              changes without a stitch (read-only; doc 05 §42)
  footprint-check             Check every footprint against datasheet land patterns from a
                              reference library of trusted brands: pad count, positions, sizes,
                              drills, mirroring (read-only; doc 05 §43)
  advice-check                Check an advice file (doc 17) against a board: the refusals
                              `route --advice` would give, and what each hint does
  session                     Serve a board session to an agent over MCP (stdin/stdout) or JSON
                              lines: list open connections, route with hints, rip, undo, save
                              (doc 19)
  style                       Style metric of a routed board: bends, acute angles, stair-steps,
                              detours (doc 05 §39)
  causes                      Why connections stay open on a routed board: each open connection
                              is routed again with other nets' copper removed near its ends,
                              away from them or everywhere (doc 05 §55)
  layers                      Write a copy of a board with another copper layer count (inner
                              layers added, or empty ones removed; doc 05 §53)
  srj-import                  Convert a Simple Route JSON problem (tscircuit) to a KiCad board
                              with its project and rules
  srj-export                  Write a routed board's copper as the `traces` of its Simple Route
                              JSON problem
  tui                         Choose the route options on a terminal screen, then run, print or
                              save them

docs.title: tracemaker rules
docs.text:
Detect component categories and report the component-aware layout rules (doc 15)


tracemaker rules [OPTIONS] board


POSITIONALS:
  board TEXT:FILE REQUIRED    Board file

OPTIONS:
  -h,     --help              Print this help message and exit
          --json TEXT         Write the full report (every rule of every instance) as JSON
          --mode TEXT:{report,soft,on}
                              Which statuses to report: report (check only), soft (as placement
                              would apply them), on (with keep-outs)
          --dru TEXT          Write the generated custom rules (sidecar .kicad_dru) to this
                              file
          --roles-from TEXT   Detect and bind roles on this version of the board (e.g. the
                              placement input), measure on the given one
          --catalogue TEXT    Catalogue JSON to use instead of the built-in one
                              (scripts/crules_catalogue.py output)
          --rules-override TEXT:FILE
                              User override file (JSON, doc 15 §6.3): disable rules,
                              assert/deny categories, set parameters

docs.title: tracemaker route
docs.text:
<pre><code>Route all unrouted connections of a board


tracemaker route [OPTIONS] board


POSITIONALS:
  board TEXT:FILE REQUIRED    Board file (.kicad_pcb)

OPTIONS:
  -h,     --help              Print this help message and exit
          --config TEXT:FILE  Read options from a file of `name = value` lines, as `tracemaker
                              tui` saves them; options on the command line win
  -o,     --output TEXT REQUIRED
                              Output .kicad_pcb
          --time FLOAT        Time limit, seconds (safety net; results then depend on machine
                              speed)
          --work INT          Deterministic work budget in search expansions per router (e.g.
                              50000000); with the default portfolio every variant gets the
                              whole budget, so a run does up to --variants times this work
          --pitch-um FLOAT    Lattice pitch in micrometres (default: automatic)
          --via-cost-mm FLOAT Cost of a via as equivalent track length
          --seed UINT
          --layer-assign      Prefer per connection the layer with the fewest crossings
                              (two-layer boards; doc 16 F2)
          --crowded-source    Every strict search starts from the end with more copper and pads
                              of other nets near it, a boxed-in pin is proved at once (doc 05
                              §55; the portfolio does so in four of its eight variants by
                              default)
          --relax             Portfolio: route under 60 % and 80 % of the clearance first,
                              legalise (move vertices off the lattice) up to the real rules,
                              repeat on stalls; until complete, in rounds of --round-work (20 M
                              default, up to --rounds 200): --work does not limit it, --time
                              does
          --relax-late        With --relax: begin under the real rules and relax only when
                              those stall (fresh start from the loosest stage)
          --heuristic-weight FLOAT
                              Weighted A* factor (1.0 = optimal searches)
          --no-rip-up{false}  Disable negotiated rip-up and reroute
          --micro-vias        Use micro vias (outer layer to the next) where a through via is
                              blocked (only on boards that allow them)
          --blind-vias        Use blind/buried vias where a through via is blocked (only on
                              boards that allow them)
          --diff-pairs        Route differential pairs (KiCad P/N or +/- names) as coupled
                              pairs first (doc 05 §15)
          --pair-twists, --no-pair-twists{false}
                              Coupled pairs may swap sides at a layer change, for pairs whose
                              pin order is mirrored between the ends (default on; only with
                              pair routing)
          --pair-skew-mm FLOAT
                              Intra-pair skew limit for coupled pairs: meanders on the shorter
                              half (0 = custom skew rules only)
          --global            Global routing first: detailed search follows coarse corridors
          --no-optimize{false}
                              Skip the post-routing clean-up pass (fewer vias, shorter tracks)
          --plan-gap, --no-plan-gap{false}
                              Plan connections by copper-to-copper distance between pads rather
                              than centre to centre (default on)
          --escape-plan, --no-escape-plan{false}
                              Reserve escape corridors for the pins of dense packages (QFP,
                              BGA) before routing
          --escape-flow       Escape plan v2: min-cost-flow channel and layer assignment for
                              deep BGA arrays (implies --escape-plan; experimental)
          --reroute           Remove every unlocked track and via first and route the whole
                              board again
          --halving           With more --variants than --threads: successive halving over all
                              the variants instead of running only the first ones
          --cut-report        Report straight lines across the board that more nets must cross
                              than tracks fit (proof that the placement cannot be routed)
          --escape-report     Report the pins of deep BGA arrays per ring and how many were
                              connected
          --fast-bends{false} Approximate bend costs (1 state per lattice point instead of 9)
          --no-gpu            Compute cost-to-go fields on the CPU instead of the GPU (same
                              results)
          --soft-zones        Zone fills do not block other nets (refill the zones afterwards);
                              unused fills become plane targets
          --no-refill-repair  With --soft-zones: only count what the zone refill leaves
                              unconnected, do not route it
          --via-in-pad        Inner balls / enclosed SMD pads may take a minimum-size via in
                              the pad (needs filled, capped vias)
          --keep-vias-off-pads
                              Vias keep clear of SMD pads narrower than --vias-off-pads-below
                              (via-in-pad excepted)
          --vias-off-pads-below FLOAT
                              Pad width (mm) below which --keep-vias-off-pads applies (default
                              2)
          --no-neck-nets TEXT ...
                              Comma-separated nets that are never narrowed below their class
                              width nor given the small neck-down via (power nets of a
                              rule-relaxed routing)
          --first-nets-ordered
                              Route the --first-nets in the order of the list (e.g. the pins of
                              a package round its perimeter), not in the router's own order
          --first-nets TEXT ...
                              Comma-separated nets routed first, also after restarts; other
                              nets do not rip them (e.g. crystal lines)
          --bus TEXT ...      Experimental. Route these nets as a bus, NAME=PATTERN
                              (repeatable): lane by lane on the same layers, e.g.
                              'DATA=/D[0-7]' or 'LCD=/LCD_*'. PATTERN matches whole net names:
                              * and ? as in net-class patterns, [N-M] a number in that range
                              (doc 05 §38)
          --buses             Experimental. Also find buses in the net names: nets differing
                              only in a trailing index, four or more between the same two
                              components
          --bus-first         Route the buses before everything else (default: each bus where
                              the router's order puts its first connection)
          --bus-skew-mm FLOAT Length-match the --bus groups: meanders until their lengths
                              (tracks and via height, as KiCad's skew check) differ by at most
                              this (0 = only the board's custom skew rules)
          --no-field{false}   Use the octile heuristic only (no cost-to-go fields)
          --kb TEXT           Knowledge base file (failure memory across runs)
          --no-kb             Do not read or update the knowledge base
          --threads INT       Threads for the portfolio (differently configured routers, best
                              kept). Without --variants it is also the portfolio size, except
                              with --work, where all variants run and the output is identical
                              for any thread count
          --variants INT      Portfolio size (1 = single router; default: all with --work, else
                              --threads); the output never depends on --threads with --work.
                              --time applies to each variant from its start
          --no-tracks-on TEXT ...
                              Copper layers that get no new tracks, e.g. In1.Cu,In2.Cu (vias
                              still pass through and reach zone fills there)
          --layer-cost TEXT ...
                              Track cost per layer as LAYER=FACTOR, e.g. In1.Cu=4,In2.Cu=4 (1 =
                              normal, at most 1000)
          --no-fill-planes    Leave zones that have no fill unfilled while routing (default:
                              fill them in memory and route with --soft-zones, so plane nets
                              drop vias into their planes)
          --pour TEXT ...     Add a copper pour before routing: auto (the ground net on the
                              first inner layer, else the back layer, when the board has no
                              zone) or NET@LAYER; repeatable. Turns on --soft-zones; the pour
                              is written with its fill
          --copper-layers INT:INT in [2 - 32]
                              Route with this many copper layers (even): inner layers are
                              added, or empty ones removed, in the output too
          --try-layers INT ...
                              Layer-count advisor: route with each count (e.g. 2,4,6), fewest
                              first, stop at the first that completes and write that board; the
                              summary's "layers" lists every count tried
          --view              Stream the routing live to the browser viewer
          --return-paths TEXT ...
                              After routing, audit the reference return of nets matching these
                              KiCad wildcards (comma separated, e.g. 'DDR*'): copper under each
                              trace on its reference layer, the detour round voids, layer
                              changes without a stitching via. Read-only; the report is in the
                              log and the summary, the paths in the viewer (doc 05 §42)
          --return-path-classes TEXT ...
                              With --return-paths: also the nets of these net classes
          --return-path-pairs Audit the nets that are halves of a differential pair too
          --return-path-radius-mm FLOAT:POSITIVE
                              How far a stitching via or capacitor may be from a layer change
                              (default 5)
          --footprint-refs TEXT
                              Before routing, check every footprint against datasheet land
                              patterns from this reference library (a directory or a JSON file;
                              doc 05 §43). A footprint that differs from its datasheet is an
                              error and stops the job
          --footprint-trusted TEXT:FILE
                              With --footprint-refs: the trusted brand list (default:
                              trusted_brands.txt beside the references); references of other
                              brands give no verdict
          --footprint-trust-all
                              With --footprint-refs: use the references of every brand (nobody
                              vouched for them)
          --footprint-require TEXT ...
                              With --footprint-refs: designators (KiCad wildcards, comma
                              separated) that must have a trusted reference, else it is an
                              error
          --footprint-warn-only
                              With --footprint-refs: report the discrepancies and route anyway
          --footprint-tol-mm FLOAT:NONNEGATIVE
                              With --footprint-refs: tolerance of pad positions, sizes and
                              drills in millimetres (default 0.05; a reference may set its own)
          --si-rules          JLCPCB's three routing rules at once (doc 05 §44): critical nets
                              (from the component rules' roles and differential pairs) routed
                              first, dearer vias for them (x3), and a cost for their tracks
                              over a void of the adjacent reference plane (+4 pitches per
                              lattice step); each can be set with the options below instead.
                              After routing, layer changes of critical nets without a return
                              via get one (doc 05 §57; --no-si-stitch)
          --no-si-stitch{false}
                              With --si-rules: no return-path stitching vias for the critical
                              nets' layer changes that the reference-return audit finds without
                              one (doc 05 §57)
          --critical-nets TEXT ...
                              Nets that are critical whatever their role, KiCad wildcards comma
                              separated (e.g. 'CLK*,USB_D*'); they are tier 1, like clocks, and
                              the nets found by --critical-auto follow in their own tiers
          --critical-auto     Critical nets from the component rules' roles (clock, crystal,
                              USB, Ethernet, PCIe, DDR ...) and from differential pairs
          --critical-first    Route the critical nets before all others, tier by tier (clocks
                              and crystals, differential links, memory buses); --first-nets
                              stay in front
          --critical-via-cost FLOAT:FLOAT in [1 - 100]
                              A via costs a critical net this many times --via-cost-mm (default
                              1; 3 with --si-rules)
          --critical-via-max INT:NONNEGATIVE
                              Warn in the report when a critical net has more vias than this (0
                              = no limit)
          --split-cost FLOAT:NONNEGATIVE
                              Cost, in pitches per lattice step, of a critical net's track over
                              a void of the adjacent reference plane: a split, a slot or an
                              antipad field (default 0; 4 with --si-rules)
          --split-hard        Close plane voids to critical nets instead of charging for them:
                              a critical net with no way round a split stays unrouted
          --no-freeze         With --view: the viewer does not hold the scene on a routing
                              stall (it normally freezes on the stuck net, with the rejected
                              paths and what rejected them; Space resumes)
          --record TEXT       Write the routing events (JSON lines, time-stamped) to a file for
                              replay; zstd-compressed if FILE ends in .zst
          --view-host TEXT    Viewer bind address (default $TM_VIEW_HOST, else 127.0.0.1: this
                              machine only). 0.0.0.0 or a LAN address lets other machines
                              connect, and then a token is required
          --view-token TEXT   Token for a viewer that other machines can reach (16+ characters;
                              default: a random one, printed in the URL)
          --view-insecure     Serve a viewer that other machines can reach WITHOUT a token
                              (anyone who can reach the port can watch the board)
          --view-port INT     Viewer port (default 8766)
          --view-embed TEXT   Pages that may show the viewer in a frame, origins separated by
                              spaces (e.g. a dashboard: http://host:8771); default: none
          --hold              Keep serving the viewer after routing finishes
          --json TEXT         Write a result summary as JSON
          --report TEXT       Write a run report for designers: what was routed, what is open
                              and why, the rules read and not read, the signal-integrity audit,
                              the DRC before and after, the options and the seed. HTML, or
                              Markdown if FILE ends in .md. Every number in it is a field of
                              the --json summary (written to FILE.json when --json is not
                              given)
          --component-rules TEXT:{off,report,soft,on}
                              Component-aware rules (doc 15): off (default); report/soft write
                              <output>.tracemaker.kicad_dru; on also routes with the generated
                              keep-outs (crystal, switching-regulator inductor) as in-memory
                              rule areas
          --rules-override TEXT:FILE
                              User override file for --component-rules (JSON, doc 15 §6.3):
                              disable rules, assert/deny categories, set parameters
          --advice TEXT:FILE  Advice file (JSON, doc 17): typed hints (nets first, connection
                              priority, layer costs, regions that reserve space for some nets).
                              They run as extra portfolio variants next to the unadvised ones,
                              so the result is never worse
          --advice-variants INT:INT in [1 - 8]
                              Advised variants to add (default: the file's "variants", else 4)
          --advisor TEXT      A command (run with sh -c) that reads the stuck report (JSON) on
                              stdin and writes an advice file on stdout; consulted only if the
                              route leaves connections open, then the board is routed again
                              with its advice (advisors/ has a reference one)
          --advisor-timeout FLOAT:POSITIVE
                              Seconds the advisor may take (default 120; not counted as routing
                              work)
          --advisor-rounds INT:INT in [1 - 8]
                              Consult the advisor again with the advised run's result while
                              connections are open (default 1)
          --advisor-redact    Send net and part names to the advisor as aliases (N1, P3),
                              without part values or library ids; the advice is mapped back
          --advice-out TEXT   Where the advisor's advice is saved (default
                              <output>.advice.json); route again with --advice FILE to repeat
                              the run
          --stuck-report TEXT Write the stuck report (what failed and why, JSON) of the run the
                              advisor sees, or the final one
          --emit-items TEXT   Write the new tracks and vias as JSON (for the KiCad plugin)
          --widen-power       After routing: widen new tracks that are narrower than their net
                              class width back up to it where there is room, and nets with a
                              target (--widen-net, or a width the component rules computed)
                              towards the target (doc 05 §39)
          --widen-net TEXT ...
                              With --widen-power: target width for nets as PATTERN=WIDTH_MM,
                              e.g. '+5V=0.8' or 'VBUS*=1' (repeatable)
          --stitch-vias TEXT:{planes,return,all}
                              After routing: add stitching vias. planes: vias of a plane's net
                              on a grid where its fills overlap on two or more layers; return:
                              a plane via near each via of the nets that need a reference plane
                              (component rules, --stitch-return); all: both
          --stitch-pitch FLOAT:POSITIVE
                              Grid pitch of plane stitching vias, mm (default 5.08, the
                              catalogue's value)
          --stitch-distance FLOAT:POSITIVE
                              Return-path stitching: largest distance from a signal via to its
                              plane via, mm (default: the rule's, else 5.08)
          --stitch-return TEXT ...
                              Return-path stitching for nets as PATTERN=PLANE_NET, e.g.
                              'USB_D*=GND' (repeatable). Return-path stitching from component
                              rules is experimental
          --pass-work INT:POSITIVE
                              Work budget of each after-route pass, in exact checks (default
                              2,000,000)
</code></pre>

docs.title: tracemaker-place
docs.text:
TraceMaker placer: quadratic + SimPL global placement, legalisation and
annealing


tracemaker-place [OPTIONS] board


POSITIONALS:
  board TEXT:FILE REQUIRED    Input .kicad_pcb

OPTIONS:
  -h,     --help              Print this help message and exit
  -o,     --output TEXT REQUIRED
                              Output .kicad_pcb
          --mode TEXT:{full,refine,auto,routable,eco}
                              full (place from scratch) or refine (improve the current
                              placement)
          --time FLOAT        Wall-time stop for the annealer, seconds (0 = none; budgets are
                              in moves)
          --seed UINT         Random seed
          --threads INT       Threads for parallel annealing runs (0 = min(cores, 16))
          --runs INT          Independent annealing runs (0 = one per thread)
          --effort FLOAT      Annealing moves per run = effort x 4000 x movable parts
          --alpha-cross-mm FLOAT
                              Cost of one airwire crossing in mm of signal HPWL
          --courtyard-clearance-mm FLOAT
                              Override the courtyard clearance (default: rules, else 0.25 mm)
          --move-connectors   Also move connectors that touch the board edge
          --scratch           The input has no placement (parts piled or beside the board, as
                              after importing a schematic): input positions of movable parts
                              carry no intent and are never fallen back to
          --repair-input      routable, eco and --route-check: an input placement with overlaps
                              or parts off the board is replaced, as the baseline and fallback,
                              by its minimal repair (only the conflicting parts moved to the
                              nearest legal spot). Off by default: the placement model is
                              stricter than KiCad's DRC
          --no-decap-affinity Do not tie decoupling capacitors to their IC's supply pins
          --component-rules TEXT:{off,report,soft,on}
                              Component-aware layout rules (doc 15): off, report (detect and
                              list only), soft (proximity pseudo-nets: crystal, ESD, regulator
                              caps, generalised decoupling); default soft (D52)
          --decap-weight INT:INT in [1 - 1000]
                              Weight of each decoupling-capacitor tie (D25); a signal net
                              weighs 10 (the default)
          --crules-weight INT:INT in [1 - 1000]
                              Scale of the component-rule proximity weights in percent (100 =
                              as the rules say)
          --crules-two-stage, --no-crules-two-stage{false}
                              Full mode with component rules (default on): place with the
                              decoupling ties first, lock those capacitors and their ICs, then
                              refine with the component-rule pulls
          --edge-attraction   With --component-rules soft/on: pull movable connectors (CONN-01,
                              USB2-11, DISP-02) toward the nearest board edge (objective only;
                              pin headers are not pulled)
          --rules-override TEXT:FILE
                              User override file for --component-rules (JSON, doc 15 §6.3):
                              disable rules, assert/deny categories, set parameters
          --json TEXT         Write the placement report as JSON
  -v,     --verbose           Log the spreading iterations
          --route-check INT   Route the input and the new placement with this work budget (A*
                              expansions per variant) and keep the placement that routes more
                              connections (0 = off)
          --route-threads INT Router portfolio size for --route-check
          --no-fallback       Full mode: keep the result even if some parts could not be placed
          --debug-part TEXT   Print the legality map of one part and exit
          --tempering         Parallel tempering over the annealing runs (replica exchange)
                              instead of independent runs
          --lns-rate FLOAT    Share of annealing steps that are large-neighbourhood (window
                              rip-up and re-place) moves
          --lns-window INT    Parts per LNS window (2..12)
          --lns-polish INT    LNS windows run on the annealing result
          --beta FLOAT        Routability weight: mm of signal HPWL per mm of RUDY overflow (0
                              = off)
          --flip              Side assignment (D48): movable surface-mount parts may move to
                              the other side (KiCad-mirrored footprints); through-hole, locked
                              and fixed parts never do
          --flip-via-mm FLOAT With --flip: cost of one estimated via (a net's surface-mount pin
                              on its minority side) in mm of signal HPWL
          --flip-rate FLOAT   With --flip: share of annealing moves that are flips
          --keep-side TEXT    With --flip: references that must stay on their side (comma
                              separated)
          --debug-flip TEXT   Write the input with these footprints (comma separated
                              references, or 'all') flipped in place, KiCad style, and exit
          --rounds INT        routable: re-placement rounds after the seeds
          --eco-rounds INT    eco: commit rounds
          --eco-candidates INT
                              eco/routable: moves routed per round
          --loop-beta FLOAT   routable/eco: routability weight in the loop
          --final-work INT    routable/eco: route the winner and the input again with this
                              budget; keep the winner only if not worse (default 4 x
                              --route-check, 0 = off)
          --record TEXT       routable: write the placement timelapse (JSONL: header, then one
                              frame per stage)
          --loop-time FLOAT   routable: wall-time stop in seconds; checked between seeds and
                              routes, keeps the best placement so far (0 = none)

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
Lessons that take you from nothing to a routed board, one step at a time. The commands of the first tutorial were run before they were written down, and the output shown is what they printed (release 0.10.0, 2026-10-21). The plugin tutorial follows the steps that scripts/kicad_gui_roundtrip.py checks in KiCad 10.0.6.

  • Route your first board: build TraceMaker, route the example four-layer board, check it.
  • Route from inside KiCad: install the plugin, route the open board with one click, undo it.

docs.title: Route your first board
docs.text:
In this tutorial you build TraceMaker, route a small four-layer board that comes with it, and check the result with a design-rule check. It takes about fifteen minutes, most of it the build. You need Linux, CMake, Ninja and GCC 13 or newer; no GPU and no KiCad.

No compiler?

A tagged release carries a ready-built Linux tarball (tracemaker-VERSION-linux-x86_64.tar.gz) with the same example board in share/tracemaker/examples/plane_smd/. Unpack it, put its bin/ on your PATH, and start at step 2 with tracemaker in place of build/cpu-only/src/app/tracemaker.

docs.title: 1. Build
docs.text:
From the top of the repository:

cmake --preset cpu-only
cmake --build --preset cpu-only
build/cpu-only/src/app/tracemaker version

The last line prints tracemaker 0.10.0 (or a newer version). The cpu-only preset builds without CUDA; with a CUDA 12.x GPU you can use release instead, and the results are the same (see Use the GPUs).

To keep the commands short, name the program once:

TM=build/cpu-only/src/app/tracemaker

docs.title: 2. Look at the board
docs.text:
The example is tests/boards/plane_smd/plane_smd.kicad_pcb: a 24 × 14 mm board with every part on the top side, a ground plane on In1.Cu and a 3.3 V plane on In2.Cu. It has a 0.4 mm-pitch ball array, a QFN microcontroller and a 32.768 kHz crystal, and no tracks yet.

$TM inspect tests/boards/plane_smd/plane_smd.kicad_pcb

tests/boards/plane_smd/plane_smd.kicad_pcb
  format 20260206 (named nets), 4 copper layers: F.Cu In1.Cu In2.Cu B.Cu
  11 nets, 16 footprints, 91 pads, 0 tracks, 0 arcs, 0 vias, 4 zones
  outline 24.000 x 14.000 mm

Check it before routing, so you know what "better" will mean:

$TM drc tests/boards/plane_smd/plane_smd.kicad_pcb

It reports unconnected_items 47: nothing is routed yet. The design rules come from plane_smd.kicad_pro next to the board, as they do in KiCad.

docs.title: 3. Route it
docs.text:
Make a folder for the result (build/ is ignored by git) and copy the project file into it, so the routed board keeps its design rules:

mkdir -p build/tutorial
cp tests/boards/plane_smd/plane_smd.kicad_pro build/tutorial/routed.kicad_pro
$TM route tests/boards/plane_smd/plane_smd.kicad_pcb -o build/tutorial/routed.kicad_pcb \
    --soft-zones --via-in-pad --keep-vias-off-pads --first-nets XIN,XOUT \
    --work 3000000 --variants 4 --no-gpu

What the options are for, on this board:

Option Why --soft-zones No pad touches a plane, so every ground and 3.3 V pad needs a via down into its plane. Zone fills stop blocking other nets, and the job refills them afterwards to check that nothing was cut off. --via-in-pad One inner ball of the ball array has no other way out than a via in its pad. --keep-vias-off-pads No plane vias in the small 0402 and QFN pads. --first-nets XIN,XOUT The crystal lines go first, so they stay short. --work 3000000 A budget in search steps instead of seconds, so you get the same result every time, at any thread count. --variants 4 Run four of the eight differently configured routers and keep the best result. --no-gpu Compute on the CPU only. The results are the same either way.

After about five seconds the last lines read:

  variant 2 fast bends, longest first (2x pitch on large boards) routed 44 in 4.7 s
  variant 1 fast bends, shortest first, crowded source routed 47 in 3.3 s
soft zones: after refilling 2 zones, 0 items unconnected
routed 49/49 connections, 108 tracks, 42 vias, pitch 0.025 mm, ...

Every connection is routed. The exit code is 0 when nothing is left open.

docs.title: 4. Check the result
docs.text:
The written board keeps its old zone fills (TraceMaker does not change what it did not create). Refill them for the check, the way KiCad does before its own check:

$TM drc build/tutorial/routed.kicad_pcb --refill-zones

It prints zones refilled 2 and no violations. With --json report.json it writes the report in kicad-cli's layout.

TraceMaker's own check is fast but is not the judge: KiCad's is. If you have KiCad 9 or 10, or Docker (Run kicad-cli from Docker):

kicad-cli pcb drc --refill-zones --format json -o build/tutorial/drc.json build/tutorial/routed.kicad_pcb

KiCad 10.0.6 prints Found 33 violations and Found 0 unconnected items. The 33 are silkscreen warnings (silk_over_copper, silk_overlap, silk_edge_clearance) that the unrouted board already had; routing added no error. Comparing with the check of the input board, rather than looking for zero, is how the benchmarks judge too.

Open build/tutorial/routed.kicad_pcb in KiCad to look at it, and press B to refill the zones there.

docs.title: 5. Watch it route (optional)
docs.text:
The live viewer is a web page. Build it once (needs Node.js), then route with --view --hold:

(cd viewer && npm install && npm run build)
$TM route tests/boards/plane_smd/plane_smd.kicad_pcb -o build/tutorial/routed.kicad_pcb \
    --soft-zones --via-in-pad --keep-vias-off-pads --first-nets XIN,XOUT --view --hold

Open http://localhost:8766/. --hold keeps the page up after the route ends; Ctrl-C stops it.

docs.title: Route from inside KiCad
docs.text:
In this tutorial you install the TraceMaker plugin in KiCad 10, route the open board with one click, and undo it. You need KiCad 10 and either a TraceMaker release or a build (Route your first board, step 1).

What has been checked

The plugin's round trip (tracks appear, one Ctrl+Z removes them, Ctrl+Y brings them back) is checked by scripts/kicad_gui_roundtrip.py in KiCad 10.0.6 running under Xvfb. Installing the package by hand in a desktop KiCad has not been tried by the project yet; tell us how it goes.

docs.title: 1. Get the package
docs.text:
From a release (Linux x86_64). Download tracemaker-VERSION-pcm-linux-x86_64.zip from the release page. It carries its own copy of the router, so nothing else is needed.

From your build. Make the package and check it:

python3 scripts/make_pcm_package.py
python3 scripts/validate_pcm.py build/pcm/tracemaker-*.zip

This package does not contain the router. Tell the plugin where it is before you start KiCad:

export TRACEMAKER=$PWD/build/cpu-only/src/app/tracemaker

docs.title: 2. Install it
docs.text:
1. In KiCad 10, open Preferences > Plugins and tick Enable KiCad API. Plugins of this kind only run with it.
  2. Open the Plugin and Content Manager, choose Install from File..., pick the zip and press Apply. KiCad creates a Python environment for the plugin (it installs kicad-python), which can take a minute.
  3. Restart the PCB editor. Autoroute with TraceMaker appears in the toolbar and under Tools > External Plugins.

docs.title: 3. Route
docs.text:
Open a board with unrouted connections: tests/boards/plane_smd/plane_smd.kicad_pcb from the repository will do.

Press Autoroute with TraceMaker. The plugin saves a copy of the board with its project (so every design rule is used), routes it with a 120 s limit, and adds the new tracks and vias to the open board as one commit. Your board file is not overwritten until you save.

Press B to refill the zones, then run KiCad's Inspect > Design Rules Checker.

docs.title: 4. Undo and redo
docs.text: One Ctrl+Z removes the whole result; Ctrl+Y brings it back.

docs.title: 5. Change the settings
docs.text:
The plugin reads its settings from environment variables, set where KiCad is started (a shell or a desktop file):

To… Set Route for 60 s with 8 threads and watch it in the browser TRACEMAKER_ARGS="--time 60 --threads 8 --view" Remove the unlocked copper and route the whole board again TRACEMAKER_REROUTE=1 Let TraceMaker move footprints first TRACEMAKER_PLACE=auto Refill the zones afterwards TRACEMAKER_REFILL=1 (the refill is its own undo step)

The full list is in kicad_plugin/README.md.
